TwkBJRhg4H.one_liner: Adapts a frozen pretrained MAE for multivariate forecasting with variable-context and temporal-periodic refinement modules fused by a learned gate.
TwkBJRhg4H.problem: Existing vision-model forecasters must balance independent per-variable visual spaces against cross-variable dependency modeling, and must adapt natural-image backbones to the temporal semantics of time-series images.
TwkBJRhg4H.method: MUSE keeps a pretrained MAE fully frozen and adds the Variable Context Refinement Module (VCR), which aggregates shared temporal information within each variable and models cross-variable contextual dependencies, and the Temporal-Periodic Refinement Module (TPR), which refines features at different encoder depths and models across-period and within-period dependencies. The two modules each produce a forecast, and the forecasts are fused by a learnable prediction-level gate.
TwkBJRhg4H.key_idea: Add lightweight cross-variable and period-axis refinement modules around a frozen MAE, each producing its own forecast, then combine the forecasts with a learnable prediction-level gate.
TwkBJRhg4H.evidence: Experiments on 10 real-world multivariate time-series datasets.
TwkBJRhg4H.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper identifies relevant limitations of visual forecasting (missing cross-variable interaction, different semantics of the two period-folded image axes) and that the lightweight adaptation of a frozen backbone is reasonable and extensively tested on 10 public datasets.
TwkBJRhg4H.main_concern: The experiments do not show that the gains come from the dependency-aware design rather than from added trainable capacity, and the frozen-backbone motivation (the structural semantic gap) is asserted rather than demonstrated.

AL9I4VjoM4.one_liner: Circuit model of grid, place and direction cells shows theta sweeps broadcast information to unvisited regions, speeding cognitive-map learning.
AL9I4VjoM4.problem: Animals learn map-like representations from limited experience, but the neural mechanisms behind this sample-efficient learning remain unclear.
AL9I4VjoM4.method: Builds a network of direction, grid and place-cell modules in which theta modulation and firing-rate adaptation generate theta sweeps and error-modulated Hebbian plasticity lets place cells bind observations, then runs simulations and ablations on dorsal-ventral grid organization and annealed theta modulation.
AL9I4VjoM4.key_idea: Theta sweeps from theta modulation and adaptation in multi-scale grid modules bind current observations to unvisited places via Hebbian learning, and reduced theta anchoring anneals learning.
AL9I4VjoM4.evidence: Simulations and ablations of the entorhinal-hippocampal network compared with a Vector-HaSH control, producing three testable predictions, with many results from 3 seeds or a single seed.
AL9I4VjoM4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper proposes an interesting, falsifiable function for theta sweeps and ties it to measurable circuit variables and testable predictions.
AL9I4VjoM4.main_concern: The sweep mechanism is not separated from generic spatial smoothing or from model-capacity effects, and results rely on few seeds, no significance tests, one control model, and overlap with prior smoothing work.

XSUChuUG9R.one_liner: Learns imaging forward operators from unpaired data by matching both degraded-side and restored clean-side distributions through differentiable plug-and-play restoration.
XSUChuUG9R.problem: Distribution matching on generated measurements barely constrains components the operator suppresses, so operators that look alike as forward models can invert very differently.
XSUChuUG9R.method: Adds a clean-side comparison to degraded-side matching: real degraded images, once restored by a differentiable plug-and-play algorithm parameterized by the operator being learned, should be distributed like clean images.
XSUChuUG9R.key_idea: Backpropagate a clean-side distribution-matching loss through a differentiable plug-and-play restorer parameterized by the learned operator, so inversion quality constrains the operator.
XSUChuUG9R.evidence: Spatially varying PSF calibration and blind super-resolution, with a theorem on how sensitivity of measurement matching decays faster than reconstruction risk at low SNR; reviews cite DPIR and IKL components and comparisons to Restormer and OmniLens.
XSUChuUG9R.claimed_gains: Recovers more accurate operators than degraded-side matching alone and closes much of the gap to restoration with the true operator; no numbers stated in the abstract.
XSUChuUG9R.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the reconstruction-side loss addresses a real limitation of measurement-only matching and improves operator estimation, backed by a motivating theorem and strong gains in the measured PSF setting.
XSUChuUG9R.main_concern: Limited methodological advance and reliance on a fixed pretrained denoiser: the loss resembles cycle consistency and builds on existing IKL and DPIR, theory uses a simplified MMSE setting, and training is about 5.7 to 6.6 times slower.

0GPhXVIbK0.one_liner: Approximate policy iteration for zero-sum POSGs that updates both players' policies along conservative-update trajectories using one linear bound per update.
0GPhXVIbK0.problem: Solvers for zero-sum POSGs usually optimize a central value function, which restores Bellman recursion but requires value updates over a high-dimensional space.
0GPhXVIbK0.method: The method keeps one policy per player and updates both jointly along trajectories induced by conservative policy updates, relying on a single linear bound induced by the current joint policy instead of a full central value function. It alternates local policy improvements and conservative updates, concentrating computation where the joint policy can still be exploited.
0GPhXVIbK0.key_idea: Replace the central value function with a single hyperplane from the current joint policy, and move policies conservatively along the induced occupancy trajectories.
0GPhXVIbK0.evidence: Finite-horizon zero-sum POSG benchmarks compared with PBVI, HSVI and CFR+, plus theory on the linear structure of a fixed policy's value in focal beliefs and a convergence theorem.
0GPhXVIbK0.claimed_gains: Competitive at small horizons and often a better runtime-accuracy trade-off than PBVI, HSVI and CFR+ at larger horizons; no numbers stated.
0GPhXVIbK0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem well motivated and the player-specific focal-belief representation, with a policy value linear in the belief, conceptually interesting and useful for scaling to longer horizons.
0GPhXVIbK0.main_concern: The algorithm and convergence argument are incomplete or imprecise (undefined VECTOR, unclear stochastic-approximation conditions), and the authors acknowledge the code needs cleanup before the experimental results are fully supported.

3lSas96zVV.one_liner: Builds response-centered memory units by recovering interaction flow across speakers, turns and modalities for multimodal multi-party conversation agents.
3lSas96zVV.problem: Existing agent memory organizes content by temporal proximity, semantic similarity or generic visual content, leaving event information fragmented across speakers, turns and modalities.
3lSas96zVV.method: IGMem first recovers the interaction flow from multiple conversational cues, then compiles the relevant textual and visual evidence into response-centered memory units that bring information about the same event together. Reviewers describe a multimodal LLM call per turn with conditioned uptake and recursive propagation.
3lSas96zVV.key_idea: Use each response as the signal that links scattered sources and selects relevant content, compiling that evidence into one memory unit per response.
3lSas96zVV.evidence: Two benchmarks (H2HMem and Mem-Gallery per reviewers) and two backbones, averaged over three runs, with ablations of flow recovery, conditioned uptake and recursive propagation.
3lSas96zVV.claimed_gains: Outperforms competitive baselines on two benchmarks across different settings; no numbers stated in the abstract.
3lSas96zVV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem formulation sensible and the method well motivated by the limits of turn-based memory, with consistent gains across two benchmarks and backbones and ablations showing each component matters.
3lSas96zVV.main_concern: Answer refusal consistently regresses, suggesting compiled contexts add unsupported information, and the quality of the recovered interaction flow and the write-time construction cost are not directly assessed.

tsMr8CEzPv.one_liner: Multi-granularity graph anomaly detection using information-bottleneck losses on hidden layers and cross-granularity consistency regularization.
tsMr8CEzPv.problem: Existing multi-granularity graph anomaly detectors ignore hierarchical information in latent representations and cross-granularity interdependencies, making latent-space evolution less discriminative.
tsMr8CEzPv.method: GaHIGAD explores latent evolutionary information in hidden representations through Information Bottleneck theory, and integrates cross-granularity representations to exploit latent consistency dependencies for representation regularization. Per the reviews, granularity-specific encoders share information through gated fusion.
tsMr8CEzPv.key_idea: Apply an information-bottleneck loss at intermediate layers and regularize each granularity's representation with cross-granularity consistency.
tsMr8CEzPv.evidence: Experiments on public datasets; reviews cite 14 datasets in single-graph and multi-graph settings, zero-shot cross-granularity transfer, noise robustness, and component ablations.
tsMr8CEzPv.claimed_gains: Claims effectiveness over state-of-the-art baselines; no numbers are stated.
tsMr8CEzPv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the unified node-, edge-, and graph-level setting is well motivated, the method is clearly described, and the experiments over many datasets support it.
tsMr8CEzPv.main_concern: Novelty is seen as limited since information-bottleneck losses are already common in graph learning, with missing ablations of the all-layer IB design and an unclear objective formulation.

gtb1ceJJsc.one_liner: Compares Guess-and-Check rejection sampling with SGD to show SGD achieves larger input-space margins and better generalization.
gtb1ceJJsc.problem: It is unclear whether over-parameterized networks generalize because most interpolating solutions generalize (volume hypothesis) or because of the inductive bias of optimization.
gtb1ceJJsc.method: Gives a sample-dependent generalization bound for Guess-and-Check (G&C), proves a statistical separation between G&C and GD in a Gaussian model, and compares G&C with SGD empirically on common datasets under the margin assumption.
gtb1ceJJsc.key_idea: Use rejection-sampling G&C as a pure-volume baseline, and show SGD exploits the margin structure of the landscape that random sampling does not.
gtb1ceJJsc.evidence: A generalization bound for G&C, a Gaussian-model separation proof, and experiments on common datasets measuring input-space margin and generalization.
gtb1ceJJsc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the question of where generalization comes from important and the Gaussian separation and direct G&C-versus-SGD comparison useful, with a counting-based bound that refines interpolation-probability bounds.
gtb1ceJJsc.main_concern: The two hypotheses may not be cleanly separable: G&C's prior or loss-threshold restriction may confound the comparison, so results may only contrast different priors.

uNAtJyMyws.one_liner: Multi-view novel class discovery that models similarity relations between novel samples and known-class prototypes within a matrix-factorization framework.
uNAtJyMyws.problem: Existing multi-view NCD methods use distributional correlations and view fusion but leave the similarity relations between known and novel categories insufficiently explored.
uNAtJyMyws.method: Multi-view matrix factorization learns view-specific latent structures coupled by a shared partition representation whose known-class part is constrained by ground-truth labels, injecting supervision into representation learning and adaptive view weighting. Per the reviews, known-class prototypes then act as relation anchors and a relation-consistency constraint guides novel-class partitioning.
uNAtJyMyws.key_idea: Use known-class prototypes as relation anchors and enforce relation consistency so novel-class partitions inherit structure from known classes.
uNAtJyMyws.evidence: Reviews describe extensive experiments against multi-view clustering and NCD baselines; the abstract is cut off before the results.
uNAtJyMyws.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that learning known-novel relations with prototype anchors is an interesting idea, the paper is clear, and the experiments are extensive and support the method.
uNAtJyMyws.main_concern: Novelty over closely related multi-view NCD and matrix-factorization clustering methods (e.g., IICMVNCD) is not clearly established, and reporting details such as optimization settings and run variance are missing.

jBuI45kXtp.one_liner: Shows induction circuits in Pythia move to the fastest surviving RoPE band when the fastest band is disabled from initialization.
jBuI45kXtp.problem: Strong dependence of a trained circuit on a component does not show the component is developmentally necessary, as with induction and RoPE's fastest band in Pythia.
jBuI45kXtp.method: The authors disable the fastest RoPE band during training across independent 70M initializations and from the public 160M initialization, then use head-set knockouts, early-checkpoint tests, and frequency permutations to test which band induction recruits.
jBuI45kXtp.key_idea: Induction recruits the fastest RoPE frequency band that remains available (band downshift), producing learned functional dependence without band 0 being necessary.
jBuI45kXtp.evidence: Pythia-70M and 160M with counterfactual retraining, head-set knockouts on synthetic induction and held-out text prediction, and early-checkpoint tests.
jBuI45kXtp.claimed_gains: In pretrained Pythia-70M, disabling the fastest band in one previous-token head reproduces 87% of the induction-accuracy drop caused by disabling it model-wide.
jBuI45kXtp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the phenomenon interesting and the counterfactual retraining with controls such as frequency permutations reasonably convincing, with band-1 functional support from head-level knockouts.
jBuI45kXtp.main_concern: Reviewers say the frequency-selection rule is only partly causally tested, since deeper transitions rely on attribution rather than knockouts, and the evidence is limited to the Pythia family with a single 70M initialization.

4i0ydmsCNQ.one_liner: Proves tight convergence rates for Random Reshuffling across all epoch counts, with and without convex components.
4i0ydmsCNQ.problem: Existing Random Reshuffling guarantees mostly require many epochs, and a tight characterization across the full range of epoch counts, with and without component convexity, is missing.
4i0ydmsCNQ.method: The paper analyzes worst-case convergence of constant-stepsize SGD under RR for finite sums of smooth components whose average is strongly convex, proving upper and lower bounds for convex and nonconvex components.
4i0ydmsCNQ.key_idea: Matching upper and lower bounds in n, K, and kappa reveal a phase transition at K of order kappa, and a nonconvex-component cost that depends on kappa/n.
4i0ydmsCNQ.evidence: Theory: tight rates up to polylogarithmic factors for convex components and lower bounds for nonconvex components; no experiments stated.
4i0ydmsCNQ.claimed_gains: With convex components, RR matches with-replacement SGD below K of order kappa and is faster above it; without convexity, order max{kappa, kappa^2/n} epochs are necessary and rates worsen by a factor of max{1, kappa/n}.
4i0ydmsCNQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper fills a clear gap with explicit bounds in n, K, and kappa, a sharp phase transition for convex components, and a clear comparison with i.i.d. SGD.
4i0ydmsCNQ.main_concern: Reviewers raise no major weaknesses, only requests to clarify the parameter range of Theorem 4.2 and for more settings such as convex but not strongly convex.

8d1C6Gf5cl.one_liner: Co-evolves a training harness with the policy, adapting task sampling, rollout guidance, and rubric criteria for rubric-based open-ended RL.
8d1C6Gf5cl.problem: Rubric rewards in open-ended RL become non-discriminative or spurious as the policy evolves because the training configuration stays fixed.
8d1C6Gf5cl.method: HarnessRL keeps a training-time memory of within-task history and cross-task evidence; a harness evolver attributes each reward failure to task sampling, rollout guidance, or rubric criteria, and a proposer plus just-in-time critic loop accepts an update only after measuring its effect on the current frozen policy.
8d1C6Gf5cl.key_idea: Attribute each reward failure to one training interface and accept a proposed update only after a critic measures its effect on the current frozen policy.
8d1C6Gf5cl.evidence: Rubric-Mix-10k, a new five-domain suite (medical, science, writing, role-playing, instruction-following), at two policy scales per reviews.
8d1C6Gf5cl.claimed_gains: Outperforms the strongest baseline on Rubric-Mix-10k (abstract truncated; no numbers visible).
8d1C6Gf5cl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the framework addresses reward saturation and spurious rewards by jointly adapting several interfaces, with consistent improvements across policy scales and domains.
8d1C6Gf5cl.main_concern: Reviewers worry the same model family acts as judge, attributor, proposer, and critic, risking self-reinforcing evaluation bias, and note the critic's acceptance criterion does not directly validate reward quality.

TWHGQoKsP3.one_liner: RAESR performs real-world super-resolution in a frozen DINOv3-L fused-layer latent space using a 415M decoder with reconstruction and adversarial losses.
TWHGQoKsP3.problem: Reconstruction-oriented latent spaces and pixel space place degraded images far from the clean-image manifold and lack semantic information, making real-world super-resolution hard and prone to hallucination.
TWHGQoKsP3.method: The fused latent of 23 layers of a frozen DINOv3-L serves as the restoration substrate, where degraded images embed near the manifold and a hierarchy from pixel detail to degradation-robust semantics guides restoration; a 415M decoder is trained with reconstruction and adversarial objectives (abstract truncated).
TWHGQoKsP3.key_idea: Restore images in a frozen vision-foundation latent space whose multi-layer hierarchy places degraded inputs near the clean manifold, decoding in one pass.
TWHGQoKsP3.evidence: Comparisons across four benchmarks with runtime, ablations, a matched comparison with a VAE latent, latent interpolation, layer-wise information recovery analysis and human evaluation.
TWHGQoKsP3.claimed_gains: Per the TLDR, one decoder pass gives the best fidelity-perception trade-off at 37 ms; the abstract is truncated before reporting results.
TWHGQoKsP3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the framing that the restoration latent space matters more than the generator choice compelling, with comprehensive, well-controlled experiments (four benchmarks, runtime, ablations, VAE-latent comparison).
TWHGQoKsP3.main_concern: The DINOv3 versus SD3-VAE comparison is not fully controlled (different token width and input projections), and novelty relative to RAE/RAEv2 and vision-foundation-feature SR guidance is unclear.

eNPLqnZHfT.one_liner: Learns shared and specialized parameter-group modules inside dense LLMs from domain-conditioned and cross-domain gradient similarity.
eNPLqnZHfT.problem: LLMs train on heterogeneous data mixtures that need both shared knowledge and specialization, while existing modular approaches impose explicit components or find modules by interpretability analysis after training.
eNPLqnZHfT.method: CORTEX partitions trainable matrices into parameter groups and learns module assignments from domain-conditioned gradient and cross-domain gradient similarity. It also introduces a selective lesion score and module-domain mutual information to characterize lesion effects and alignment.
eNPLqnZHfT.key_idea: Assign parameter groups to shared or domain-specific modules during training using domain-conditioned versus cross-domain gradient similarity, keeping the dense architecture.
eNPLqnZHfT.evidence: Experiments with 160M, Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-32B backbone models on synthetic and real domains.
eNPLqnZHfT.claimed_gains: Highest synthetic-domain exact match and largest average perplexity reduction, while remaining competitive on real-domain evaluations, with no numbers stated.
eNPLqnZHfT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that learning internal modularization in a dense model is a useful direction that adds no inference-time routing, and the empirical results compare favorably with MoE-style baselines.
eNPLqnZHfT.main_concern: The method looks like domain-conditioned gradient reweighting, so the benefit of the learned assignment over simpler gradient-weighting baselines is not established.

GYAq3FTjvs.one_liner: Augments the observed tensor dictionary with a latent component for tensor low-rank representation, applied to anchor-graph multi-view clustering.
GYAq3FTjvs.problem: Tensor low-rank representation uses the observed tensor as its own dictionary, which captures the underlying subspace poorly when data are limited and noisy.
GYAq3FTjvs.method: LT-LRR adds an unobserved latent component to the dictionary and admits a closed-form structural characterization under the t-product, with low-rank constraints on the representation and latent correction tensors. ETRL-SMVC applies it to anchor graph learning through compact dictionary-based tensor factorization instead of sample-level self-representation.
GYAq3FTjvs.key_idea: Augment the observed-tensor dictionary with a latent tensor, giving a closed-form t-product self-representation with low-rank representation and correction tensors, and apply it on anchor graphs.
GYAq3FTjvs.evidence: Experiments on benchmark datasets, with ablations of the low-rank regularizers (per reviews).
GYAq3FTjvs.claimed_gains: Consistently outperforms competitors while maintaining favorable scalability, with no numbers stated.
GYAq3FTjvs.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that adding a latent component to tensor representation is well motivated for limited or noisy data, and the method gives competitive clustering results with supportive ablations.
GYAq3FTjvs.main_concern: Scalability rests on theoretical complexity without runtime or memory comparisons, and the latent mechanism's own contribution and its relation to existing latent low-rank methods are not isolated.

wfkAb1ORCz.one_liner: Benchmarks tabular regression objectives, finds quantile loss beats MSE, and adds heteroskedasticity-aware quantile loss with input-dependent label smoothing.
wfkAb1ORCz.problem: The choice of regression objective for tabular deep learning is understudied and comparisons are confounded by datasets, backbones and protocols, and even with quantile loss, regions with different target noise peak at different epochs so one global early-stopping checkpoint is a compromise.
wfkAb1ORCz.method: Systematically re-evaluates regression objectives across established tabular datasets and multiple neural backbones, then introduces a heteroskedasticity-aware extension of quantile loss (AdaQR per the reviews) that uses input-dependent label smoothing.
wfkAb1ORCz.key_idea: Extend quantile loss with input-dependent label smoothing that accounts for heteroskedastic target noise, addressing the mismatch of best epochs across uncertainty regions.
wfkAb1ORCz.evidence: Re-evaluation across established tabular datasets and multiple backbones (41 datasets per reviews, with AdaQR evaluated on 28).
wfkAb1ORCz.claimed_gains: Quantile loss gives consistent aggregate improvements over MSE across the tested backbones, many other proposed objectives give limited or inconsistent gains, and the new loss improves over quantile loss (rest truncated), with no numbers stated.
wfkAb1ORCz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is important and understudied and the benchmark is extensive and rigorous, with a well-written analysis.
wfkAb1ORCz.main_concern: AdaQR gains are small, it is evaluated on fewer datasets than the benchmark and adds a learnable parameter and a hyperparameter, and foundation models are not included.

bTFXpRaA8A.one_liner: Learns state-level return relevance from real trajectories to focus exploration, model learning and imagination in Dreamer.
bTFXpRaA8A.problem: World-model bias can distort return differences among weakly supported local behaviors, shrinking or reversing real return advantages in imagination and misguiding policy optimization.
bTFXpRaA8A.method: FocusDreamer learns state-level return relevance from completed real trajectories, characterized by criticality (relative strength) and polarity (direction of return-predictive progression), and uses criticality to concentrate exploration, model learning and imagination while polarity modulates policy-side intervention, without altering the Dreamer objectives.
bTFXpRaA8A.key_idea: Estimate per-state criticality and polarity of return relevance from real trajectories, and allocate exploration, model learning and imagination to high-criticality states.
bTFXpRaA8A.claimed_gains: A 53.1% average return improvement over DreamerV3 on DMControl.
bTFXpRaA8A.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that prioritizing return-relevant states is interesting and well motivated, with theoretical and ablation analysis supporting the resource-allocation scheme at minimal overhead.
bTFXpRaA8A.main_concern: The empirical evaluation is thin: no confidence intervals or seed information, some results within error bars, and only low-dimensional benchmark subsets.

w3MqNWQDZV.one_liner: Lifts transformer arithmetic-circuit lower bounds to numerically-branched Word-RAM algorithms, preserving the LH N^(omega-o(1)) time bound.
w3MqNWQDZV.problem: It was open whether the Saha-Xu-Ye-Yu transformer lower bound for extended arithmetic circuits survives in the Word-RAM model, whose algorithms branch on the values they compute.
w3MqNWQDZV.method: Defines numerically-branched Word-RAM algorithms, whose real-cell operations come from +, -, x, /, exp and ln and whose real values reach word memory only by comparison or by bit reads through functions with level sets that are countable unions of intervals. Proves that any circuit lower bound whose reduction reads only local information transfers to them.
w3MqNWQDZV.key_idea: Work with the algorithm's own trace: if every circuit matching f on some open subset has size at least s, any numerically-branched algorithm for f takes time at least s.
w3MqNWQDZV.evidence: One theorem and a corollary proved formally, with a matrix-multiplication application per reviews; no experiments.
w3MqNWQDZV.claimed_gains: A time lower bound of LH N^(omega-o(1)) for numerically-branched algorithms for all omega >= 2.
w3MqNWQDZV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the proofs are sound and the lifting theorem usefully moves transformer lower bounds from arithmetic circuits closer to the machine models transformers run on, with applicability beyond transformers.
w3MqNWQDZV.main_concern: Clarity drops sharply in the later sections, and the exact-real-arithmetic model with a broad class of bit-reading operations limits practical relevance.

H6BXp56mQj.one_liner: Adapts frozen diffusion SBI models to revised priors via an exact score-transport identity, with no extra simulation or training.
H6BXp56mQj.problem: Amortized SBI models are tied to the prior used in training, but scientific analyses often need revised priors as knowledge accumulates or assumptions change.
H6BXp56mQj.method: Spectra uses an exact score-transport identity to obtain the adapted score from a frozen diffusion model in closed form for structured prior changes, through a single transformed query. Per the reviews, it extends to mixture prior ratios by estimating component weights.
H6BXp56mQj.key_idea: Transform the query to the frozen diffusion model so its output equals the score of the revised-prior posterior, in closed form for structured prior ratios.
H6BXp56mQj.claimed_gains: Accurate adaptation under strong prior shifts at low online sampling cost across six SBI benchmarks, with no numbers stated.
H6BXp56mQj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the exact score-transport result is elegant, well written and reproducible, and that it improves on PriorGuide, especially in runtime and for narrow target priors.
H6BXp56mQj.main_concern: Applicability is limited: experiments use relatively low-dimensional parameter spaces, and the method needs prior ratios of a specific quadratic-exponential form whose practical frequency is unclear.

6fMQxKz49U.one_liner: Benchmark and entity-level rubric evaluator for abstract image-editing instructions, such as mood, judged by a VLM.
6fMQxKz49U.problem: Image editing benchmarks focus on explicit, literal commands, leaving abstract instructions such as mood largely unexplored.
6fMQxKz49U.method: They formalize a definition and taxonomy of abstract image editing, introduce Entity-Rubrics, which breaks abstract edits into individual entity-level assessments, and contribute AbstractEdit, a benchmark of abstract editing across diverse real-world scenes.
6fMQxKz49U.key_idea: Break each abstract edit into individual entity-level rubric assessments scored by a VLM judge instead of one holistic score.
6fMQxKz49U.evidence: Evaluation of 11 leading editing models on AbstractEdit and a human study (1,080 ratings per reviews) of agreement with Entity-Rubrics, on a test set of 470 samples over 257 context images per reviews.
6fMQxKz49U.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the abstract-editing problem is timely and that the identification-versus-specificity taxonomy and paired abstract and explicit prompts form a useful benchmark design with more interpretable entity-level diagnostics.
6fMQxKz49U.main_concern: The VLM judge (Gemini 3 Flash) is not independently validated and shares a family with the top-ranked Gemini editors, with only moderate per-entity agreement (kappa 0.41).

7RpZD4ii4y.one_liner: Self-supervised audio encoder combining recording-level contrast with masked-patch latent discrimination against other recordings' teacher targets.
7RpZD4ii4y.problem: Recording-level contrastive objectives encourage agreement between pooled audio representations but do not explicitly supervise time-frequency local representations.
7RpZD4ii4y.method: AudioFM combines recording-level contrast with patch-wise masked latent discrimination, in which a student predicts representations of masked patches from visible context and identifies their full-view teacher targets among candidates from other recordings. Weaker supervision from eligible temporal neighbors encourages local temporal consistency.
7RpZD4ii4y.key_idea: Identify each masked patch's full-view teacher target among candidates from other recordings, alongside recording-level contrast and temporal-neighbor supervision.
7RpZD4ii4y.evidence: Linear probing, fine-tuning, and zero-shot transfer across diverse audio domains, including general audio, bioacoustics, medical acoustics, and speech emotion, with AudioSet pretraining of about 1.68M clips per reviews.
7RpZD4ii4y.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the evaluation is broad, spanning general audio, bioacoustics, medical acoustics, and speech emotion, with consistent gains over prior self-supervised baselines.
7RpZD4ii4y.main_concern: The methodological contribution is incremental over AudioMosaic, and ablations do not compare the new objectives with matched latent-regression or alternative contrastive objectives.

gXZqO79EIr.one_liner: Proves behavioral Nash equilibria of mean field games have equivalent mixed equilibria over populations of deterministic-policy agents.
gXZqO79EIr.problem: Mean field games rely on behavioral homogeneity (one shared policy) and policy stochasticity (randomized actions), whose necessity has not been questioned.
gXZqO79EIr.method: They prove, analogously to Kuhn's theorem, that for any behavioral-strategy Nash equilibrium of an MFG there is a constructively equivalent mixed-strategy equilibrium over a population of agents with diverse deterministic policies. This yields Fictitious Play and finite-agent learning variants that use only pure policies.
gXZqO79EIr.key_idea: Replace each randomized policy with an occupancy-weighted population of deterministic policies so population-level mixing reproduces the same state distributions.
gXZqO79EIr.evidence: Equilibrium-equivalence proofs, new pure-policy learning algorithms (Fictitious Play and finite-agent variants), and experiments on performance, scalability, and behavior on multi-agent RL tasks.
gXZqO79EIr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the Kuhn-style equivalence between behavioral and population-level mixed equilibria is a clean, well-motivated theoretical contribution.
gXZqO79EIr.main_concern: The proof of the finite-population guarantee is challenged as incorrect because it treats an agent's state as independent of its assigned pure policy.

f77ozA8Rwc.one_liner: Slow/fast parameter groups with distinct learning rates and sync frequencies, plus peer consensus weighted by client compatibility.
f77ozA8Rwc.problem: Data heterogeneity in decentralized federated learning is non-uniform across parameters and across clients, but existing methods apply largely uniform optimization and consensus rules.
f77ozA8Rwc.method: GeoSF dynamically organizes parameters into slow parameters (stable across clients, smaller learning rates, more frequent synchronization) and fast parameters (respond to local data, evolve faster, synchronize less often). At the client level it adapts peer-to-peer consensus to client-wise collaboration geometry, meaning compatibility between clients.
f77ozA8Rwc.key_idea: Partition parameters dynamically by cross-client stability into slow and fast groups with different learning rates and synchronization intervals, and weight peer consensus by client-pair compatibility.
f77ozA8Rwc.evidence: Feature-skew and label-skew image and text classification (including CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and Office10) across several architectures, communication topologies, and client counts, plus theoretical analysis.
f77ozA8Rwc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that jointly modeling parameter-wise adaptation timescales and client-wise compatibility, instead of using uniform rules, is a flexible way to balance shared knowledge and personalization, backed by broad experiments.
f77ozA8Rwc.main_concern: The framework introduces many sensitive hyperparameters (learning rates, shrinkage coefficient, communication interval, temperature, shared-parameter ratio) and an unquantified per-client computation overhead.

UmzQqgrCPV.one_liner: DARWIN co-evolves a jailbreak attacker with an external strategy pool and an adversarially trained guardrail in a continual attack-defense loop
UmzQqgrCPV.problem: Most LLM safety evaluation and defense is static, using fixed attack methods and fixed malicious prompt datasets, while real adversaries keep evolving their attacks.
UmzQqgrCPV.method: DARWIN-Attack discovers attack strategies from broad external sources, generates variants through self-reflection and genetic evolution, filters them by performance against aligned LLMs, and adaptively selects and composes them using feedback from target LLMs and guardrails. Guardrails are continuously updated through the attack-defense loop, with benign disguising of adversarial training data per reviewers.
UmzQqgrCPV.key_idea: Keep jailbreak strategies in an external pool evolved by discovery, mutation, and selection, and train the guardrail online against the evolving attacker with benign-disguised counterparts.
UmzQqgrCPV.evidence: Attack success against frontier LLMs and guardrails compared with LSA and MAGIC, guard evaluation on static benchmarks (unsafe recall, over-refusal, JBB-Benign), and ablations.
UmzQqgrCPV.claimed_gains: DARWIN-Attack reaches nearly 100% attack success on DeepSeek-V4-Pro, over 90% on GPT-5.5, and nearly 100% on YuFeng-XGuard, outperforming recent evolving frameworks such as LSA and MAGIC.
UmzQqgrCPV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the strong attack results over LSA and MAGIC, the explicit expanding strategy pool evolved without fine-tuning the attacker, and thorough ablations including benign disguising for guard training.
UmzQqgrCPV.main_concern: The static-to-continuous-loop framing is overclaimed given prior evolving frameworks, the methods section lacks key details, and the guard is never evaluated against a strong adaptive attacker other than its own trainer.

vFiySeyi1k.one_liner: SCARS redirects RLVR rollout budget toward under-covered successful regions using a hierarchical semantic tree and prefix-conditioned generation
vFiySeyi1k.problem: In RLVR, successful responses concentrate in fewer semantic reasoning modes as training proceeds, so finite-rollout on-policy sampling revisits dominant modes and limits policy improvement, which the paper attributes to finite-sample policy gradient estimation.
vFiySeyi1k.method: SCARS organizes discovered responses and intermediate reasoning states in a hierarchical semantic tree and redirects rollout budget to under-covered successful regions through prefix-conditioned generation, with prefix credit reassignment per reviewers.
vFiySeyi1k.key_idea: Cluster successful reasoning into a hierarchical semantic tree and spend rollout budget on prefixes from under-covered branches rather than relying on policy entropy.
vFiySeyi1k.evidence: Multiple reasoning benchmarks with GRPO and DAPO (including Qwen3-4B-Base per reviewers), a theoretical analysis of concentration under finite samples, and ablations.
vFiySeyi1k.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract claims improved overall reasoning performance and substantially higher successful-response diversity than baselines, without figures)
vFiySeyi1k.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the distinction between token entropy and successful-reasoning diversity well motivated, the theoretical and ablation analysis thorough, and prefix reuse a practical way to revisit rare successful paths.
vFiySeyi1k.main_concern: Training cost is unreported (32 initial responses per prompt and an 8B embedding model), gains are small on some models, and it is unclear how much comes from semantic coverage versus reinforcing successful prefixes.

pQ2RUGx1FY.one_liner: Introduces games with stochastic action sets and a ranking-regret algorithm that computes compactly represented Nash equilibria in two-player zero-sum games.
pQ2RUGx1FY.problem: When players' available actions are randomly restricted, strategies and Nash equilibria have prohibitively large representations and existing algorithms scale poorly.
pQ2RUGx1FY.method: Under independent action availability between players, equilibria of two-player zero-sum GSAS are approximately representable by a compact vector of size |A_i|. An algorithm minimizing ranking regret converges to NE with high probability, and a stochastic approximation over its iterates recovers a compact NE.
pQ2RUGx1FY.key_idea: Minimize ranking regret over action rankings and represent strategies by a vector of size |A_i| instead of per-subset policies.
pQ2RUGx1FY.evidence: Theoretical results (compact representation, convergence rate, and a correlated-availability lower bound per the reviews) plus experiments including a runtime comparison.
pQ2RUGx1FY.claimed_gains: Convergence to NE with high probability at rate O(sqrt(|A_i| log|A_i| / T)) for time horizon T, with equilibria represented by a compact vector of size |A_i|.
pQ2RUGx1FY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper is clearly written, introduces a simple and valid new setting with a systematic theoretical treatment, and gives a useful compact-representation result with a learning guarantee.
pQ2RUGx1FY.main_concern: Central ingredients have substantial precedent (Luce-model results and FTPL with counting-asleep estimators), and the independence and i.i.d. availability assumptions need concrete motivation.

ndUcmJ8Zrx.one_liner: Training-free monitoring of predicted clean outputs during diffusion that redirects generation away from IP characters using a generic-category-anchored contrast.
ndUcmJ8Zrx.problem: Text-to-image models can produce recognizable IP characters from direct names or name-free descriptions, which prompt-inspection and parameter-level mitigations handle poorly.
ndUcmJ8Zrx.method: The framework monitors target-like semantics through the predicted clean output early in diffusion, then redirects the same trajectory with a generic-category-anchored contrast that reduces target-related components while anchoring the requested visual content, without modifying model parameters.
ndUcmJ8Zrx.key_idea: Detect emerging target identity from the predicted clean output and remove the target-aligned component using a generic-category anchor within the same generation trajectory.
ndUcmJ8Zrx.evidence: Experiments on FLUX.1-dev and Stable Diffusion 3.5 Medium under direct and indirect prompting, measuring target-character detections and consistency with prompt-specified visual characteristics.
ndUcmJ8Zrx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is practically relevant and the training-free design is well motivated, with strong experimental support that predicted clean outputs reveal target identity early in sampling.
ndUcmJ8Zrx.main_concern: Novelty over inference-time negative guidance is not established, the adaptive threshold and comparison with Guardians of Generation are unjustified, and the method assumes the target character is known in advance.

SJMGtBGVvG.one_liner: PIVOT corrects frozen neural operators by probing their responses to small physically admissible input perturbations.
SJMGtBGVvG.problem: Neural operators under distribution shift lose physical consistency and accumulate error over long rollouts, and adaptation methods that update parameters underuse the physical information frozen operators retain.
SJMGtBGVvG.method: For each sample PIVOT learns admissible perturbation directions, queries the frozen operator with paired opposite perturbations, checks candidate response corrections for physical consistency, and a lightweight adapter weights them per location with bounded correction magnitude.
SJMGtBGVvG.key_idea: Extract local physical response directions and magnitudes from paired perturbed predictions of a frozen operator, and apply them as physically checked, bounded corrections.
SJMGtBGVvG.evidence: Experiments across six datasets per reviews, with metrics for PDE residuals, balance violations, frequency and energy errors; the abstract is cut off before results.
SJMGtBGVvG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the observation that frozen operators retain accurate local responses under shift is interesting, and that the evaluation separates accuracy from physical consistency.
SJMGtBGVvG.main_concern: The method has many heuristic components, and the gains are not isolated to probing since much of the physical-consistency gain comes from a generic acceptance step that no baseline receives.

rwI0uJi435.one_liner: Discrete-token Transformer trained on 12 aligned modalities predicts any modality at any time from any input combination, enabling chained generation.
rwI0uJi435.problem: Video models usually work in one representation space (RGB or semantic features) although different spaces capture complementary aspects and the best prediction space varies by sample.
rwI0uJi435.method: They build an any-to-any multimodal video model (called Video-4M in reviews) that predicts any modality at any time step given any inputs, using temporal masking strategies (FCFF, FCAF, CFP) for future prediction and a new dataset, K600-MM, with 12 temporally aligned modalities. Chained generation decomposes a task such as caption-to-video into sub-tasks that predict intermediate modalities.
rwI0uJi435.key_idea: Traverse a time-modality grid with one masked-token model so tasks can be chained through intermediate modalities and future prediction can choose its modality space.
rwI0uJi435.evidence: Chained versus direct generation with the same Large model (FVD and caption alignment per reviews), future prediction in different modality spaces, and comparison with specialist models on several tasks.
rwI0uJi435.claimed_gains: not stated; the visible abstract reports only that chained generation yields higher-quality generations than direct generation and that no single prediction space is optimal.
rwI0uJi435.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree one model covering perception, generation, and forecasting across many modalities is a useful extension of any-to-any modeling and that chaining improves quality in the evaluated setting.
rwI0uJi435.main_concern: Chained-generation gains are not separated from its extra inference cost, and the best forecasting chain is chosen using the realized future, showing potential rather than a usable selection method.

P7mAH8IlqC.one_liner: CoFree preserves LLM reasoning in embedding models using reference-guided SFT followed by RL with embedding and reasoning rewards.
P7mAH8IlqC.problem: Specializing LLMs toward embedding objectives can suppress useful reasoning generation or produce retrieval-irrelevant text, which the authors call reasoning collapse.
P7mAH8IlqC.method: Stage one applies reference-guided supervised fine-tuning to restore reasoning ability while retaining the foundation embedding model's representation strength. Stage two runs reinforcement learning with an embedding-oriented reward and a reasoning-oriented reward.
P7mAH8IlqC.key_idea: Couple reasoning generation and embedding optimization by first restoring reasoning with reference-guided SFT, then rewarding both retrieval relevance and reasoning quality in RL.
P7mAH8IlqC.evidence: Multiple retrieval benchmarks and model sizes (1.5B and 4B per reviews), ablations, transfer tests of generated reasoning to six frozen encoders with Echo and length-matched Noise controls, and a real-world retrieval deployment.
P7mAH8IlqC.claimed_gains: CoFree-4B achieves an average absolute improvement of 2.8 (abstract text cuts off before the baseline and units).
P7mAH8IlqC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is well motivated, the evaluation is broad, and the generated reasoning text helps frozen encoders beyond Echo and noise controls at low generation length.
P7mAH8IlqC.main_concern: The source of gains is unclear because teacher knowledge (Qwen3-235B reasoning traces and Qwen3-Reranker signals) is uncontrolled, and the RL stage adds only a modest improvement.

ZBxXrGIRAW.one_liner: Frozen time-series foundation model augmented with evolving memory, an RL-trained retrieval trigger, and memory-based residual forecast correction.
ZBxXrGIRAW.problem: Most time-series foundation models stay fixed after pretraining and cannot incorporate new experience as data distributions evolve.
ZBxXrGIRAW.method: MemTime adds a self-evolving memory that acquires, uses, and consolidates deployment-time experiences without changing backbone parameters; an RL-based Cognitive Sentinel decides when to retrieve memory, and a Mental Retracer turns retrieved experiences into correction signals that adjust the forecast trajectory (abstract truncated).
ZBxXrGIRAW.key_idea: Separate when to adapt from how to adapt: a learned sentinel triggers memory retrieval, and retrieved experience yields residual corrections to a frozen flow-matching forecaster.
ZBxXrGIRAW.evidence: Streaming forecasting experiments against zero-shot time-series foundation models, with Sundial as the main frozen backbone per reviews, plus long-term stability and efficiency analyses.
ZBxXrGIRAW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem practically relevant and the framework coherent, combining adaptive memory invocation, residual correction, and memory maintenance while keeping the backbone frozen.
ZBxXrGIRAW.main_concern: Main results compare only against zero-shot foundation models even though MemTime trains auxiliary modules on target-domain validation data, and comparisons with online and test-time adaptation baselines are missing.

kw1764GtFE.one_liner: Stabilizes zeroth-order fine-tuning of sparse MoE models by replaying recorded expert selections within one-sided finite-difference estimates.
kw1764GtFE.problem: Parameter perturbations in zeroth-order fine-tuning change which experts a token routes to, mixing continuous parameter effects with discrete routing changes in finite-difference estimates.
kw1764GtFE.method: At each update an unperturbed forward pass records the selected expert indices; perturbed queries reuse them while recomputing routing weights, and selections are refreshed at the next update. The recording pass also supplies a shared loss baseline, so replay adds no forward queries to the one-sided estimator.
kw1764GtFE.key_idea: Fix expert indices from an unperturbed pass during perturbed queries, which removes the expert-switching term from the finite-difference estimate, and reuse that pass as the one-sided baseline.
kw1764GtFE.evidence: Two sparse MoE backbones and six downstream tasks, a mathematical decomposition isolating the expert-switching term, and ablations separating expert replay from router freezing.
kw1764GtFE.claimed_gains: Highest average accuracy among evaluated ZO methods across two backbones and six tasks, faster loss descent and negligible memory or runtime overhead; no numbers stated.
kw1764GtFE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper identifies a clear optimization issue (expert switching under perturbation), formalizes it with a decomposition, and fixes it with a direct method of low overhead.
kw1764GtFE.main_concern: Reviewers question the evidence and novelty: the main comparison confounds replay with router freezing, experiments use a single seed with no uncertainty, and replay is added to an existing ZO framework with unclear advantage over LoRA or QLoRA.

5o0FTJld2s.one_liner: Multi-frame LiDAR and 4D radar fusion for adverse-weather 3D detection using reliability-aware temporal reweighting and radar-guided compensation.
5o0FTJld2s.problem: Single-frame LiDAR and 4D radar fusion cannot fully observe targets in adverse weather, and naive multi-frame fusion accumulates temporal noise and unreliable history, giving little or no gain.
5o0FTJld2s.method: TMF's Temporal Radar Denoising (TRD) block performs reliability-aware temporal reweighting that discounts clutter at aggregation time, followed by a Radar-Guided Temporal Compensation (RGTC) block; the abstract is truncated after this point.
5o0FTJld2s.key_idea: Reweight historical frames by estimated reliability so radar clutter does not accumulate during multi-frame aggregation, then compensate temporal features guided by radar.
5o0FTJld2s.evidence: Experiments on K-Radar (V1.0 and V2.0 protocols) with temporal-window, filtering-ratio and computational-cost analyses, per reviews.
5o0FTJld2s.claimed_gains: The visible abstract gives no numbers; reviewers cite a 6.49% AP3D gain highlighted in the abstract and contributions.
5o0FTJld2s.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the motivation is practical, that using historical observations to compensate degraded weather frames is worthwhile, and that K-Radar experiments show gains with informative ablations.
5o0FTJld2s.main_concern: The gain over a matched temporal baseline is small (+1.13 AP3D over the adapted L4DR baseline in Table 4), recent fusion methods are missing from comparisons, and some method details are unclear.

NDjJoW9GzZ.one_liner: Benchmark holding spoken content fixed while varying speaker and language to measure behavioral consistency of speech-input multimodal LLMs.
NDjJoW9GzZ.problem: Existing speech-input MLLM benchmarks report aggregate task performance and say little about whether behavior stays stable when different speakers say the same content.
NDjJoW9GzZ.method: 3MSpeechBench is built from four established corpora and covers spoken multiple-choice QA, spoken visual QA, article summarization and dialogue summarization, with 50 speakers per language and up to 10 languages. Models are scored on task performance and on within-instance consistency across speakers.
NDjJoW9GzZ.key_idea: Fix the linguistic content and vary only the speaker, then measure within-instance consistency across speakers alongside task accuracy.
NDjJoW9GzZ.evidence: Evaluation of MLLMs on four tasks across up to 10 languages and 50 speakers per language, with content fidelity checked by two ASR systems and speaker similarity (per reviews).
NDjJoW9GzZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the controlled same-content, different-voice design is valuable, scales beyond prior work across languages and open-ended tasks, and is validated for content and speaker fidelity.
NDjJoW9GzZ.main_concern: Reviewers say the consistency analysis is not sufficiently validated: there is no same-speaker re-synthesis baseline to attribute instability to speaker, open-ended results depend on one LLM for unit extraction without a human audit, and synthesized voices lack manual checks.

3DRMF68SSD.one_liner: Estimates mutual information between discrete variables by framing it as a domain-transfer problem solved with discrete diffusion bridge matching.
3DRMF68SSD.problem: Conventional mutual information estimators have difficulty with discrete data.
3DRMF68SSD.method: DBMI frames MI estimation as a domain-transfer problem and builds an estimator on the discrete-state formulation of bridge matching models. Per reviews it combines the InfoBridge MI formulation with categorical bridge matching and samples intermediate states from reference bridges.
3DRMF68SSD.key_idea: Express MI between discrete endpoints as transition-level KL divergences along a shared discrete bridge, estimated with categorical bridge matching without simulating full trajectories.
3DRMF68SSD.evidence: Three MI estimation benchmarks: low-dimensional, DNA with low-dimensional tags, and image-based.
3DRMF68SSD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper is clearly written and technically sound, with strong empirical performance on benchmarks where ground-truth MI is available.
3DRMF68SSD.main_concern: Reviewers question the significance of the contribution, since the estimator appears to follow from combining InfoBridge with existing categorical bridge matching, and they also question the factorized estimator's justification and the limited dimensionality (D=50) of benchmarks.

W7RSDab0a4.one_liner: EditFlow is a flow-matching model editing masked residue variables of bound peptides, supporting redesign and property optimization via search.
W7RSDab0a4.problem: Peptide lead optimization needs control over which residues and which molecular variables change while keeping target engagement, which pocket-conditioned sequence-structure generation does not provide directly.
W7RSDab0a4.method: Residue-variable masks specify the scope of each edit, so one conditional model regenerates selected amino acid identities, backbone geometry and side-chain conformations while preserving the receptor and unselected peptide variables. A frozen editor plus external property evaluation and search gives iterative optimization through local modifications.
W7RSDab0a4.key_idea: Condition a flow-matching model on residue-by-variable masks so selected sequence, backbone and side-chain variables are regenerated while all others stay fixed.
W7RSDab0a4.evidence: Protein-peptide complex benchmarks for joint sequence-structure redesign and full generation, and single- and multi-objective property optimization using PeptiVerse predictors and Rosetta interface energy with search policies (best-of-N, beam search, MCTS).
W7RSDab0a4.claimed_gains: No numbers in the available text; the abstract claims leading joint sequence-structure redesign, competitive full generation, and better property improvement and trade-offs than strong baselines.
W7RSDab0a4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the unified editing framework with explicit residue-variable masks is flexible and clearly presented, supporting several editing operations and swappable search objectives with one set of weights.
W7RSDab0a4.main_concern: Validation is weak: property gains are measured with the same predictors used for selection with no independent or wet-lab check, and joint-redesign baselines (random-backbone Rosetta) are too weak to show the benefit.

4RzWLdQgcX.one_liner: Inserts a frozen pretrained tabular foundation model column encoder before existing feature-scoring rules to screen features in embedded space.
4RzWLdQgcX.problem: Feature screening that scores raw values in high-dimensional tabular learning can miss nonlinear or distributional structure.
4RzWLdQgcX.method: PACE places a frozen tabular foundation model column encoder before an existing feature-scoring rule, expanding each feature into a higher-dimensional contextual representation. It does not train an encoder or modify downstream predictors.
4RzWLdQgcX.key_idea: Embed each column with a frozen tabular foundation model and apply a standard dependence score to that representation instead of the raw values.
4RzWLdQgcX.evidence: Controlled studies, TALENT and SelectArena datasets with varied downstream learners and feature budgets, matched random-weight and random-feature controls, and comparisons with task-fitted and attribution-based selectors.
4RzWLdQgcX.claimed_gains: not stated (qualitative only: better raw-space screening of nonlinear dependence at modest extra encoding cost and generally better downstream results than matched raw-space screening).
4RzWLdQgcX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the plug-and-play idea is sound, with random-weight and random-feature controls showing that pretraining rather than extra dimensions drives the gains and with strong feature recovery in controlled simulations.
4RzWLdQgcX.main_concern: The TALENT benchmark pads datasets with i.i.d. Gaussian noise columns, so gains may reflect separating noise from real columns by distribution shape rather than finding relevant features.

cizDyhcm7v.one_liner: Self-play where one policy asks and answers video questions in program-rendered environments with execution-verified labels and evolving rules.
cizDyhcm7v.problem: Existing video self-play trains on fixed recorded videos, cannot alter event dynamics, and relies on noisy pseudo-labels such as majority voting that can reinforce shared model errors.
cizDyhcm7v.method: Executing a program renders a video with the ground-truth option and interval for each question. A single policy plays Questioner and Solver, answering with timestamped evidence lines, and is trained on execution-grounded rewards; Solver performance steers a curriculum and the policy selects rule changes that enrich later event dynamics.
cizDyhcm7v.key_idea: Render videos by executing programs so answers and intervals come from execution traces, and let the policy choose rule changes that evolve the environment.
cizDyhcm7v.evidence: Trained solely on simple programs without supervised fine-tuning or external video data and compared with base models and recent self-play baselines; reviews cite Charades-STA and four backbones.
cizDyhcm7v.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract claims gains over base models and recent self-play baselines but is cut off before any numbers).
cizDyhcm7v.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that executable supervision gives reliable labels and temporal evidence, and that training on simple rendered videos transfers to real-video benchmarks across several backbones.
cizDyhcm7v.main_concern: Sources of gain are not isolated (no controlled comparison of execution-derived versus majority-vote labels or policy-selected versus random rule changes), and hand-designed environments may not scale to real-world video.

F9WNs3dn5t.one_liner: Removes objects and effects from panoramic video using spherical RoPE and SphericalControl, trained on a new paired dataset.
F9WNs3dn5t.problem: Perspective-based removal methods struggle on panoramic video because ERP seam discontinuities and polar distortions hinder spherical reconstruction and target-effect association, and paired panoramic removal data are scarce.
F9WNs3dn5t.method: The authors build PanoVOR (1.53M panoramic frames, 26.6 hours, source-clean pairs with target masks). PanoErase first learns panorama-aware completion on large-scale panoramic video with SC-RoPE, then refines it with paired supervision through SphericalControl, which combines target-specific local evidence with panorama-wide context.
F9WNs3dn5t.key_idea: Encode spherical positional relations with SC-RoPE during completion pretraining, then condition removal on both target-local evidence and panorama-wide context through SphericalControl.
F9WNs3dn5t.evidence: PanoVOR-Eval and PanoVOR-Wild benchmarks against existing object removal methods, with ablations cited in reviews.
F9WNs3dn5t.claimed_gains: not stated (qualitative only: consistent improvements over existing methods, particularly in seam-crossing and polar regions).
F9WNs3dn5t.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree PanoVOR is a useful first paired dataset for panoramic object removal and that the geometry-aware design is well motivated and supported by ablations.
F9WNs3dn5t.main_concern: It is unclear whether gains come from the method or from training on PanoVOR, since baselines use released weights and none were fine-tuned on panoramic data.

iOMrEsKlZG.one_liner: Detects poisoned semantic-cache hits by searching shortened cache-key variants for similarity gains and checking whether removed text matters.
iOMrEsKlZG.problem: Semantic caches retrieve on embedding similarity alone, so an attacker can cache a malicious response under a query highly similar to benign requests, and embeddings lose information needed to separate valid from invalid hits.
iOMrEsKlZG.method: The defense exploits the rewrite-plus-residual structure of poisoning attacks. Deletion Gain searches shortened variants of the cached query for similarity gains, and an Answer Check tests whether the removed text contributes to the stored answer; the authors prove Deletion Gain stays positive when a deletion leaves text close enough to the rewrite.
iOMrEsKlZG.key_idea: Poisoned keys are a rewrite plus residual text, so deleting the residual raises similarity to the query; pair this Deletion Gain with a check that removed text drives the answer.
iOMrEsKlZG.evidence: Three poisoning attack categories including the new CAP attack, adaptive attacks, benign-query controls and vCache workloads per the reviews (abstract truncated before results).
iOMrEsKlZG.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract is cut off before the results).
iOMrEsKlZG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it is a practical, lightweight defense that needs no extra serving-time model calls and is evaluated against adaptive attacks and real workloads.
iOMrEsKlZG.main_concern: The defense targets a rewrite-plus-residual attack form and is evaluated mainly on simple Q&A under idealized cache conditions, leaving multi-turn, agentic and realistic cache-policy settings untested.

hyyEG3mnXh.one_liner: Backpropagates atomic-level structure and confidence objectives through the full diffusion sampling trajectory of co-folding models to optimize antibody sequences.
hyyEG3mnXh.problem: Stochastic diffusion structure decoders in modern co-folding models make gradient-based antibody design difficult, so existing methods use simpler predictors or bypass the diffusion process.
hyyEG3mnXh.method: AbPilot differentiates through the native diffusion trajectory to optimize antibody sequences with atomic-level geometric and confidence objectives. Adjoint-state recursion reduces activation memory to O(1) in diffusion depth, and orthogonal rectification uses an external structural verification as a search signal to mitigate predictor hacking.
hyyEG3mnXh.key_idea: Differentiate through sampled diffusion coordinates with adjoint-state recursion, and rectify gradients orthogonally against predictor hacking using an external structure verifier.
hyyEG3mnXh.evidence: A new 12-target de novo antibody design benchmark for VHH and scFv, plus a prospective VHH design against mICAM-1 (reviews cite a 50-design ELISA test and a distogram-surrogate ablation).
hyyEG3mnXh.claimed_gains: In silico success rates more than sevenfold those of the strongest baseline for both VHH and scFv on a 12-target benchmark, and prospective VHH design against mICAM-1 yields nanomolar binders.
hyyEG3mnXh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is well chosen, differentiating through the diffusion trajectory is practical, and the ablation against a distogram surrogate and the wet-lab results are promising.
hyyEG3mnXh.main_concern: Technical novelty is unclear relative to existing differentiable samplers and AlignProp-style backpropagation through denoising chains, and AF3 is used for both selection and final scoring with only a single-target wet-lab study.

6mOJW1VvOu.one_liner: Fine-tunes LLMs with closed-form first-order safety calibration, safety-preserving task updates and periodic recalibration to raise safety and utility together.
6mOJW1VvOu.problem: Safety-preserving fine-tuning methods only preserve safety, lack a theory of the optimal safety subspace and task update, and use a static safety subspace that becomes outdated as the model evolves.
6mOJW1VvOu.method: ASCENT models safety as a function S(theta) and uses its first-order approximation. Under a fixed rank and Frobenius-norm budget, the update built from the top-r singular components of the safety-function gradient maximizes the estimated safety change; task updates are then corrected to preserve safety and calibration is repeated periodically.
6mOJW1VvOu.key_idea: Build safety calibration updates from the top singular components of the safety-function gradient, correct task updates to preserve it, and recompute the safety subspace periodically.
6mOJW1VvOu.evidence: Four LLMs and four downstream tasks (16 model-task settings) with safety benchmarks, jailbreak attacks, component ablations and calibration-interval analyses, per the reviews.
6mOJW1VvOu.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract is cut off before the results).
6mOJW1VvOu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the first-order closed-form formulation is clear and verifiable and that experiments show consistent safety-utility gains across models and tasks.
6mOJW1VvOu.main_concern: Safety is judged by attack success rate under a judge the method optimizes, with no over-refusal or benign-request evaluation, and novelty over gradient-projection methods such as SPARD and SafeGrad is not tested by direct comparison.

6g4chvY7vj.one_liner: Benchmark scoring generated tests on accepting all valid and rejecting all invalid implementations, plus a cross-validation test generator.
6g4chvY7vj.problem: Evaluating generated tests against a single reference solution overlooks alternative valid implementations and can overstate test quality.
6g4chvY7vj.method: TestPrism has 300 test tasks from 17 sources and 3000 candidate implementations split evenly between valid and invalid; its Joint Success Function requires tests to fail on the initial program state, accept every valid candidate and reject every invalid one. TestHelix combines heterogeneous synthesis of test and repair pairs with peer cross validation and recursive self improvement.
6g4chvY7vj.key_idea: Score tests against a fixed panel of valid and invalid implementations, and generate tests through peer cross-validation with recursive self-improvement.
6g4chvY7vj.evidence: Fourteen baseline coding agent configurations on TestPrism, failure analysis, and TestHelix tested with two models.
6g4chvY7vj.claimed_gains: Joint Success Function reaches only 28.00% versus 59.67% for single reference success across fourteen configurations, and TestHelix improves it by 8.67 to 9.00 percentage points over native harness comparators across two models.
6g4chvY7vj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it addresses an important weakness of single-reference test evaluation and that the benchmark and failure analysis are useful.
6g4chvY7vj.main_concern: Candidate validity labels come from the source test suites with no independent audit, so label noise could bias the headline gap between joint and single-reference success.

C6SgO0M4n2.one_liner: Treats particle-group split and merge as state transitions of recurrent neuronal-world states that inherit memory instead of restarting history.
C6SgO0M4n2.problem: When coarse particle groups are reorganized, their current contents disconnect from the accumulated predictive context.
C6SgO0M4n2.method: On splits and merges, NWD recomputes physical moments from the unchanged particles while copying or combining compact memories locally, then shared recurrent dynamics refine the inherited context using each successor's current observations.
C6SgO0M4n2.key_idea: Regrouping is a state transition in which physical moments are recomputed from particles and recurrent memories are copied or combined, preserving history across split and merge.
C6SgO0M4n2.evidence: Four particle benchmarks (including N-body, Dam2D and Sand2D), memory ablations, and a theoretical analysis of decoder ambiguity and the reorganization-retention trade-off.
C6SgO0M4n2.claimed_gains: Lowest mean 100-step position NRMSE in all five settings, with 51.8-52.6% reductions over the recurrent-token baseline on N-body and 10.7-14.5% over fixed-cardinality variants.
C6SgO0M4n2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that memory inheritance across split and merge is a sound idea and NWD shows consistent gains, especially on N-body, with supporting ablations and physical diagnostics.
C6SgO0M4n2.main_concern: Gains are modest outside N-body, the memory-handoff ablation shows only a 2.8% drop, and the presentation is hard to follow.

Z0RV8JnMl5.one_liner: Reference-based object insertion fine-tuned on paired rendered scenes, with geometric foundation-model features and soft spatial attention guidance.
Z0RV8JnMl5.problem: Object insertion must preserve identity while adapting appearance and geometry, and scene-object interactions such as shadows, reflections and occlusions need supervision beyond the object region.
Z0RV8JnMl5.method: Builds a rendered dataset of scenes with and without selected objects plus multi-view, multi-illumination references, injects features from a pretrained geometric foundation model into the editing backbone, and adds soft spatial attention guidance for placement and object-scene interaction.
Z0RV8JnMl5.key_idea: Paired with/without-object renderings supervise shadows and reflections, while geometric foundation-model features and soft spatial attention guide placement.
Z0RV8JnMl5.evidence: A synthetic dataset (InsertWorld, BlenderKit assets), a benchmark of geometric and physical plausibility including a VLM-based Phy-VLM score, and ablations.
Z0RV8JnMl5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the full package of dataset, method and benchmark addresses a practically relevant, harder insertion setting and that the method outperforms existing models.
Z0RV8JnMl5.main_concern: Physical plausibility is learned from synthetic data and losses without explicit physical modeling, and is evaluated mostly with 2D image metrics and a VLM score on a single-source synthetic dataset.

VHD7PibsBE.one_liner: GraphRAG that speculates bridge clues on an LLM-free, text-order hypothetical graph, then corrects them for multi-hop retrieval.
VHD7PibsBE.problem: GraphRAG suffers from low-quality graphs, giving redundant retrieval results and biased retrieval paths that make second-hop evidence hard to reach.
VHD7PibsBE.method: A lightweight model serializes passages into entity-relation sequences to build a hypothetical graph (HypoKG) that preserves word order, and speculation-driven retrieval repeatedly locates clues and speculates bridge entities, with a correction step deriving the answer.
VHD7PibsBE.key_idea: Speculate bridge entities on a word-order-preserving graph using subject-predicate-object adjacency, rather than traversing a rigid, noisy constructed graph.
VHD7PibsBE.evidence: Multi-hop QA datasets (including MuSiQue) with a preliminary reachability study and indexing-cost and retriever-runtime comparisons against HippoRAG and KG-Translator.
VHD7PibsBE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the reachability analysis is a useful diagnostic and that HypoKG indexing is cheap (spaCy only, no LLM tokens) while keeping evidence traceable to source text.
VHD7PibsBE.main_concern: Efficiency is overclaimed because online cost is dominated by about 3.91 LLM calls per query with no end-to-end latency reported, and the method relies on English subject-predicate-object structure.

POJ7IYMTqS.one_liner: Training-free compositional diffusion planning that replaces overlap transitions with maximal-noise steps, plus a low-frequency spectral split.
POJ7IYMTqS.problem: Composing multimodal local plans on overlaps averages incompatible modes into infeasible long-horizon plans.
POJ7IYMTqS.method: MaxCD builds the next noisy state on overlaps from the denoised estimate and fresh Gaussian noise, dropping the predicted noise direction without extra denoiser evaluations, and applies this only to low-frequency components through a spectral split.
POJ7IYMTqS.key_idea: Discarding the predicted noise direction at overlap transitions forces mode-averaged overlaps to be revised rather than preserved.
POJ7IYMTqS.evidence: OGBench long-horizon planning (locomotion, object manipulation, mazes) and compositional panorama generation, built on pretrained CompDiffuser planners.
POJ7IYMTqS.claimed_gains: Substantially improves long-horizon planning on OGBench and the visual consistency of compositional panorama generation; no numbers stated.
POJ7IYMTqS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple, training-free, adds little compute, and clearly improves on CompDiffuser in the Giant mazes across several domains.
POJ7IYMTqS.main_concern: Novelty is limited because maximal-noise transitions match the maximum stochasticity in StochSync, and a closer training-free baseline (RCD) is not compared.

cQOyBCdKTa.one_liner: Localizes super-resolution hallucinations with VLM grid marks, then builds region-swapped preference pairs for region-level preference optimization.
cQOyBCdKTa.problem: Generative SR introduces hallucinated objects, textures or text, and image-level or predefined-unit preference signals do not localize the actual hallucinations.
cQOyBCdKTa.method: HGM has a VLM propose candidate regions on a 16x16 grid and verifies them against ground truth into a cell-level hallucination mask; HSPO swaps hallucinated and faithful regions among SR candidates from the same LR input to form preference pairs, and AHS scores hallucination severity.
cQOyBCdKTa.key_idea: Region-level preference pairs are made by exchanging hallucinated and faithful regions among candidates for the same input, so optimization targets local failures.
cQOyBCdKTa.evidence: Syn-TestSet and RealSR-4x with C-FLUX and DP2O backbones, ablations and human evaluation.
cQOyBCdKTa.claimed_gains: Lower hallucination scores than C-FLUX on Syn-TestSet and RealSR-4x; the abstract is cut off and gives no numbers.
cQOyBCdKTa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that localizing hallucinations and optimizing at region level is well motivated, with a sound region-exchange pair construction supported by ablations and human evaluation.
cQOyBCdKTa.main_concern: Generalization is shown on only two related SR models and two test sets, and the AHS metric lacks sufficient validation against human judgment.

LQHbXm498Y.one_liner: Models hand-object interaction videos as persistent interaction traces built from fast dense perception and slow temporal propagation.
LQHbXm498Y.problem: Existing approaches model hand-object entities, trajectories and relations as isolated cues, lacking a mechanism that keeps localized contact evidence and persistent identities across a video.
LQHbXm498Y.method: Fast-Slow Trace Identification combines dense interaction-aware perception with sparse temporal propagation to build traces of hands, objects, contact and state evolution, encoded as HOI mask videos and instance-aware trace marks, with causal identity and contact-attribution constraints.
LQHbXm498Y.key_idea: Dense fast perception captures brief contacts while sparse slow propagation keeps instance identities, producing traces fed to the multimodal LLM as masks and marks.
LQHbXm498Y.evidence: Fine-grained HOI video understanding benchmarks against RGB fine-tuned backbones and structured baselines using the same perception, with ablations.
LQHbXm498Y.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that linking brief contact evidence to persistent object identity is an important problem and that the fast-slow design shows clear gains over baselines, with ablations.
LQHbXm498Y.main_concern: It is unclear how contacts occurring between sparse slow-timeline frames reach the final representation, and the method is hard to follow with old baselines and hand-crafted contact masks.

rWcZNr7vK6.one_liner: Modulates domain-shifted class prototypes with a foreground distribution prior from support samples for cross-domain few-shot medical segmentation.
rWcZNr7vK6.problem: Domain shifts across imaging devices, protocols and modalities degrade few-shot medical segmentation, and existing methods overlook the support-query foreground distribution relationship.
rWcZNr7vK6.method: DA-Proto extracts a stable foreground distribution prior from target-domain support samples and uses it to modulate domain-shifted class prototypes into distribution-aligned prototypes, with a statistics encoder and intensity-statistic reconstruction used in training.
rWcZNr7vK6.key_idea: Support and query foreground distributions are consistent within a domain, so a foreground-statistics prior additively modulates class prototypes toward distribution-aligned prototypes.
rWcZNr7vK6.evidence: Multiple cross-domain settings, including cross-modality and cross-sequence transfers such as CT to MR, with ablations on the distribution components.
rWcZNr7vK6.claimed_gains: Outperforms prior methods across multiple cross-domain settings; no numbers in the abstract.
rWcZNr7vK6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the results are the strongest part, with the highest mean Dice in all four transfer directions and ablations showing the value of the distribution branch.
rWcZNr7vK6.main_concern: Novelty over standard statistical conditioning and prototype modulation is unclear, and one reviewer reports the released evaluation code does not match the described single-support-slice protocol.

CzC4NApviT.one_liner: Supervised GRN inference with expression-guided adaptive graph context, a teacher-induced higher-order view, and partner-based neighborhood contrastive learning.
CzC4NApviT.problem: Local message passing is bounded by incomplete reference topology, and same-gene contrastive alignment ignores known training TF-target partners as positives.
