CzC4NApviT.method: GRASP retains edges guided by expression, builds a teacher-induced higher-order view beyond recorded neighborhoods, and uses neighborhood contrastive learning with fixed training partners as positives within and across views, plus a role-specific decoder for ordered TF-target scores; evaluation uses pair-disjoint splits.
CzC4NApviT.key_idea: Training TF-target partners serve as extra positives in cross-view neighborhood contrastive learning, over graphs adapted by expression-guided edge retention and a higher-order teacher view.
CzC4NApviT.evidence: 42 evaluation settings (seven cell types, three reference networks, two gene set sizes) against eight baselines, with a 2^3 factorial ablation and pair-disjoint evaluation.
CzC4NApviT.claimed_gains: Achieves the highest results across 42 evaluation settings; the abstract is cut off and gives no numbers.
CzC4NApviT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the evaluation is broad (42 settings, full factorial ablation) and that the leakage finding in the standard edge split is useful to the community.
CzC4NApviT.main_concern: The method assembles known components with small gains on the Specific reference, and some baseline results (GENIE3 beating supervised models on STRING) raise protocol questions.

W8ySWD8L6y.one_liner: Rebuilds on-policy distillation advantages from pairwise comparisons within a small token neighborhood around the sampled token.
W8ySWD8L6y.problem: Sampled-token on-policy distillation is unreliable in cross-origin teacher-student settings because the advantage looks only at the sampled token's teacher-student probability ratio.
W8ySWD8L6y.method: NC-OPD reconstructs the sampled-token advantage through pairwise comparisons within a lightweight neighborhood of tokens ranked above the sampled token by the teacher or below it by the student, keeping the sampled-token policy-gradient interface.
W8ySWD8L6y.key_idea: Anchor-relative advantage from pairwise contrasts with teacher-preferred and student-disfavored neighbor tokens exposes relative-preference direction that a sampled-token ratio or summed reverse-KL hides.
W8ySWD8L6y.evidence: Two main transfer settings plus code generation and multi-teacher experiments, with results on AMC, AIME 24 and AIME 25 against sampled-token OPD and distribution-alignment baselines.
W8ySWD8L6y.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the tunnel-vision failure mode is clearly motivated, the objective is simple, and NC-OPD consistently beats sampled-token OPD and distribution-alignment baselines.
W8ySWD8L6y.main_concern: Novelty is questioned as close to logit distillation, component analysis of the gains is thin, and the evaluated algorithm is not uniquely specified between the main text and appendix.

dc9YUzX2GK.one_liner: Neural fields from overlapping adaptive local polynomials decoded by a small MLP, with hp-approximation rates for values and derivatives.
dc9YUzX2GK.problem: MLP-only neural fields scale poorly to large scientific signals, and hybrid MLP plus hash-grid methods show artifacts under differentiation.
dc9YUzX2GK.method: LBNFs place overlapping local polynomial functions adaptively across the domain and decode their features with a lightweight MLP, so polynomial degree and placement density independently control model complexity and its allocation.
dc9YUzX2GK.key_idea: A partition-of-unity of local polynomials gives explicit, independent control of degree and density, inheriting classical convergence rates for values and derivatives.
dc9YUzX2GK.evidence: Analytic benchmarks checking hp-approximation rates and large scientific signals such as astronomical simulations and turbulent flows, compared with SIREN and hash-grid hybrids.
dc9YUzX2GK.claimed_gains: For smooth targets, O(h^(p+1)) convergence in value and O(h^(p+1-nu)) for derivatives of order nu <= p; empirical results are cut off in the abstract.
dc9YUzX2GK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper is clear and technically sound, linking classical polynomial approximation theory to scalable, derivative-accurate neural fields.
dc9YUzX2GK.main_concern: Positioning against closely related work is weak (a prior polynomial-basis neural field and a hybrid-grid derivative-aware method), and the choice of polynomials over tiny MLPs is not experimentally justified.

qNhb4oDXxT.one_liner: Four-stage training for few-step reference-video visual effect transfer: adaptive reference modulation, multi-source guidance, then distribution matching distillation.
qNhb4oDXxT.problem: Reference videos entangle the intended effect with reference-specific content, so effect transfer must capture the change evidence while adapting its influence to the target.
qNhb4oDXxT.method: Reveris trains an image-to-video backbone through reference adaptation, modulation calibration, multi-source classifier-free guidance and few-step distillation via distribution matching into a four-step generator, combining clean-reference temporal variation with caption-conditioned content matching and target-conditioned modulation.
qNhb4oDXxT.key_idea: Target-conditioned modulation scales the influence of reference temporal-variation evidence, and multi-source classifier-free guidance is distilled by distribution matching into a four-step generator.
qNhb4oDXxT.evidence: Automated evaluation, ablations and an external dataset, on a curated dataset of 49,194 videos spanning 350 effect types in 13 families.
qNhb4oDXxT.claimed_gains: Consistent improvements in effect fidelity, source preservation and visual quality; no numbers stated.
qNhb4oDXxT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is practically useful and the method transfers effects with substantially faster generation, supported by comparisons, ablations and external-dataset evaluation.
qNhb4oDXxT.main_concern: Novelty is limited because the framework combines existing techniques, and human evaluation and controlled tests of adaptive modulation against generic reference-strength modulation are missing.

HuZlayXcZn.one_liner: Decision-Transformer-style policy trained with actor-critic and context-truncated lambda-return critics instead of behavior cloning, for offline-to-online RL.
HuZlayXcZn.problem: Decision-Transformer-style models trained with behavior cloning stay tied to dataset actions and lack explicit policy improvement.
HuZlayXcZn.method: AC/DT optimizes a sequence-conditioned stochastic Transformer policy with twin Markovian critics trained position-wise on context-truncated lambda-returns, with conservative value regularization offline and restricted to offline experience during online fine-tuning.
HuZlayXcZn.key_idea: Replace the likelihood loss of a Decision Transformer with value-based actor-critic updates, using position-wise multi-step lambda-return targets from lightweight Markovian critics.
HuZlayXcZn.evidence: D4RL benchmarks with 5 seeds and IQM aggregation, ablations of actor and critic architectures, multi-step targets and conservative regularization, and a state-matched distributional analysis of action marginals.
HuZlayXcZn.claimed_gains: Competitive with action-likelihood Transformer baselines such as ODT, hybrid variants like ODT+TD3 and other O2O methods on D4RL; no numbers in the abstract.
HuZlayXcZn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that replacing behavior cloning with actor-critic in a DT-style policy is simple and well motivated, with strong D4RL results over Transformer baselines and candid ablations.
HuZlayXcZn.main_concern: Gains may come from the multi-step critic rather than the Transformer design, ablations do not isolate removing behavior cloning, and novelty over prior value-guided Transformer methods is limited.

69Vz1tbMkI.one_liner: Reweights GRPO token credit by aligning frozen reward-model gradients, mapped to logit space, with each token's update direction.
69Vz1tbMkI.problem: GRPO shares one response-level advantage across all tokens, so its updates do not always point toward higher reward at the token level.
69Vz1tbMkI.method: DATC maps frozen reward-model gradients into policy logit space and assigns token weights by how well the reward direction aligns with GRPO's signed sampled-action update direction, preserving the sign and mean of the response-level advantage.
69Vz1tbMkI.key_idea: A work-based view of credit: a token's weight is the reward change along the policy update direction, computed from reward-model gradients projected into logit space.
69Vz1tbMkI.evidence: Four settings across two model families, mainly against vanilla GRPO, with P2T and RED compared only in an ablation on Qwen3-14B-Base.
69Vz1tbMkI.claimed_gains: DATC outperforms GRPO in all four settings across two model families; no numeric gains stated.
69Vz1tbMkI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree credit assignment under sparse reward is an important question and the formulation is interesting and clean, with strong results and interpretable token weights.
69Vz1tbMkI.main_concern: Baseline coverage is limited (main experiments compare only with vanilla GRPO), and DATC needs differentiable reward-model gradients in a shared tokenization, making the comparison with zeroth-order GRPO unfair.

TGFT9c6e8W.one_liner: Distills image-expert supervision into video diffusion with a learnable linear latent connector and motion-preserving constraints.
TGFT9c6e8W.problem: Image experts are cheap to query but lack motion supervision and live in latent spaces different from video models, so frame-level gains can harm temporal consistency.
TGFT9c6e8W.method: MILD aligns student latent states and predicted updates with image experts through a learnable linear connector, constrains image-guided corrections around the pretrained student's predictions, and adds an optical-flow-based motion reward.
TGFT9c6e8W.key_idea: A linear connector maps video latents into the image expert's space for on-policy supervision, with corrections constrained near the student's own prediction to keep motion.
TGFT9c6e8W.evidence: Wan2.1-1.3B, Wan2.2-5B and LTX-Video-2B with image experts for aesthetics, composition and OCR, against video-to-video on-policy distillation baselines.
TGFT9c6e8W.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that using specialized image experts instead of costly video teachers is practical and well motivated, with consistent gains across several video backbones.
TGFT9c6e8W.main_concern: The benefit of cross-modal distillation is not isolated from simpler baselines or from combining multiple specialized experts, and the connector's noise-compatibility assumption lacks direct validation.

l3PDajTr20.one_liner: Two coupled generators produce context-dependent low-rank updates for the vision-language and action modules of a VLA policy.
l3PDajTr20.problem: A single static fine-tuning update fits a mixture of operations with competing parameter adjustments, leaving individual operations insufficiently adapted.
l3PDajTr20.method: MorphAct trains a vision-language generator and an action generator jointly through the native action objective, with action-side parameter generation conditioned on the adapted vision-language representation, without operation labels or expert-adapter targets.
l3PDajTr20.key_idea: Share an adaptation rule that generates context-dependent low-rank updates, with action-side generation conditioned on the vision-language side.
l3PDajTr20.evidence: Three VLA backbones on LIBERO and Meta-World, real-world tests against pi0, and atomic-task diagnostics of competing update directions on RoboCasa.
l3PDajTr20.claimed_gains: Improves average success rates across three VLA backbones on LIBERO and Meta-World by up to 15.13%, and by up to 17% over pi0 in real-world evaluation.
l3PDajTr20.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the coupling of representation and action adaptation is coherent, evaluation is broad across three backbones and benchmarks, and results are consistent.
l3PDajTr20.main_concern: The diagnostics do not establish within-task, stage-dependent update conflicts (cosine near 1e-3, no confidence intervals), and no direct comparison with other VLA parameter-generation methods such as Hyper-LoRA is given.

4hfCnOAavd.one_liner: Physics-inspired RGB-thermal Gaussian splatting with a transmission network using RGB depth and a conduction network using RGB edges.
4hfCnOAavd.problem: Prior RGB-T reconstruction either degrades RGB quality or ignores cross-modal physical relationships, causing artifacts in distant regions and near object boundaries.
4hfCnOAavd.method: A Light Transmission Network uses RGB depth consistency to improve thermal transmission distance estimation, and a Thermal Conduction Network uses RGB edge consistency to reduce thermal boundary blurring, inside a 3DGS reconstruction.
4hfCnOAavd.key_idea: Learned networks modeled on atmospheric attenuation and heat diffusion condition thermal rendering on RGB depth and edge consistency.
4hfCnOAavd.evidence: 11 RGBT-Scenes test scenes and 22 ThermoScenes scenes against ThermalGaussian and other methods, with a comparison of explicit consistency losses versus network conditioning.
4hfCnOAavd.claimed_gains: Improves thermal PSNR over ThermalGaussian by 3.72 dB on average while keeping RGB quality comparable to or surpassing prior methods.
4hfCnOAavd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is well motivated by specific RGB-T limitations and delivers consistent thermal reconstruction gains without large RGB quality loss.
4hfCnOAavd.main_concern: It is unclear whether gains come from the physics-inspired design or added network capacity, the physical interpretation is not identifiable, and Thermal3D-GS and other related methods are not discussed.

aD7X1oBLBz.one_liner: Actor-critic for multi-turn LLM agents using turn-level distributional critics to rank candidate turns by mean return plus deviation bonus.
aD7X1oBLBz.problem: Stochastic generation does not guarantee effective environment exploration in agentic RL, with repeated trajectories and limited state coverage alongside weak credit assignment.
aD7X1oBLBz.method: DCGPO learns a turn-level categorical distributional critic that supports turn-level advantage estimation and provides action-conditioned return mean and dispersion, then ranks policy-generated candidate turns before execution to direct training-time interactions.
aD7X1oBLBz.key_idea: Rank sampled candidate turns by predicted return mean plus a standard-deviation bonus from a categorical distributional critic, steering training-time environment interaction.
aD7X1oBLBz.evidence: Embodied and web-based interactive tasks (including ALFWorld and WebShop) across multiple model scales, with component ablations, visitation analyses and a fixed-policy error-bound analysis.
aD7X1oBLBz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method unifies credit assignment and exploration, adds no inference overhead, and outperforms competitive baselines in carefully run experiments.
aD7X1oBLBz.main_concern: Ablations do not show that the distributional critic or dispersion bonus drives the gains (WebShop success 77.60 vs 77.87, within seed variance), and the exploration advantage lacks a matched-compute comparison.

ShMtO50MjO.one_liner: Clusters evaluation instances by candidates' behavioral responses online and evaluates only representative instances in LLM-assisted evolutionary algorithm design.
ShMtO50MjO.problem: Evaluating each generated algorithm on all training instances is the computational bottleneck of LLM-assisted evolutionary search, and many instances are redundant.
ShMtO50MjO.method: B-DICS builds a behavior matrix from evaluations the search already performs, clusters instances in behavior space, and selects core instances; B-DICS-LES co-evolves algorithms and instance structure so new algorithms sharpen the clustering.
ShMtO50MjO.key_idea: Represent instances by how candidate algorithms behave on them and evaluate only representative instances chosen from clusters in this evolving behavior space.
ShMtO50MjO.evidence: Three algorithm design tasks with independent search runs, component ablations, ranking-fidelity analysis and additional public benchmarks.
ShMtO50MjO.claimed_gains: Reduces evaluation cost by an average of 29.8% without sacrificing performance on three algorithm design tasks.
ShMtO50MjO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree evaluation cost is a practical bottleneck and that feature-free, behavior-based instance structure is a useful way to cut it, with ablations and ranking-fidelity analysis.
ShMtO50MjO.main_concern: Differentiation from concurrent behavior-based clustering work (DvCA/DyCA) is unclear without a direct comparison, and the core-instance selection rule is under-specified.

RRqtS1rFKl.one_liner: Image-to-video human animation that reconciles pose and appearance conditions to preserve the first frame, trained in staged decoupled objectives.
RRqtS1rFKl.problem: The dominant Reference-to-Video paradigm's image-to-motion binding ignores spatio-temporal misalignments, causing identity drift and visual artifacts.
RRqtS1rFKl.method: SteadyDancer uses a Condition-Reconciliation Mechanism to harmonize conflicting conditions, Synergistic Pose Modulation Modules for an adaptive pose representation compatible with the reference image, and a Staged Decoupled-Objective Training Pipeline that optimizes motion fidelity, visual quality and temporal coherence.
RRqtS1rFKl.key_idea: Use an image-to-video backbone so the first frame is preserved, and reconcile the pose-control and fidelity conditions that conflict.
RRqtS1rFKl.evidence: Experiments on existing benchmarks and the proposed X-Dance cross-source benchmark, with ablations.
RRqtS1rFKl.claimed_gains: Better appearance fidelity and motion control than compared methods while requiring significantly fewer training resources; no numbers in the abstract.
RRqtS1rFKl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the spatio-temporal misalignment problem is real and well motivated, and that the I2V approach gives strong qualitative results with fewer training resources.
RRqtS1rFKl.main_concern: Evidence for individual components is weak (marginal ablation differences) and pose-control accuracy is not measured quantitatively (e.g., PCK).

mTLAJN9VpV.one_liner: Benchmark of phone-use agent misuse on 11 social media apps, and VEIL attack that edits agent observations to launder intent.
mTLAJN9VpV.problem: Phone-use agents could cheaply automate social media abuse functions such as reporting, but existing benchmarks use mock apps and cover few real abuse scenarios.
mTLAJN9VpV.method: BadPhoneAgent provides a high-fidelity environment of 11 apps and 18 abuse-relevant functions with 150 manually built test cases, and VEIL exploits the gap between the model's observation and the true phone state by editing the view it receives.
mTLAJN9VpV.key_idea: VEIL launders harmful intent by editing the view the agent observes, so its safety judgment differs from the actual phone state it acts on.
mTLAJN9VpV.evidence: 150 test cases in 8 categories and 35 subcategories, a physical-phone replay reproducing outcomes (91.5% agreement), and attacks on frontier models plus two off-the-shelf defenses.
mTLAJN9VpV.claimed_gains: VEIL reaches attack success rates of 88% on GPT-6-Astra and 64.7% on Claude Fable 5, while these models refuse only 8.0% and 1.3% of requests, respectively.
mTLAJN9VpV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the risk is timely, the benchmark is solid and validated on real devices, and the observation-action gap is a clean attack surface.
mTLAJN9VpV.main_concern: VEIL's novelty over compositional task-decomposition jailbreaks is not distinguished, and it assumes the attacker can modify inputs while offering little defense exploration.

IGmM2Do74x.one_liner: Memory ranker that iteratively adds the top memory to the query cue and stops via a learned sufficiency predictor.
IGmM2Do74x.problem: Single-pass memory rankers score each candidate once against the raw query and cut at a fixed top-K, missing memories that look unrelated to the query and ignoring how many memories a query needs.
IGmM2Do74x.method: ReMind runs a recurrent loop: each step appends the top-ranked memory to the query context and reranks the remaining candidates under the expanded cue. A sufficiency predictor estimates whether the collected memories can answer the query and ends the loop, so the number of selected memories adapts per query.
IGmM2Do74x.key_idea: Compound cueing (add each selected memory to the query, then rerank the rest) plus a sufficiency predictor that terminates selection per query.
IGmM2Do74x.evidence: Per reviews, experiments span multiple memory benchmarks (including PersonaBench) and three retrievers with all rankers given the same frozen top-50 candidates, plus ablations and a QA test of adaptive stopping; the abstract is cut off before results.
IGmM2Do74x.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the motivation clear and the design intuitive, with evidence across several benchmarks and retrievers that conditioning selection on earlier picks and stopping adaptively helps.
IGmM2Do74x.main_concern: The methodological novelty over existing sequential evidence selection with adaptive termination is limited, and the gains are hard to attribute to recurrent selection rather than richer training supervision.

jJ7ZiV00I4.one_liner: Shows spectrum-only constraints match direction-constrained continual learning; SPAR sets LoRA rank per task from probed update spectral capacity.
jJ7ZiV00I4.problem: Subspace-based continual learning methods impose opposing directional constraints (isolating versus sharing subspaces) yet show similar update-spectrum patterns, leaving unclear whether the direction constraint itself matters.
jJ7ZiV00I4.method: The authors replace each method's directional constraint with a training-time constraint that matches the recorded update spectrum while leaving directions free. They then propose SPAR, which uses a few probing updates to estimate each task's demand for spectral capacity (spectral energy and effective rank) and allocates its LoRA rank accordingly.
jJ7ZiV00I4.key_idea: Control only update spectral capacity (spectral energy and effective rank) by scheduling LoRA rank per task from a probe of its demand, with no directional constraints.
jJ7ZiV00I4.evidence: Spectrum-replay interventions against existing subspace-based continual learning methods, plus comparisons on diverse benchmarks; specific datasets are not named in the abstract.
jJ7ZiV00I4.claimed_gains: No numbers stated; the abstract says the spectrum-only intervention matches or surpasses the original methods and SPAR is competitive or superior.
jJ7ZiV00I4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers like the spectrum-replay finding that dropping directional constraints recovers accuracy, and see SPAR as a simple, actionable replacement for stored subspaces.
jJ7ZiV00I4.main_concern: Novelty is limited against adaptive-rank LoRA methods (AdaLoRA, SoRA, AutoLoRA) and prior work separating spectrum from direction, and demand-aware allocation is not compared with a fixed-decay LoRA.

BWw1mzIisX.one_liner: Routes short-video fake news samples by conformal uncertainty to adaptive-depth reasoning over progressive claim-evidence graphs.
BWw1mzIisX.problem: Existing detectors apply a fixed reasoning depth to every sample, under-verifying claims that need external evidence and subjecting reliable predictions to costly, potentially harmful slow deliberation.
BWw1mzIisX.method: A lightweight multimodal fast system gives an initial veracity estimate, and a controller using label-conditional conformal prediction sends uncertain samples to slow deliberation, with trajectory-level calibration deciding when to stop. Slow reasoning builds a sample-specific graph of claim-evidence units with support, refute, and unresolved relations, aggregated by relation-aware graph attention and a reliability-gated residual that revises the initial estimate.
BWw1mzIisX.key_idea: Label-conditional conformal prediction decides which samples get slow evidence reasoning, and a reliability-gated residual over a progressive relational evidence graph revises, not replaces, the fast estimate.
BWw1mzIisX.evidence: The abstract describes a newly built large-scale dataset (SV-CoRE, cut off in the text); reviews mention FakeTT, analyses of how often evidence corrects or introduces errors, and fewer LLM calls.
BWw1mzIisX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the focus on deciding when extra evidence is useful, praising conformal routing as a statistically grounded alternative to heuristic confidence thresholds and the analysis of corrected versus introduced errors.
BWw1mzIisX.main_concern: The statistical guarantee of the full routing-and-stopping pipeline is unclear, and errors from upstream LVLM or LLM claim extraction can propagate into the evidence graph without any check.

toBKhiSBSp.one_liner: Training-free patch-correspondence similarity of intermediate diffusion features reveals concept-level geometry across pretrained diffusion models.
toBKhiSBSp.problem: It is hard to probe how pretrained diffusion models organize relationships among visual concepts, because intermediate representations of related concepts differ in spatial configuration.
toBKhiSBSp.method: SIS builds patch-wise feature correspondences between intermediate diffusion representations and keeps the spatial evidence behind each similarity score. TSIS aggregates these correspondences across generations to expose concept-level relational structure, including color, material, and viewpoint across blocks and timesteps.
toBKhiSBSp.key_idea: Compare intermediate diffusion features through patch-wise spatial correspondences that preserve where similarity comes from, then aggregate across generations to obtain concept geometry.
toBKhiSBSp.evidence: Analyses across diverse pretrained diffusion models (13 per reviews, both U-Net and transformer), object categories, attribute factors over blocks and timesteps, and a rarity comparison of final images.
toBKhiSBSp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate that SIS keeps spatial contributions so scores can be traced to image regions, the broad evaluation across 13 models, and the link between intermediate geometry and final image rarity.
toBKhiSBSp.main_concern: The global-mean-pooling comparison changes both spatial matching and attention weighting, so the benefit of correspondence is not isolated, and the presentation is hard to follow.

Dix8xa7Mvt.one_liner: Multi-view clustering with residual encoder stages and gated cross-view transformer consensus passed to the next stage.
Dix8xa7Mvt.problem: Stacked nonlinear view-specific encoders in deep multi-view clustering can degrade useful features learned at earlier layers.
Dix8xa7Mvt.method: Each stage has a residual connection carrying the projected input plus a nonlinear branch learning an incremental update. A cross-view transformer estimates level-wise consensus across views of the same instance, which is projected into the next stage and injected through a feature-wise gate; training uses reconstruction, inter-view feature contrast, and inter-level assignment contrast.
Dix8xa7Mvt.key_idea: Residual encoding at each level plus level-wise cross-view transformer consensus fed into the following stage through feature-wise gates.
Dix8xa7Mvt.evidence: Experiments on benchmark datasets, with analyses showing residual connections reduce degradation as depth grows and gated guidance beats direct consensus integration.
Dix8xa7Mvt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the hierarchical residual design with cross-view guidance well motivated, with informative ablations and strong results on several benchmarks.
Dix8xa7Mvt.main_concern: Novelty is questioned because the method combines existing components, and most results come from a fixed random seed.

Z6jfaWEp5p.one_liner: Query-time grounding in aerial 3D Gaussian scenes by actively choosing views and refining Gaussian-level target posteriors.
Z6jfaWEp5p.problem: Grounding language queries in large aerial 3D scenes requires separating visually similar structures and recovering complete 3D support despite large viewpoint changes and incomplete observations.
Z6jfaWEp5p.method: AQVE maintains competing cross-view target hypotheses, accumulates visibility-aware positive and negative evidence, and selects informative views. ESR fuses reliable foreground and background observations into Gaussian-level target posteriors and combines them with local geometric consistency to recover missing support and suppress foreground leakage; it runs on standard 3D Gaussian Splatting.
Z6jfaWEp5p.key_idea: Hypothesis-driven active view selection to disambiguate targets, then Gaussian-level posterior fusion with geometric consistency to complete the target region.
Z6jfaWEp5p.evidence: Experiments on the new AeroRef3D benchmark (six aerial scenes, spatial-attribute, commonsense, functional, and hypothetical queries with zero-to-many targets) and two aerial open-vocabulary segmentation benchmarks.
Z6jfaWEp5p.claimed_gains: No numbers stated; the abstract says it substantially outperforms the evaluated baselines on AeroRef3D and is competitive on two aerial open-vocabulary segmentation benchmarks.
Z6jfaWEp5p.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the split between AQVE (disambiguation) and ESR (spatial extent) well motivated and supported by ablations, and value AeroRef3D for going beyond category-level segmentation.
Z6jfaWEp5p.main_concern: It is unclear how much of the gain comes from AQVE and ESR rather than the stronger MLLM plus SAM 3 pipeline, since baselines do not share the same backbone or masks.

6K2K5cAxlD.one_liner: Benchmark organizing egocentric audio-visual QA by Ego-Action-World interaction structures: Node, Edge, Chain, and Loop.
6K2K5cAxlD.problem: Egocentric video benchmarks study perception, goals, actions, and feedback in isolation although they are coupled in a closed interaction loop.
6K2K5cAxlD.method: The paper defines four interaction structures (Node, Edge, Chain, Loop) and an interaction-first, evidence-grounded pipeline that extracts structured interactions from egocentric video, grounds them in visual and auditory evidence, and generates questions per structure, with required modality and dialogue form following from the interaction.
6K2K5cAxlD.key_idea: Generate questions from extracted Ego-Action-World interaction structures grounded in audio-visual evidence, so modality and dialogue form follow from the interaction rather than separate task families.
6K2K5cAxlD.evidence: Per reviews, in-domain and cross-benchmark experiments plus training results showing gains on the new benchmark; the abstract is cut off before results.
6K2K5cAxlD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the Node/Edge/Chain/Loop taxonomy, the evidence-grounded construction with provenance, and the training gains on the benchmark.
6K2K5cAxlD.main_concern: Data correctness is validated mainly by LLMs with no reported human-review numbers, and composed or feedback reasoning is not directly tested against shortcut baselines.

jzXBCbeI63.one_liner: Adds a lightweight projective sparse residual branch to a frozen 3D foundation model to use known camera calibration.
jzXBCbeI63.problem: Calibration-aware feed-forward 3D models do not guarantee that predicted depth back-projects to geometry consistent with the provided camera intrinsics and extrinsics.
jzXBCbeI63.method: CalibAdapter attaches a projective sparse residual branch to a selected cross-view interaction block while keeping all pretrained parameters frozen. The mismatch is measured with a new Calibrated Pointmap Error (CPE) that gives pixel-corresponded metric 3D error.
jzXBCbeI63.key_idea: A projective sparse residual branch inserted into one cross-view interaction block injects camera calibration while all pretrained weights stay frozen.
jzXBCbeI63.evidence: Tested on four backbones (VGGT-Ω, VGGT, DA3, π³) and held-out benchmarks; reviews also cite autonomous driving and real-world robotic manipulation experiments and controls against parameter-matched adapters.
jzXBCbeI63.claimed_gains: Average relative CPE reduction of 28.3% across VGGT-Ω, VGGT, DA3, and π³, together with overall improvements in conventional reconstruction metrics.
jzXBCbeI63.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers see a practical, small adapter that exploits free calibration across four backbones, with sensible controls such as parameter-matched adapters and shuffled-camera inputs.
jzXBCbeI63.main_concern: Baselines are incomplete (no training-free scale-alignment, LoRA, or fine-tuning comparison) and the architectural novelty is seen as incremental.

e7mxvL0i2r.one_liner: Distills user logs into rules, scores a cognitive gap against model knowledge, and routes data to adapter or critique loop.
e7mxvL0i2r.problem: Learning from user interaction logs is hard because logs are unstructured and noisy, LLMs struggle to separate useful feedback from noise, and logs are collected off-policy relative to model optimization.
e7mxvL0i2r.method: UNO distills logs into semi-structured rules and preference pairs, clusters them by query and feedback to handle heterogeneity, and quantifies the cognitive gap between the model's prior knowledge and the log data. The gap filters noisy feedback and sends data to either a generation adapter or a reflective critique loop.
e7mxvL0i2r.key_idea: A cognitive-gap score between model prior knowledge and rules distilled from logs filters noise and routes data to a generation adapter or a reflective critique module.
e7mxvL0i2r.evidence: The abstract says extensive experiments were run but is cut off; reviews cite comparisons against a broad set of baselines on MemoryBench and WildFB with component ablations.
e7mxvL0i2r.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem important and the design (rule distillation, gap-based routing between improving generation and critiquing outputs) reasonable and supported by comprehensive experiments and ablations.
e7mxvL0i2r.main_concern: Rule extraction depends on the base LLM and its quality is not reliably controlled, yet the rules drive both clustering and cognitive-gap estimation.

yQmt4fbGDM.one_liner: Scores query-identity pairs from the empirical distribution of historical matching responses for open-vocabulary multi-object tracking association.
yQmt4fbGDM.problem: In open-vocabulary tracking, prototypes or pooled similarities compress appearance history and obscure how past observations support the current query.
yQmt4fbGDM.method: Each query-identity pair is represented by the empirical distribution of its historical matching responses; recent and long-term evidence are combined by a candidate-specific temporal gate and a candidate-relative scorer. A moment-generating formulation gives a compact second-order parameterization without explicit covariance, as a lightweight frame-causal layer on frozen visual frontends trained with Base identity supervision only.
yQmt4fbGDM.key_idea: Model identity history as a distribution of matching responses, summarized by a moment-generating second-order descriptor and fused by a candidate-specific temporal gate.
yQmt4fbGDM.evidence: Evaluated on TAO validation and test; reviews cite ablations against a capacity-matched MLP and fixed temporal fusion, and a frontend-generalization table.
yQmt4fbGDM.claimed_gains: Reaches 43.3 Novel AssocA on TAO validation and 33.6 on test.
yQmt4fbGDM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the diagnosis convincing (the correct identity usually stays in the candidate pool but is ranked below first) and the controls against a capacity-matched MLP and fixed fusion persuasive.
yQmt4fbGDM.main_concern: Methodological novelty is limited and the moment-generating descriptor is only a combination of mean and variance, so its link to the gains is not established.

OqQi651YHl.one_liner: Tightens the certified l1 radius for Bernoulli-smoothed rate-encoded SNNs from exponential to linear decay in latency and adds SEA-PGD attack.
OqQi651YHl.problem: The certified l1 radius for rate-encoded SNNs under Bernoulli smoothing shrinks exponentially with latency T, despite experimental evidence of robustness.
OqQi651YHl.method: The authors prove an improved guarantee under the same setting, extend the proof to signed rate encoding, and improve the l0-norm-bounded sparse encoding attack (SEA) into SEA-PGD.
OqQi651YHl.key_idea: Re-derive the Bernoulli-smoothing bound for rate-encoded SNNs so the certified l1 radius shrinks as 1/(T+1) instead of exponentially in latency T.
OqQi651YHl.evidence: A proof for rate encoding and signed rate encoding, plus attack experiments on three standard datasets (CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, SVHN per reviews) and encoding techniques.
OqQi651YHl.claimed_gains: Certified radius decays only linearly with latency, (p_a - p_b)/(2(T+1)), instead of exponentially, (p_a - p_b)/(2T3^(T-1)); SEA-PGD consistently outperforms SEA across three standard datasets and encoding techniques.
OqQi651YHl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit a solid theoretical analysis that narrows the gap between certified and empirical robustness, and see SEA-PGD as a stronger, realistic spike-flipping attack.
OqQi651YHl.main_concern: The theoretical gain relies on Bernoulli randomized smoothing rather than SNN-specific dynamics, and the framework is restricted to rate encoding.

r4Kz9ZLe05.one_liner: Query-conditioned hypergraph neural network retrieves documents, and gradient attribution decodes explicit hyper-paths for LLM multi-hop reasoning.
r4Kz9ZLe05.problem: Existing hypergraph retrievers rely on predefined structural expansion or diffusion, missing query-dependent interactions, and leave connections among retrieved evidence implicit for the LLM to reconstruct.
r4Kz9ZLe05.method: Each document is a hyperedge over its extracted entities, with shared entities linking hyperedges; HyperGNN message passing with joint document and entity supervision learns query-dependent interactions to retrieve complementary evidence. GGHD then uses gradient attribution to turn the learned interactions into explicit hyper-paths given to the LLM.
r4Kz9ZLe05.key_idea: Learn query-dependent message passing on a document-entity hypergraph, then convert gradient attribution of the learned interactions into explicit hyper-paths for the LLM.
r4Kz9ZLe05.evidence: The abstract is cut off at 'Experiments on six'; reviews cite three multi-hop benchmarks, retrieval recall and QA accuracy gains over HGRAG, and tests with different embedding models.
r4Kz9ZLe05.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem important and report consistent gains in retrieval recall and downstream QA accuracy over HGRAG, with explicit hyper-paths addressing implicit evidence composition.
r4Kz9ZLe05.main_concern: The HyperGNN retriever is seen as methodologically limited relative to existing hypergraph and learned graph retrieval methods such as HGRAG, GFM-RAG, and HyperRAG.

2hnMITiNob.one_liner: Derives timestep schedules for diffusion and flow samplers by minimizing a surrogate of generation error weighted by error propagators.
2hnMITiNob.problem: Common timestep schedules (time-uniform, logSNR-uniform) rely on unrealistic assumptions of locally stationary score errors, slowly varying noise levels, and uniform error propagation along the trajectory.
2hnMITiNob.method: EP-Flow models the sampler as a discrete-time dynamical system and derives a surrogate splitting total error into a persistent directional bias from score error, residual variance from step-local stochastic error, and local truncation error, each weighted by trajectory-dependent propagators. The objective can improve heuristic schedules or refine already-learned ones.
2hnMITiNob.key_idea: Weight each step's score bias, stochastic variance, and truncation error by how much it propagates to the final sample, and optimize the schedule against that surrogate.
2hnMITiNob.evidence: Four datasets (CIFAR-10, FFHQ, AFHQv2, ImageNet-64), EDM2 training recipes, learned schedules in Stable Diffusion v1.5, and text-to-image generation with FLUX.1-dev.
2hnMITiNob.claimed_gains: No numeric gains stated; the abstract says EP-Flow improves few-step generation over the Karras schedule on CIFAR-10, FFHQ, AFHQv2, and ImageNet-64.
2hnMITiNob.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers like the propagation-aware viewpoint and the broad evaluation across model families and solvers, with low-NFE gains and no retraining or added inference cost.
2hnMITiNob.main_concern: The surrogate stacks several approximations (for example scalar trace quantities replacing matrix propagators), and comparisons omit recent schedule-optimization and learned-solver baselines.

RBoG5kVQXp.one_liner: Compresses the KV cache by refining per-head token importance with cross-head consensus, then selecting tokens for semantic coverage.
RBoG5kVQXp.problem: Head-specific importance from observation-window attention gives partial views of token importance, and picking highly attended tokens omits other crucial information under tight cache budgets.
RBoG5kVQXp.method: A soft cross-head consensus mechanism uses collective signals to refine head-specific attention while preserving head distinctiveness. On the calibrated scores, a cross-token completeness selection strategy promotes broader semantic coverage.
RBoG5kVQXp.key_idea: Calibrate each head's attention importance with soft cross-head consensus, then select tokens with a completeness criterion that trades importance against coverage.
RBoG5kVQXp.evidence: Needle-in-a-Haystack and 16 LongBench datasets on three LLMs.
RBoG5kVQXp.claimed_gains: No numbers stated; the abstract says CoCoKV outperforms competitive baselines on Needle-in-a-Haystack and 16 LongBench datasets across three LLMs.
RBoG5kVQXp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the motivation clear and the method easy to follow, with improvements across three models and 16 LongBench datasets.
RBoG5kVQXp.main_concern: Evaluation appears limited to the query-aware setting, and a direct comparison with MixKV, which also combines importance and diversity, is missing.

NkJf006rpD.one_liner: Treats each reverse-diffusion step as a maximum-entropy RL decision, giving local objectives that backpropagate through one denoising step.
NkJf006rpD.problem: Applying maximum-entropy RL to diffusion policies must handle the whole reverse-diffusion chain, although only the final denoised action is executed in the environment.
NkJf006rpD.method: DA-MDPs augment policy and target trajectories with intermediate diffusion variables and derive a reverse-KL upper bound, via the data-processing inequality, that decomposes across denoising transitions. This yields diffusion-augmented soft rewards, value functions, and local policy objectives, instantiated with PPO, REPPO, and a maximum-entropy extension of WPO.
NkJf006rpD.key_idea: Augment trajectories with intermediate diffusion variables so a reverse-KL upper bound decomposes per denoising transition, enabling local maximum-entropy RL updates.
NkJf006rpD.evidence: Continuous-control experiments (MuJoCo Playground per reviews), StackCube and PushT manipulation tasks, and a memory study with additional diffusion steps; the abstract is cut off.
NkJf006rpD.claimed_gains: No numbers stated; the abstract reports improved continuous-control performance, benefits from additional diffusion steps, and memory-efficient training.
NkJf006rpD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers see a principled, general framework with clean derivations and improvements across all three instantiations (PPO, REPPO, WPO).
NkJf006rpD.main_concern: The contribution is seen as limited because the variational formulation comes from DIME and local objectives are explored elsewhere, with few comparisons to competitive diffusion maximum-entropy RL baselines.

Fprv3ftIzX.one_liner: Character video generation with large-angle camera control via back-projected point-cloud guidance and geometry-aligned multi-view memory attention.
Fprv3ftIzX.problem: Existing methods struggle with large-angle camera trajectories, and viewpoint changes that reveal unseen character regions cause geometric distortion, appearance degradation, and identity drift.
Fprv3ftIzX.method: The initial view is back-projected into a 3D point cloud and rendered along the target trajectory to give geometric guidance and coverage masks. Geometry-Aligned Memory Attention (GAMA) aligns multi-view anchor geometry with target-view geometry in a shared frame to retrieve and inject view-relevant character features; the authors also build the CLACT dataset and benchmark.
Fprv3ftIzX.key_idea: Render trajectory-aligned point-cloud guidance from the first frame and retrieve missing character appearance from multi-view anchors through geometry-aligned memory attention.
Fprv3ftIzX.evidence: CLACT contains 80,000 synthetic training samples and 42 synthetic and real-world evaluation scenes; the abstract is cut off before results, and reviews cite component ablations.
Fprv3ftIzX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers see an important problem and a sensible combination of trajectory-aligned geometric guidance with multi-view character memory, supported by component ablations.
Fprv3ftIzX.main_concern: Gains are hard to attribute, since WorldCast uses multiple reference views while some baselines use one, and GAMA's geometry alignment is not isolated from extra memory capacity.

nq1LibDQdF.one_liner: Action-conditioned bimanual world model that generates both wrist-camera views with per-arm action injection and sparse hub-token exchange.
nq1LibDQdF.problem: Existing interactive world models rely on text or single-camera control and struggle to follow each arm's actions while keeping the two wrist views consistent.
nq1LibDQdF.method: UMI-WM jointly generates both wrist views from observation history, per-arm relative camera poses, and gripper widths. Each arm's actions go into its own wrist stream while sparse hub tokens exchange scene information between streams, with camera-aware geometry conditioning and camera-guided noise; a 30-step Teacher is distilled into a Student with four denoising steps.
nq1LibDQdF.key_idea: Inject each arm's actions into its own wrist-view stream and exchange scene information between streams through sparse hub tokens, with camera-aware geometry conditioning.
nq1LibDQdF.evidence: Trained on self-collected open-world and in-studio UMI recordings plus public manipulation data, and evaluated with an inverse-dynamics-based Bimanual Action Fidelity (BAF) metric; the abstract is cut off before results.
nq1LibDQdF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the bimanual world-modeling formulation meaningful and report clear action following and efficient generation, with ablations tying the gain to the camera-aware design.
nq1LibDQdF.main_concern: Cross-view shared-scene consistency and action fidelity are not directly evaluated, since metrics are computed per wrist and BAF relies on an in-domain inverse dynamics model.

1rej8aLL5k.one_liner: Compile-execute-refine framework that externalizes runtime coordination from robot task programs and refines skill behavior or coordination via hypothesis tests.
1rej8aLL5k.problem: Contingencies alter runtime coordination among concurrently executing skills, and coordination embedded in task logic makes the refinement target ambiguous between skill behavior and coordination, forcing repeated recovery and validation.
1rej8aLL5k.method: At compile time RaP turns skill invocations into runtime-managed processes and adds conditional tests of hypotheses about skill behavior and coordination. At execution the runtime enforces coordination relations and records test outcomes, and refinement uses that evidence to revise skill behavior or coordination rules and distill validated repairs into reusable guidance.
1rej8aLL5k.key_idea: Make runtime coordination a persistent, separate refinement target and localize failures with hypothesis tests compiled into the task program.
1rej8aLL5k.evidence: Per reviews, evaluation on subtasks with contingency scenarios, ablations over coordination guidance, kernel variants, and hypotheses, and several reasoning-effort settings; the abstract is cut off before results.
1rej8aLL5k.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers see a meaningful problem and a sensible principle, treating coordination as an explicit repair target, with hypothesis-linked traces aiding diagnosis and knowledge retention.
1rej8aLL5k.main_concern: Ablations show coordination guidance alone recovers most of the gain (50.5% versus 53.3% for full RaP), so the added value of the runtime kernel and hypotheses is unclear.

K2M8VBBgdO.one_liner: Treats representational similarity as a function of RBF bandwidth scale, producing a multiscale similarity signal and aggregate scores from CKA.
K2M8VBBgdO.problem: Existing similarity measures characterize alignment at a single predefined scale, although local neighborhood structure and broader global organization capture different aspects of alignment.
K2M8VBBgdO.method: Motivated by the link between RBF kernels and heat diffusion, the RBF bandwidth serves as the scale parameter, and the multiscale similarity signal (MS-Signal) characterizes alignment across scales. Scalar scores are then derived by aggregating similarity across scales.
K2M8VBBgdO.key_idea: Sweep the RBF kernel bandwidth, motivated by heat diffusion, to express similarity as a function of scale, then aggregate across scales into a scalar score.
K2M8VBBgdO.evidence: Controlled synthetic perturbations at local, intermediate, and global scales, learned neural representations, and the ReSi benchmark spanning graph, vision, and language domains.
K2M8VBBgdO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers like the simple, intuitive multiscale perspective, which they report performs well on the ReSi benchmark across domains, and find the paper easy to follow.
K2M8VBBgdO.main_concern: Closely related multiscale and neighborhood-based similarity work is not positioned, and the single-scale RBF CKA baseline uses only one bandwidth, leaving the source of the gain unclear.

w6eDqMuDK8.one_liner: Restricts KV-cache construction to local temporal blocks while denoising still attends to history, reducing drift in causal long-video generation.
w6eDqMuDK8.problem: Error accumulation in causal video generation, which attending to history during KV cache construction may exacerbate even though the same context is needed for denoising.
w6eDqMuDK8.method: Local Forcing applies an attention-mask modification, consistently across teacher forcing, consistency distillation, self-rollout distillation, and inference, so frames are generated with historical context but encoded locally into the cache.
w6eDqMuDK8.key_idea: Generate with context, encode locally: mask attention so cache entries are written from the local temporal block only, while denoising still reads the full history.
w6eDqMuDK8.evidence: Evaluated across several training and inference pipelines including minute-level rollouts; reviews cite matched teacher-forcing experiments over three seeds, a locality ablation, and 240-second rollouts.
w6eDqMuDK8.claimed_gains: No numbers stated; the abstract says LF enables stable minute-level rollouts without attention-sink strategies, extra memory modules, or long-horizon distribution matching distillation, with consistent video-quality gains across evaluated methods.
w6eDqMuDK8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the idea clean and simple, separating history used for denoising from history used for cache encoding, with no added parameters or losses and encouraging results across pipelines.
w6eDqMuDK8.main_concern: Novelty is modest relative to existing sink-exclusion strategies, and the error-propagation explanation and cache-history ablations are less firmly established than the quality gains.

9KtcjE2y2l.one_liner: Iteratively adapts an AI-image detector on target images using predicted-synthetic pseudo-labels, trusted real replay, and stochastic exploration.
9KtcjE2y2l.problem: Detectors' forensic cues may fail on new generators, and initial synthetic predictions on difficult source distributions cover only part of the images from the same source.
9KtcjE2y2l.method: The framework repeatedly adapts on target images predicted as synthetic, with asymmetric supervision: predicted-synthetic images give source-specific signals while trusted real-image replay supplies real supervision without treating missed synthetic images as real. Stochastic exploration provisionally labels a small subset of the remaining target images as synthetic, with replay constraining noisy updates.
9KtcjE2y2l.key_idea: Self-train only on predicted-synthetic target images, anchor real supervision with trusted real replay, and randomly label a few remaining images synthetic to expand recall.
9KtcjE2y2l.evidence: Experiments across unseen generators and diverse synthesis paradigms; reviews indicate a DINOv3 ViT-L backbone with LoRA.
9KtcjE2y2l.claimed_gains: No numbers stated; the abstract says it outperforms recent methods by a substantial margin across unseen generators and diverse synthesis paradigms.
9KtcjE2y2l.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the observation that initial synthetic predictions seed same-source recovery useful and the asymmetric supervision design well motivated.
9KtcjE2y2l.main_concern: The components are common (pseudo-label self-training, replay, random exploration), and gains are not separated from backbone fine-tuning or from per-target adaptation that baselines lack.

M3oCmJtb7J.one_liner: Distills defect patterns and repair actions from high-resource-language bug fixes into a skill library retrieved to guide low-resource program repair.
M3oCmJtb7J.problem: LLM program repair is weaker for low-resource languages such as Rust than for high-resource ones such as Java, and fine-tuning or program translation adds adaptation cost or semantic inconsistencies.
M3oCmJtb7J.method: RepairChemist distills defect patterns and repair actions from bug-fix pairs in high-resource languages and groups the skills by statement type into a skill library. At repair time it retrieves applicable skills from the defect's statement types and patterns to guide patch generation, with no parameter updates or program translation.
M3oCmJtb7J.key_idea: Abstract high-resource repair knowledge into statement-type-grouped skills and retrieve them by statement type and defect pattern to guide patches in low-resource languages.
M3oCmJtb7J.evidence: Experiments on xCodeEval and SWE-bench Multilingual across low-resource languages and LLMs, in both procedural and agentic repair settings.
M3oCmJtb7J.claimed_gains: No numbers stated; the abstract says repair performance improves consistently across low-resource languages and LLMs in procedural and agentic settings.
M3oCmJtb7J.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find reusing repair knowledge without fine-tuning or translation a useful direction, with several baselines compared, supportive ablations, and coverage of procedural and agentic settings.
M3oCmJtb7J.main_concern: Novelty over existing knowledge-reuse methods such as ExpeRepair is limited, and gains may reflect teacher-model transfer rather than cross-language transfer, with Java as the only source language.

IEAVz5ihi7.one_liner: Spiking network for irregular multivariate time series forecasting using a leaky neuron with interval-aware fractional memory.
IEAVz5ihi7.problem: Existing irregular multivariate time series methods rely on temporal alignment or structural reformulation and do not exploit the sparse event characteristics arising from partial observability.
IEAVz5ihi7.method: TAFNet uses a time-adaptive fractional leaky integrate-and-fire (TAF-LIF) neuron that puts actual inter-observation intervals and a fractional memory kernel into the membrane potential evolution. It also builds multi-granularity temporal representations and combines them with global periodic information extracted from irregular timestamps.
IEAVz5ihi7.key_idea: A leaky integrate-and-fire neuron whose membrane update weights history by real inter-observation intervals through a fractional memory kernel.
IEAVz5ihi7.evidence: Experiments on real-world datasets (not named in the abstract, which is cut off); reviews mention a comparison against f-LIF in Table 3.
IEAVz5ihi7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers see a good problem and an interesting TAF-LIF neuron that uses real intervals and fractional dynamics for irregular sampling, with competitive results.
IEAVz5ihi7.main_concern: The gain of TAF-LIF over the closely related f-LIF is not isolated, and key training details such as handling non-differentiable spiking and learnable parameters are missing.

sUp6WnbULa.one_liner: Next-scale mesh generation: dyadic voxel-grid collapse defines scales and a masked discrete diffusion model learns inverse split-and-rewire steps.
sUp6WnbULa.problem: Artist-style mesh generation relies on costly autoregressive models or flow models with heuristic connectivity decoders, and existing next-scale methods use simplification-based scales that remove intra-scale parallelism and scale steps linearly with face count.
sUp6WnbULa.method: Scales are dyadic spatial grid resolutions, with coarsening merging vertices that share a voxel cell and inheriting connectivity. The inverse split-and-rewire decides which octant sub-vertices exist for each coarse face and resolves local connectivity with discrete structural tokens, learned by a scale-conditioned masked-uniform discrete diffusion model.
sUp6WnbULa.key_idea: Define mesh scales by deterministic voxel-cell vertex merging and generate by per-face split-and-rewire with discrete tokens, enabling parallel intra-scale prediction.
sUp6WnbULa.evidence: Per reviews, comparisons with baselines on four criteria, faster inference, and ablations including a continuous variant; the abstract is cut off before results.
sUp6WnbULa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the canonical, parallel dyadic hierarchy a fix for the sequential bottleneck of simplification-based hierarchies, with joint vertex and connectivity generation and faster inference than baselines.
sUp6WnbULa.main_concern: It is unclear how conflicting vertex and edge predictions across adjacent faces are resolved to guarantee topological validity, and no manifoldness or watertightness metrics are reported.

TilvqUF0Wu.one_liner: Full-pipeline recipe (SFT data selection, text-only mixing, RLVR) injects tool use into thinking models without hurting no-tool reasoning.
TilvqUF0Wu.problem: Tool-enabled evaluation can degrade strong thinking models even when they make almost no tool calls, so tool-use behavior must be added without losing no-tool reasoning.
TilvqUF0Wu.method: The recipe runs tool-integrated SFT on learnable teacher trajectories that favor tool-suited problems, controls the share of tool-use trajectories against forgetting, and picks SFT checkpoints by pass@k and response length rather than loss. A stable RLVR stage with safeguards against mode collapse follows, applied to Qwen3 thinking models at 4B and 30B scales.
TilvqUF0Wu.key_idea: Select learnable tool-suited teacher trajectories, cap the tool-trajectory share to avoid forgetting, pick SFT checkpoints by pass@k and length, then run stable RLVR with mode-collapse safeguards.
TilvqUF0Wu.evidence: Qwen3 thinking models at 4B and 30B scales on a wide range of benchmarks including AIME 2025; reviews mention tool-enabled versus no-tool comparisons and a contamination audit.
TilvqUF0Wu.claimed_gains: The abstract cites 96.7% and 99.2% on benchmarks before it is cut off, and the TLDR gives 99.2% on AIME 2025 with a 30B model.
TilvqUF0Wu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem practical and the results strong, with useful diagnoses of failure modes such as degradation when tools are enabled, fabricated execution outputs, and unstable SFT-to-RL transitions.
TilvqUF0Wu.main_concern: Positioning against prior tool-integrated reasoning work (START, CoRT, ToRL and others) is unclear, since the recipe's components are known post-training practices recombined.

oNRr3O4ZbT.one_liner: Detects code LLM memorization of functional logic by testing whether target-model continuations match original outputs on agent-generated inputs.
oNRr3O4ZbT.problem: Code can be functionally equivalent while textually dissimilar, so textual-overlap audits miss leakage of logic from code a model was trained on.
oNRr3O4ZbT.method: AI coding agents generate diverse test inputs for training functions, and model-generated continuations are checked for the same outputs. A counterfactual framework compares target models exposed to the code with reference models that were not, requiring functional equivalence only for the target; it is instantiated on 4 open-source models and 5 programming languages.
oNRr3O4ZbT.key_idea: A function counts as memorized only if the exposed model reproduces its behavior on agent-generated inputs and the unexposed reference model does not.
oNRr3O4ZbT.evidence: Four open-source models and functions with meaningful logic in 5 programming languages, plus a check of LLM-based judges as a proxy for execution-based testing.
oNRr3O4ZbT.claimed_gains: 0.3-3.4% of functions are counterfactually functionally memorized, and LLM-based judges reach a true positive rate of 68% at 1% false positive rate.
oNRr3O4ZbT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find auditing code-model memorization beyond textual overlap an important gap, with concrete examples and evidence across several models and programming languages.
oNRr3O4ZbT.main_concern: Reported rates may include generalization rather than memorization, since the reference and target models differ by an entire training phase and not only the tested function.

NWTA24g36c.one_liner: Aligns RGB, depth, LiDAR, mmWave, and WiFi to a skeleton-pretrained temporal-joint motion space, then fuses by reliability and disagreement.
NWTA24g36c.problem: Heterogeneous sensors capture the same activity through different physical signals and data structures, and existing methods bridge them with modality-invariant learning or LLM-based semantic alignment.
NWTA24g36c.method: In Stage 1, modality-specific Motion Adapters with learnable joint queries map each sensor's features into joint-indexed tokens in a shared temporal-joint motion space from a skeleton-pretrained model (skeletons used only in training). In Stage 2, RDMF estimates time-varying modality reliability to form a weighted motion consensus and uses cross-modal disagreement to retain complementary information.
NWTA24g36c.key_idea: Use human motion as the shared anchor: adapters map each sensor into a skeleton-model joint-token space, then fusion weights modalities by time-varying reliability and disagreement.
NWTA24g36c.evidence: Extensive evaluations per reviews, covering seven heterogeneous modalities and inference on arbitrary modality subsets; the abstract is cut off before results.
NWTA24g36c.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the motion-as-common-ground framing a worthwhile counterpoint to semantic-alignment approaches, with a well-motivated problem and extensive evaluations.
NWTA24g36c.main_concern: Gains may come from distillation from a task-supervised skeleton teacher that baselines lack, and novelty over prior privileged 3D-pose methods is not clearly established.

4zQetevBaU.one_liner: Defers prefill of pruned multimodal tokens into spare decode compute so multi-turn MLLMs recover information lost to query-aware pruning.
4zQetevBaU.problem: Long multimodal inputs increase time to first token, and query-aware hard pruning permanently excludes information that later questions may need.
4zQetevBaU.method: An existing pruning method selects tokens for the initial prefill, and Raincheck keeps the unselected tokens and prefills them progressively in source order using spare compute during decode, continuing after the answer in scheduling gaps. Attention visibility control and affine state mapping allow context updates after generation starts in full-attention and hybrid recurrent models, and prefill-decode fusion reduces repeated weight reads.
4zQetevBaU.key_idea: Keep pruned tokens and prefill them progressively during decode, using attention visibility control and affine state mapping so context can be updated mid-generation.
4zQetevBaU.evidence: Qwen3-VL-8B and Qwen3.5-9B with 30% initial multimodal-token retention, four pruning methods, MultiVerse and ConvBench, and an SGLang implementation.
4zQetevBaU.claimed_gains: Recovers on average 73.7% and 59.3% of the quality lost to matched hard pruning on MultiVerse and ConvBench, and cuts mean first-turn TTFT by up to 24.1% relative to full prefill on MultiVerse with under 0.5% increase in mean TPOT.
4zQetevBaU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find that the method recovers pruned information and lowers first-turn latency, with gains across all model-selector pairs and a useful control showing recovery during generation beats recovery after the answer.
4zQetevBaU.main_concern: The latency benefit relies on spare decode compute that may vanish under concurrent serving, and its value over existing deferred-computation or token-recovery methods is not shown.

KCA3mnPMPa.one_liner: Benchmarks LLM-driven context engineering methods across reasoning datasets and links their gains to failure-mode diversity.
KCA3mnPMPa.problem: It is unclear when and how LLMs can engineer effective context from data when used as the engineer that draws instructions or experiences from offline trials.
KCA3mnPMPa.method: The authors build a benchmark of datasets with different reasoning patterns, compare LCE methods across 8B-size LLM families, and analyze how gains relate to the diversity of failure modes in reasoning trajectories, instruction adherence, and experience extraction.
KCA3mnPMPa.key_idea: Compare LCE methods under one shared benchmark and relate their gains to the diversity of failure modes in the reasoning trajectories they learn from.
KCA3mnPMPa.evidence: A new benchmark of datasets with different reasoning patterns, 8B-size LLM families, and scaling of model parameters and generation iterations.
KCA3mnPMPa.claimed_gains: No single LCE method wins on all tasks even against chain-of-thought, and gains are negatively correlated with failure-mode diversity (r=-0.5, p<=0.05).
KCA3mnPMPa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the unified evaluation of several LCE methods under shared models and datasets and the analysis tying failure-mode diversity to LCE gains.
KCA3mnPMPa.main_concern: The failure-mode diversity finding is correlational and may be confounded by dataset differences, with no controlled or within-dataset analysis.

F2YKNNKmF6.one_liner: Replay-training method applying one random translation per sequence, chosen from a nuisance causal model, to make decoder-free world models distractor-robust.
F2YKNNKmF6.problem: World models trained from pixels stay sensitive to camera motion and changing backgrounds even when trained without pixel reconstruction.
F2YKNNKmF6.method: CaNI uses a specified nuisance structural causal model to guide observation-proxy design before training; on a decoder-free Dreamer backbone it applies one randomly sampled padded translation consistently across each replay sequence, keeping the architecture and objectives. A theorem shows uniform posterior stability bounds changes in a fixed recurrent policy's return under observation interventions that preserve the controlled process.
F2YKNNKmF6.key_idea: Apply a single sequence-consistent random translation to replayed observations, chosen via a nuisance SCM, so latent posteriors stay stable under camera shifts.
F2YKNNKmF6.evidence: Five DeepMind Control tasks with driving-video backgrounds and camera jitter against five baselines, a no-jitter benchmark, evaluation-only jitter, two tasks with unseen DAVIS backgrounds, and a stability theorem.
F2YKNNKmF6.claimed_gains: Task-averaged return rises from 310.5 for the matched backbone to 715.5 for CaNI (approximately 130%), and time-averaged return improves by 15% on the driving-video benchmark without jitter.
F2YKNNKmF6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the clean matched-backbone comparison and large return gains, including less return loss when jitter appears only at evaluation.
F2YKNNKmF6.main_concern: Novelty and the role of the SCM are unclear because sequence-consistent random shifts already appear in DreamerPro, and the evidence covers one backbone and one nuisance type.

grRv3lEehM.one_liner: A separate model, trained with decoupled RL, decides when to generate guidance for an LLM agent and what it says.
grRv3lEehM.problem: Memory-augmented agents rely on similarity-based retrieval of static entries from episodic banks or skill libraries that often misalign with the current context.
grRv3lEehM.method: Mem-pi uses a dedicated language or vision-language model with its own parameters, separate from the downstream agent, to generate context-specific guidance. Conditioned on the agent context it jointly decides when to produce guidance and what to produce, trained with a decision-content decoupled RL objective that lets it abstain.
grRv3lEehM.key_idea: Generate guidance on demand with a separate model, learning when (or whether to abstain) and what with a decision-content decoupled RL objective instead of retrieving stored entries.
grRv3lEehM.evidence: Agentic benchmarks spanning web navigation, terminal-based tool use, and text-based embodied interaction; reviews mention four benchmarks, three seeds, ablations, and a WebArena leave-one-domain-out test.
grRv3lEehM.claimed_gains: Outperforms retrieval-based and prior RL-optimized memory baselines, with over 30% relative improvement on web navigation tasks.
grRv3lEehM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the explicit when-versus-what separation, its compatibility with frozen agents, and a broad evaluation with consistent gains and ablations.
grRv3lEehM.main_concern: There is no empirical comparison with the closest generative-memory or advisor methods (SEAM, Advisor Models), and the benefit of the decision-content objective is not cleanly isolated.

uuSS7XOl1y.one_liner: Training-free, inversion-free flow editing that correlates noise across steps as a Gaussian-Markov process and steers noise by semantic cues.
uuSS7XOl1y.problem: Independent Gaussian resampling at each step of inversion-free flow editing repeatedly shifts path-specific editing tendencies, preventing coherent accumulation and leaving incomplete edits with residual source content or artifacts.
uuSS7XOl1y.method: Noise Persistence models noise evolution as a Gaussian-Markov process combining inherited memory with newly sampled innovation. Semantic Steering selects target-favorable innovations using semantic cues within the estimated editing region while retaining the inherited memory.
uuSS7XOl1y.key_idea: Replace independent per-step noise with a Gaussian-Markov noise chain that inherits memory, and pick target-favorable innovations using semantic cues in the edit region.
uuSS7XOl1y.evidence: Per reviews, comparisons with inversion-free baselines such as FlowEdit and KV-Edit and ablations against noise averaging and velocity smoothing; the abstract is cut off before results.
uuSS7XOl1y.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the motivation clear and supported by targeted analysis, and see noise persistence as a simple training-free change that mitigates under-editing without extra network evaluations.
uuSS7XOl1y.main_concern: The preservation gain is not isolated from the masked background reset bundled with persistence, so the contribution beyond latent blending is unclear.

7bCEq4l08Q.one_liner: Template-aware spreadsheet form-filling agent that grounds errors to regions, restores corrupted template state, and re-grounds slots before further edits.
7bCEq4l08Q.problem: Errors in early edits can overwrite labels or misalign fields in spreadsheet form filling, undermining later decisions.
7bCEq4l08Q.method: CRAFT connects reflective validation to constrained local repair: detected errors are grounded to spreadsheet regions, corrupted template state is restored, and writable slots are re-grounded before later edits. A Rectangle-Aware Slot Grounder (RASG) proposes writable cells, while label-slot hints and protected regions constrain edits.
7bCEq4l08Q.key_idea: Ground detected errors to spreadsheet regions, restore corrupted template state, and re-ground writable slots with a rectangle-aware grounder before later edits, instead of regenerating the workbook.
7bCEq4l08Q.evidence: FormFillBench with 327 forms across Instruction-Only and Multi-File tracks, component-removal experiments, and a second backbone.
7bCEq4l08Q.claimed_gains: Improves pair accuracy by 8.51 and 23.38 percentage points over the strongest baselines on the Instruction-Only and Multi-File tracks, respectively.
7bCEq4l08Q.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the split into grounding, validation, and constrained local repair aimed at template-corrupting errors, with consistent gains across both tracks and two backbones.
7bCEq4l08Q.main_concern: Metrics and ablations do not directly isolate template preservation or the contribution of RASG, since accuracy measures only target-entry correctness and the ablation removes a whole module.

wHjDDPR7Fb.one_liner: Personalizes LLMs with a shared bank of low-rank factors composed per user and query, tuning only eight scalars per user.
wHjDDPR7Fb.problem: Personalized LLMs often need a complete adaptation state (a private LoRA) per user, which scales poorly as the user population grows.
wHjDDPR7Fb.method: LINEUP learns a bank of reusable low-rank personalization factors, composes them through user-conditioned recall and query-dependent calibration, and restricts target-user adaptation to a tiny user code over a shared correction space while all shared components stay fixed.
wHjDDPR7Fb.key_idea: Decouple capacity from per-user state: recall and calibrate shared low-rank factors per user and query, with each user optimizing only eight scalars.
wHjDDPR7Fb.evidence: Three empirical analyses of cross-user reuse, a finite-step finite-history risk bound, and experiments on six LaMP tasks with Llama-2-7B per reviews, plus LongLaMP in the appendix.
wHjDDPR7Fb.claimed_gains: Each target user optimizes only eight scalars, compared with 4.19 million per-user parameters in the evaluated private-LoRA configuration.
wHjDDPR7Fb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the motivation clear and grounded in evidence of reusable cross-user structure, with a coherent framework that balances personalization quality and storage cost across six LaMP tasks.
wHjDDPR7Fb.main_concern: Novelty over prior parameter-sharing personalization is unclear, and the benefit of shared capacity is not separated from adaptation rank, with evaluation limited to Llama-2-7B and LaMP.

mqfu10BVO0.one_liner: Grounds MLLM latent states in 3D-foundation-model camera and scene tokens, then explores latent-mode entry points during GRPO.
mqfu10BVO0.problem: MLLMs struggle with multi-image spatial reasoning because partial observations are hard to integrate into coherent internal spatial representations, and existing approaches need dense spatial annotations or external tools.
mqfu10BVO0.method: Stage one uses camera and scene tokens from a pretrained 3D foundation model to supervise latent states, jointly with text generation. Stage two augments GRPO with latent-mode entry point exploration, using successful exploratory trajectories to guide policy updates.
mqfu10BVO0.key_idea: Supervise latent reasoning states with 3D foundation model camera and scene tokens, then explore where to enter latent mode during GRPO and reinforce successful entry points.
mqfu10BVO0.evidence: Three multi-image benchmarks plus single-image settings; reviews cite Qwen2.5-VL-3B, MindCube-Tiny, SPAR-Bench-MV, and component ablations.
mqfu10BVO0.claimed_gains: No numbers stated; the abstract says consistent gains over spatial reasoning baselines on three multi-image benchmarks, with further improvements in single-image settings.
mqfu10BVO0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the two-stage framework and latent-mode entry exploration well motivated, with ablations supporting individual components and gains on several benchmarks.
mqfu10BVO0.main_concern: The overall framework closely resembles 3DThinker, leaving methodological novelty mainly in latent-mode entry exploration.

OQ5HpFCuRV.one_liner: Training-free probe finds an answer-conditioned feature subspace from visual representations and answer gradients, validated by deletion and steering.
OQ5HpFCuRV.problem: Attention maps and representation probes show where a VLM attends and what it encodes, but do not establish which feature directions a particular answer depends on in video spatial reasoning.
OQ5HpFCuRV.method: U-probe couples visual representations with gradients of the answer to identify an answer-conditioned feature subspace (U-space), validates its causal role with deletion and steering interventions, and traces its contributions across the visual scene and over finetuning.
OQ5HpFCuRV.key_idea: Couple visual representations with gradients of the answer to extract a causal feature subspace, then trace its regional utility across the scene and across finetuning.
OQ5HpFCuRV.evidence: VLMs finetuned on spatial tasks, deletion and steering interventions, and comparisons with random-subspace and PCA controls per reviews; subspaces for corresponding tasks agree across datasets.
OQ5HpFCuRV.claimed_gains: No benchmark gains stated; regional utility after as few as 20 finetuning steps predicts later model performance, whereas regional attention does not.
OQ5HpFCuRV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find U-probe more compelling than attention maps or plain probes because interventions beat random-subspace and PCA controls, and value its use as an early diagnostic of spatial finetuning.
OQ5HpFCuRV.main_concern: The novelty of the scene-structure finding is overstated relative to prior causal-intervention work, and it is unclear how independently the interventions validate a subspace built on the same first-order criterion.

BMFkVzbSsO.one_liner: Masked EEG pre-training with frequency-factorized targets: delta, theta, and alpha bands, each tokenized into multiple discrete slots.
BMFkVzbSsO.problem: A single broadband discrete code must compress heterogeneous rhythms into one decision, and enlarging its vocabulary does not create independently representable signal components.
BMFkVzbSsO.method: NeuroWeave factorizes each one-second channel patch into delta, theta, and alpha bands and represents each band with multiple discrete slots from independent tokenizers that generate frozen targets. A shared spatiotemporal Transformer predicts these targets from masked broadband input.
BMFkVzbSsO.key_idea: Predict frozen multi-slot discrete tokens per frequency band, rather than one broadband code, from masked broadband EEG input.
BMFkVzbSsO.evidence: Staged tests of tokenizer capacity, masked reconstruction, band selection on TUAB and TUEV validation, and downstream transfer across six datasets against single-slot, broadband VQ, and waveform-regression controls.
BMFkVzbSsO.claimed_gains: Across six datasets the three-band model surpasses single-slot, broadband VQ, and waveform-regression controls on every reported metric; no numeric gains are stated before the abstract is cut off.
BMFkVzbSsO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the design question clear and the controlled comparisons credible, with shared backbone, masking, and protocol favoring the selected configuration across six datasets.
BMFkVzbSsO.main_concern: Band selection appears to use the same TUAB and TUEV numbers later reported as results, making the broad state-of-the-art claim too strong, and comparison with other EEG transformers is limited.
