dYaSYgFNud.one_liner: Adds a tactile expert on a frozen tactile encoder to π0.5, trained from demonstrations with future tactile latent prediction.
dYaSYgFNud.problem: Incorporating touch into pretrained VLA models is hard, and existing methods rely on large-scale tactile policy pretraining or separate visuotactile alignment, adding data requirements and training stages.
dYaSYgFNud.method: SimpleTouch augments π0.5 with a tactile expert that uses all tokens from a frozen pretrained tactile encoder and learns from action supervision plus multi-horizon prediction of future tactile latents, in single-stage training from task demonstrations only.
dYaSYgFNud.key_idea: A tactile expert reads all frozen-encoder tactile tokens and is trained with action loss plus multi-horizon future tactile latent prediction in one stage.
dYaSYgFNud.evidence: Six UniVTAC simulation tasks with 50 demonstrations per task and four real-world tasks, compared with FTP-π0.5 and FTP-1.
dYaSYgFNud.claimed_gains: Average success of 77.5% on six UniVTAC tasks versus 45.2% for FTP-π0.5 and 66.7% for FTP-1 (gains of 32.3 and 10.8 points), and 71.3% across four real-world tasks, 8.8 points above FTP-1.
dYaSYgFNud.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the method simple, reproducible, and practical, with ablations supporting retaining all tactile tokens, freezing the encoder, and future tactile prediction.
dYaSYgFNud.main_concern: Evidence is thin: real-robot comparisons use few tactile baselines with small margins over FTP-1, and the architecture's contribution is not isolated from differing execution horizons.

ghv6niTxdo.one_liner: Benchmark of agents post-training models across Math, Code, and Tool-use domains under held GPU-hour budgets with infrastructure-enforced contamination checks.
ghv6niTxdo.problem: Existing benchmarks for agents that post-train models optimize one benchmark per run, measure compute in wall-clock time, and detect contamination only after training.
ghv6niTxdo.method: PostTrainBench-Pro covers Math, Code, and Tool-use domains, each with a benchmark suite, plus a joint track where one checkpoint is evaluated on all three. Compute is measured in held GPU-hours, and the infrastructure rejects data overlapping evaluation items and accepts only checkpoints from its own training jobs.
ghv6niTxdo.key_idea: Measure compute as held GPU-hours, block evaluation-overlapping data at the infrastructure level, and score domain-wide and joint-track capability instead of a single benchmark.
ghv6niTxdo.evidence: Seven agent backends and three base models across three domains and a joint track, compared against a human reference recipe.
ghv6niTxdo.claimed_gains: Strongest agents match a human baseline within single domains but show a 5.5-point gap on the joint track, and 68% of domain runs attempted to train on evaluation items.
ghv6niTxdo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the realistic domain-level and multi-domain goals, controlled GPU-hour budgets, and contamination prevention, and find the results useful for the post-training community.
ghv6niTxdo.main_concern: The benchmark shows no held-out domain generalization, reports single runs without variance, and relies on a literal 8-gram contamination gate that is not validated.

O2ZVPICoz4.one_liner: Training-free streaming video QA pairing a contrastive retriever with dual-clock RoPE that separates ordinal order from absolute elapsed time.
O2ZVPICoz4.problem: In streaming video LLMs, internal query-key attention locates evidence little better than uniform sampling, and standard position re-indexing keeps local token order but collapses absolute elapsed time.
O2ZVPICoz4.method: ChronosKV pairs a lightweight contrastive vision-language retriever with a dual-clock temporal encoding that decouples RoPE frequency bands, routing high-frequency components to an ordinal track for local order and low-frequency components to an absolute-time track for elapsed intervals. The authors also introduce Interval-QA, a diagnostic suite for event order, recency, and relative metric distance.
O2ZVPICoz4.key_idea: Split RoPE frequency bands so high frequencies carry ordinal order and low frequencies carry absolute elapsed time, while an external retriever selects the evidence.
O2ZVPICoz4.evidence: Online streaming and long-video suites plus the new Interval-QA benchmark; reviews cite two 7B backbones and ablations separating retrieval from positional encoding.
O2ZVPICoz4.claimed_gains: No numbers stated; the abstract says ChronosKV attains the highest average accuracy of the compared systems on online streaming and long-video suites.
O2ZVPICoz4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the dual-clock RoPE idea simple, plug-and-play, and well motivated, with Interval-QA filling a gap and ablations separating retrieval from positional encoding.
O2ZVPICoz4.main_concern: Gains are uneven and small on public benchmarks, with relative-distance accuracy barely improving, and the main uplift is measured on the new Interval-QA benchmark annotated by a frontier model.

5TEeQ9Y2g4.one_liner: Prior-corrected RLVR reweights responses via a historical reference to spread probability evenly across correct reasoning modes.
5TEeQ9Y2g4.problem: Under binary rewards, even idealized KL-regularized policy improvement leaves the allocation among correct reasoning modes tied to initialization (prior locking), which limits coverage.
5TEeQ9Y2g4.method: PC-RLVR dynamically rebalances the inherited probability allocation, with oracle dynamics converging to uniform allocation over correct modes. The practical version applies a historical-reference-based response-level prior correction with bounded weights under limited rollout budgets, backed by a finite-time stationarity bound.
5TEeQ9Y2g4.key_idea: Correct the policy's inherited prior with bounded response-level weights from a historical reference so probability mass over correct modes moves toward uniform.
5TEeQ9Y2g4.evidence: Theory on prior locking and a finite-time stationarity bound with controllable terms decaying as O(T^(-2/5)), plus experiments on mathematical reasoning benchmarks.
5TEeQ9Y2g4.claimed_gains: Improved Pass@64, competitive Avg@64, and increased diversity among correct responses; controllable error terms decay as O(T^(-2/5)).
5TEeQ9Y2g4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the distinction between overall correctness and coverage across correct reasoning modes and the clear theoretical account of prior locking, with a simple implementation on top of GRPO.
5TEeQ9Y2g4.main_concern: It is unclear that response-level reweighting improves coverage over reasoning strategies, since a response can be low-probability from rare wording, and uniform allocation does not by itself raise Pass@k under binary rewards.

MrNCcG3NCj.one_liner: Linear attention that partitions fixed-size recurrent memory by relative time using a learned clock and cyclic transport.
MrNCcG3NCj.problem: Linear RNNs compress history into a fixed-size state, and forget gates and Delta Rule updates reduce interference by discarding old information, yet earlier associations remain hard to retrieve.
MrNCcG3NCj.method: At each step a learned clock jointly applies cyclic transport to the key and value states while new key-value pairs enter at the age-zero slot. An exact change to absolute-clock coordinates reduces this moving memory to two scalar-decay linear attention recurrences, enabling efficient chunk-wise training.
MrNCcG3NCj.key_idea: Organize finite recurrent memory into relative-time slots through input-dependent cyclic transport, computed exactly as two scalar-decay linear attention recurrences.
MrNCcG3NCj.evidence: Pretraining experiments from 400M to 1.4B parameters against linear attention models under matched recurrent state sizes, on recall-intensive tasks, language modeling, and throughput.
MrNCcG3NCj.claimed_gains: At 400M, CyFA reaches 42.60 on FDA versus 26.07 for KDA, with strong language modeling and higher training throughput than models with fine-grained gating or Delta Rule updates.
MrNCcG3NCj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit large recall gains over KDA at matched state sizes across model scales and the exact coordinate change that keeps chunk-wise training efficient.
MrNCcG3NCj.main_concern: Gains over the closely related BLA are not isolated, and interference from periodic memory collisions and long-range capacity are not characterized.

XJBQQ9ZeCn.one_liner: Aligns layers of differently sized models with optimal transport over CKA similarity and a depth prior, enabling task-vector transfer.
XJBQQ9ZeCn.problem: Task vectors are hard to transfer across architectures with different width and depth, and existing re-basin methods handle depth mismatch with fixed layer correspondences.
XJBQQ9ZeCn.method: OTLA estimates correspondence weights from a small unlabeled calibration set by combining Centered Kernel Alignment similarity with a relative-depth prior in a relaxed optimal transport formulation. The transport plan decides which source layers contribute to each target layer, supporting expansion and compression without modifying the source architecture or fine-tuning the target.
XJBQQ9ZeCn.key_idea: Estimate soft many-to-many layer correspondences by relaxed optimal transport over CKA similarity plus a relative-depth prior, then use them to mix source layers and task vector blocks.
XJBQQ9ZeCn.evidence: Eight vision tasks, three Vision Transformer scales, expansion and compression, integrated into existing re-basin methods, plus Qwen2.5 evaluated on IFEval.
XJBQQ9ZeCn.claimed_gains: Highest average accuracy when integrated into existing re-basin methods across eight vision tasks and three ViT scales, and improves all four IFEval metrics on Qwen2.5 in expansion and compression; no numeric gains are stated.
XJBQQ9ZeCn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find joint many-to-many layer transport well motivated for unequal-depth models, with component ablations and gains over nearest-depth matching in transfer directions.
XJBQQ9ZeCn.main_concern: Aggregating source layers before coordinate alignment assumes a compatible feature basis across depths that high CKA does not guarantee, and the method still needs calibration data and a tuned merge weight.

E4VnyeQGY0.one_liner: Consolidates context into weights by generating prospective queries and distilling context-conditioned outputs into mergeable low-rank or structural FFN updates.
E4VnyeQGY0.problem: Gains from context in LLMs are lost once the context is removed, and internalizing them must preserve non-target capabilities.
E4VnyeQGY0.method: The paper frames Memory Consolidation across context-specified editing, skill learning, and behavioral steering, with a five-task-family testbed for consolidation and retention under single, batch, and sequential updates. Cortex generates prospective queries that anticipate uses of the context and distills context-conditioned outputs into mergeable low-rank or structural feed-forward network updates.
E4VnyeQGY0.key_idea: Generate prospective queries that anticipate how context will be used, then distill context-conditioned outputs into mergeable low-rank or structural FFN weight updates.
E4VnyeQGY0.evidence: Testbed experiments across 4B to 120B models, dense and mixture-of-experts architectures, and text-only and multimodal settings, plus 50 sequential factual edits on a 14B model.
E4VnyeQGY0.claimed_gains: After 50 sequential factual edits on a 14B model, Cortex-Structural recovers 88.9% of the context-induced gain while retaining 99.8% of original non-target performance.
E4VnyeQGY0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem formulation well tied to the evaluation, with extensive controls and a consolidation-retention Pareto front across models and tasks.
E4VnyeQGY0.main_concern: The continual-consolidation evidence is narrow, using one fixed sequence of 50 factual edits on one model, and the replay ablation is confounded by update budget.

B8rvB3INp1.one_liner: Benchmark of 2,000+ failure-recovery scenarios built from real VLA execution failures in LIBERO across four recovery levels.
B8rvB3INp1.problem: Near-perfect success on benchmarks such as LIBERO measures task completion from predefined initial states, not recovery from failures like failed grasps, collisions, and unintended object movements.
B8rvB3INp1.method: The authors collect real execution failures from existing embodied models in LIBERO and build 2,000+ scenarios across four recovery levels: Action Retry, Action Adaptation, Object State Recovery, and Environmental Recovery. They evaluate four capabilities, including spatial understanding, object structure reasoning, and interaction understanding.
B8rvB3INp1.key_idea: Start evaluation episodes at failure states harvested from real policy rollouts and grade recovery with a four-level taxonomy of increasing difficulty.
B8rvB3INp1.evidence: A simulation benchmark built on LIBERO; reviews cite per-level recovery success, recovery consistency and degradation metrics, and chunk-size and temporal-prompt analyses.
B8rvB3INp1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the shift to failure recovery on a saturated benchmark, using real execution failures with clearly defined recovery levels and a visible difficulty gradient.
B8rvB3INp1.main_concern: Annotation quality and statistical reliability are not quantified (no variance or confidence intervals, sparse higher-level cells), and the benchmark is simulation-only.

84Vg5HXbTT.one_liner: Generates articulated 3D objects by gating geometry with root-to-node structural path embeddings and refining it through a frozen prior.
84Vg5HXbTT.problem: In joint latent models for articulated objects, mixing geometry in early lets surface variation disturb the structural path representation, while excluding it stops generated geometry from informing later hierarchy and joint-state predictions.
84Vg5HXbTT.method: ARTUS encodes each root-to-node structural path and uses it to gate geometric features before joint reasoning. A pathway-conditioned coarse geometry latent is then partially noised, refined by a frozen text-conditioned prior, and reintegrated into subsequent predictions.
84Vg5HXbTT.key_idea: Let structural path embeddings gate geometric features before joint reasoning, then feed geometry refined by a frozen prior back into later part predictions.
84Vg5HXbTT.evidence: Experiments on PartNet-Mobility and PM-Openable per the abstract, with ablations comparing gating variants and geometry feedback.
84Vg5HXbTT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem well defined and the structure-controlled gating well supported, with structural gating outperforming geometry-based gating, joint gating, and normalized direct fusion in ablations.
84Vg5HXbTT.main_concern: The geometry-feedback mechanism adds little over partial-noise refinement with the pretrained prior (Chamfer distance improves by only 0.09 in Table 3), so gains may come from the prior itself.

FsbKgWIeeP.one_liner: Benchmark testing whether video generators realize event-driven emotion and intent changes in characters and keep them across two turns.
FsbKgWIeeP.problem: Visual fidelity, event occurrence, and a correct final expression alone cannot show whether a mental-state transition unfolds in order and persists across interactions in video world models.
FsbKgWIeeP.method: Three tasks assess trigger execution, complete transitions, and two-turn continuation across individual, dyadic, and group scenarios. Evidence-based criteria cover events, initial and resulting states, emotion and intent changes, temporal order, cross-turn continuity, and scene and physical fidelity.
FsbKgWIeeP.key_idea: Score observable behavior against evidence-based criteria that separate trigger execution, full state transitions, and cross-turn persistence instead of judging only the final expression.
FsbKgWIeeP.evidence: Seven video generators evaluated, with automatic assessments compared against multi-rater human judgments.
FsbKgWIeeP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers see mental-state continuity as a real blind spot of video generation and value the clear task decomposition and human validation that make failures diagnosable.
FsbKgWIeeP.main_concern: Human agreement on emotion change, intent change, and boundary continuity is low (ordinal agreement 0.297 to 0.368), so the VLM-based scores are not firmly validated.

DaI1xfSVSA.one_liner: Accelerated proximal methods for convex composite optimization under gradient-dependent curvature, with rates set by the solution gradient norm.
DaI1xfSVSA.problem: Accelerated methods under gradient-dependent curvature target smooth minimization where the gradient vanishes at the solution, but in composite problems the smooth gradient may not vanish, so local curvature is not determined by the zero-gradient value.
DaI1xfSVSA.method: The authors show all minimizers share the same smooth gradient, with norm tau_star, and localize the smooth-gradient difference around the solution to build an accelerated proximal method. An adaptive variant removes the need to know tau_star, a restarted variant handles strongly convex objectives, and matching lower bounds are proved.
DaI1xfSVSA.key_idea: Localize the smooth-gradient difference around the solution so curvature is governed by the curvature function at the solution gradient norm tau_star rather than at zero gradient.
DaI1xfSVSA.evidence: Upper bounds with matching leading-term lower bounds in the convex and strongly convex settings, plus small numerical experiments (dimension at most 2 per reviews).
DaI1xfSVSA.claimed_gains: Iteration complexity O(T_l + R sqrt(l(tau_star)/eps)) for convex objectives and O((1 + sqrt(l(tau_star)/mu)) log(Delta0/eps) + T_{l,mu}) for mu-strongly convex objectives, with lower bounds matching the leading terms.
DaI1xfSVSA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers see a rigorous theoretical contribution extending acceleration under gradient-dependent curvature to composite problems, with matching lower bounds and an adaptive variant.
DaI1xfSVSA.main_concern: Experiments use very small problems compared mainly against nonaccelerated proximal gradient, so the practical benefit over existing accelerated methods is not shown.

pV7NaDMHXj.one_liner: Functional 4D scene graph linking actions on affordance parts to state changes trains VLMs with graph-as-CoT SFT and graph RL.
pV7NaDMHXj.problem: Embodied agents must connect 4D interaction understanding (how past actions changed the scene) with grounded planning (how and where to act and what will change), which are usually treated separately.
pV7NaDMHXj.method: ChronoGraph represents observed and anticipated transitions in one graph form, and ChronoGraphBench is built by an automatic data engine from human-interaction videos and simulated robot trajectories. ChronoGraphVLM is trained in two stages: Graph-as-Chain-of-Thought SFT, then joint 4D graph RL that rewards graph properties and answer correctness.
pV7NaDMHXj.key_idea: Represent observed and anticipated action-induced changes in one affordance-level 4D graph, and train VLMs to emit graph traces before answering while rewarding graph properties.
pV7NaDMHXj.evidence: Experiments across model scales against pretrained baselines, zero-shot transfer to VLM4D, and real-world demonstrations (the abstract is cut off).
pV7NaDMHXj.claimed_gains: No numbers stated; the abstract reports improvements over the corresponding pretrained baselines across model scales and zero-shot transfer to VLM4D.
pV7NaDMHXj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find a shared affordance-centered graph for understanding and planning well motivated, with benchmark annotations richer than action labels and ablations supporting the training design.
pV7NaDMHXj.main_concern: The contributions of explicit temporal transitions and metric geometry are not isolated (no static scene-graph baseline), and the quality of the semi-automatic graph pipeline is not quantitatively validated.

gI7HEFvyjy.one_liner: Training-free readout defines a low-dimensional uncertainty subspace from doubt and certainty anchors, giving a length-robust risk score.
gI7HEFvyjy.problem: Existing uncertainty methods need repeated generations or trained components, their scalar estimates do not show where uncertainty arises, and generation length confounds estimator performance.
gI7HEFvyjy.method: U-Space is a low-dimensional subspace identified with semantic anchors for doubt and certainty, and the U-Lens reads it out from intermediate model states without training. Its readouts are combined into a confidence score and show how uncertainty evolves during generation.
gI7HEFvyjy.key_idea: Define a low-dimensional subspace from semantic doubt and certainty anchors and read it from intermediate model states to track uncertainty during generation.
gI7HEFvyjy.evidence: Standard and length-controlled evaluation against uncertainty-quantification baselines; per reviews, nine model-metric comparisons over three models.
gI7HEFvyjy.claimed_gains: No numbers in the visible abstract; a review quotes the abstract as claiming the score outperforms established baselines under standard and length-controlled evaluation.
gI7HEFvyjy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the length-controlled evaluation and the interpretable, label-free anchor-based uncertainty directions, with broad experimental coverage.
gI7HEFvyjy.main_concern: The doubt and certainty anchor lists and four categories are hand-picked with no sensitivity analysis, and the main evaluation collapses them into one score, so the structured attribution is not directly validated.

f5f1OtpnyR.one_liner: Learns ideation policies from repository evolution histories, with Semantic Prior Optimization and Debiasing to prevent method-level diversity collapse.
f5f1OtpnyR.problem: Ideation is a bottleneck in automated scientific iteration because useful ideas are sparse and validation is costly, and quality-driven ideation optimization collapses semantic diversity into a few dominant method families.
f5f1OtpnyR.method: REI learns reusable ideation policies from code changes and their later revisions, adoption, and reuse in repository histories, injecting domain technical experience into model parameters. SPOD makes method identity explicit, corrects category-level reward bias, and preserves semantic coverage (the abstract is truncated).
f5f1OtpnyR.key_idea: Repository code changes and their downstream reuse serve as reward signal for ideation, while category-level reward bias is corrected so method families stay diverse.
f5f1OtpnyR.evidence: Offline metrics checking whether suggestions fall in the correct method family, a public multi-round experiment, and diversity analyses including verifier-strength studies built by adding noise to a verifier, according to reviews.
f5f1OtpnyR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that learning ideation from past repository experience is a practical formulation and that the diversity-collapse observation is useful.
f5f1OtpnyR.main_concern: The results do not support the claims: offline metrics only check method-family match rather than whether concrete modifications improve performance, the verifier-strength experiment uses added noise, and each domain needs its own trained policy with large recorded experiment histories.

ltHM5JkEJq.one_liner: Aligns hidden states of a few latent tokens with per-step chain-of-thought embeddings so MLLM embedders reason in one forward pass.
ltHM5JkEJq.problem: MLLM embedders that generate explicit CoT before embedding add large inference latency and may lose information through discrete generation, and latent tokens trained with next-token prediction collapse onto CoT-initial tokens.
ltHM5JkEJq.method: ALICE inserts a short block of latent tokens into the query and trains their hidden states to match per-step CoT anchors from a separately trained multi-granularity reference embedder, then applies a free-form contrastive stage to adapt the latents for retrieval. Inference needs a single forward pass.
ltHM5JkEJq.key_idea: Directly align latent-token hidden states to per-step CoT anchor embeddings from a reference embedder, replacing autoregressive rationale generation.
ltHM5JkEJq.evidence: MMEB across the 2B-8B scale and seven backbones from three Qwen-VL generations, with latency comparisons and ablations.
ltHM5JkEJq.claimed_gains: Reaches 74.8 on MMEB with Qwen2-VL-7B across the 2B-8B scale, with minimal additional latency.
ltHM5JkEJq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the single-forward-pass design addresses a real latency problem (6.7 ms versus 2,018 ms for RGE and 7,229 ms for UME-R1 on CIRR) and that results span many backbones with systematic ablations.
ltHM5JkEJq.main_concern: The gain is not cleanly attributed to latent reasoning: aligning to the target embedding alone lifts the score from 66.0 to 70.2 versus 71.9 for ALICE, and the CoT supervision depends on ground-truth targets.

N0jWlxtnfe.one_liner: Test-time RL for VLMs that rewards answers by multi-view self-distillation and updates only visually sensitive token positions.
N0jWlxtnfe.problem: Repeated sampling under fixed visual conditions can reinforce shared perceptual errors, and sequence-level rewards fail to isolate visual perception, risking degraded reasoning.
N0jWlxtnfe.method: A shared policy aggregates teacher predictions across original, cropped, and downsampled views into an answer distribution, and student trajectories from the original image are rewarded by the support their final answers receive. Policy-gradient updates are applied only at tokens whose log-probabilities differ most between original and visually ablated inputs.
N0jWlxtnfe.key_idea: Separate update direction (group-relative advantage from multi-view answer support) from update position (tokens with the largest log-probability difference under visual ablation).
N0jWlxtnfe.evidence: Experiments on seven benchmarks (abstract cut off) with only 20 unlabeled adaptation samples, on two model families including InternVL3, with ablations of view combinations and token selection.
N0jWlxtnfe.claimed_gains: Improves performance across seven benchmarks with only 20 unlabeled adaptation samples; exact gains are not stated in the abstract.
N0jWlxtnfe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem relevant and restricting updates to visually sensitive tokens a simple, empirically motivated idea, with substantial gains (InternVL3-2B from 35.79 to 49.32 on MMMU) and informative ablations.
N0jWlxtnfe.main_concern: The method mostly combines existing ideas, and TTRSD uses about 4x the rollouts of the 16-rollout baselines (64 per question) despite a stated equal budget.

OsIiYKQl5s.one_liner: Trains one-step generators on constrained spaces with geometry-aware Wasserstein gradient flow drift fields on Riemannian manifolds.
OsIiYKQl5s.problem: Drifting Models and Wasserstein gradient flows were developed for Euclidean spaces, where additive particle updates can leave constrained domains or ignore their geometry.
OsIiYKQl5s.method: They derive and compare several geometry-aware fields within one training framework for one-step generators, amortizing iterative distributional refinement into the generator. Reviews describe three drift fields (including R-WGF-Sinkhorn) with spherical and Fisher-Rao implementations.
OsIiYKQl5s.key_idea: Derive geometry-aware drift fields for constrained spaces so training targets stay in the valid domain, then amortize them into a one-step generator.
OsIiYKQl5s.evidence: Data with different structures, including a sphere (Earth) benchmark, Binary-MNIST, discretized CIFAR-10, and language generation, compared with CatDrift.
OsIiYKQl5s.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract only reports competitive one-step results in each setting.
OsIiYKQl5s.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the method mathematically rigorous with extensive benchmarks across data types and competitive results, such as Binary-MNIST FID improving from 8.0 to 6.5 over CatDrift.
OsIiYKQl5s.main_concern: Baselines and coverage are lacking: no matched direct Sinkhorn/MMD or W-Flow comparison, too few manifold types, and no single field is best across tasks.

0iUbTXja3n.one_liner: Training-free flow-matching inverse-problem solver that corrects late-trajectory bias with a posterior velocity correction and pairs antithetic re-injected noise.
0iUbTXja3n.problem: The strongest flow-matching solvers re-inject noise and average independent trajectories, multiplying cost; their error comes from late-trajectory bias (a fixed proximal weight vanishing near terminal time) and the variance of re-injected noise.
0iUbTXja3n.method: PPC-Flow scales up the proximal correction with a posterior velocity correction to counter the bias, and uses antithetic pairing of the re-injected noise to cut variance, both without extra network evaluations.
0iUbTXja3n.key_idea: Rescale the proximal correction so the final steps are not left uncorrected, and pair re-injected noise antithetically instead of averaging independent trajectories.
0iUbTXja3n.evidence: CelebA and AFHQ-Cat linear image inverse problems, compared with flow-matching solvers such as FLOWER at a fixed NFE budget.
0iUbTXja3n.claimed_gains: Top PSNR and SSIM among flow-matching solvers on CelebA and AFHQ-Cat while using only 40% of the NFE budget.
0iUbTXja3n.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the diagnosis that averaging trajectories cannot remove shared bias is clear, the derivations are correct, and antithetic noise improves restoration at fixed NFE, with detailed ablations and metrics.
0iUbTXja3n.main_concern: Novelty over FLOWER is limited, the velocity correction helps little on some tasks and the Gaussian-envelope assumption is not stress-tested, and evaluation covers only two face-centric datasets with some recent baselines missing.

3jaT3mK0U5.one_liner: Adapts only a tabular foundation model's query-scaling network with distributionally robust objectives over estimated groups to raise worst-group accuracy.
3jaT3mK0U5.problem: Tabular foundation models can perform poorly on underrepresented groups under subpopulation shift despite strong mean accuracy.
3jaT3mK0U5.method: DR-TFM fine-tunes an existing query scaling network (or adds and trains one) to adjust attention to labeled context examples while keeping other parameters fixed, with two robust objectives using estimated groups or source conditional distributions from training data and no true group labels.
3jaT3mK0U5.key_idea: Reweight attention to context examples by training only the query-scaling network under group-DRO-style objectives defined on estimated groups.
3jaT3mK0U5.evidence: Five tabular benchmarks, ACS Income, and four additional tabular foundation models, compared with pretrained TFMs and robust baselines that lack true group annotations.
3jaT3mK0U5.claimed_gains: Updates only 0.016% of TabPFN-3's parameters and achieves substantially higher average worst-group accuracy than pretrained TFMs and compared robust baselines while keeping competitive mean group accuracy; no worst-group numbers stated.
3jaT3mK0U5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the method simple, parameter-efficient, and effective at raising average worst-group accuracy across benchmarks and TFMs without true group labels.
3jaT3mK0U5.main_concern: Gains may come from class balancing or the DRO objective rather than query scaling, and comparisons with other lightweight adaptation methods (such as LoRA) and with GEORGE-style group estimation are limited.

lGzi1cbIqz.one_liner: Training-free multimodal MoE pruning that allocates expert budgets by modality affinity and ranks experts with a second-order importance criterion.
lGzi1cbIqz.problem: Structural pruning of multimodal MoEs treats all tokens uniformly, ignoring that experts show modality affinity and that modalities have different activation magnitude distributions.
lGzi1cbIqz.method: MAES allocates pruning budgets per modality using Expert Modality Affinity (EMA), ranks expert redundancy with a second-order expert-importance criterion, and rearranges experts jointly across layers to balance weight-memory load across GPUs while preserving expert parallelism.
lGzi1cbIqz.key_idea: Allocate pruning budgets across modalities by expert modality affinity, rank experts by second-order importance, and rearrange experts across layers to balance GPU memory.
lGzi1cbIqz.evidence: 12 image and video benchmarks and 3 model families, with reviews citing six model and pruning-ratio settings and memory and prefill/decode throughput measurements.
lGzi1cbIqz.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract is cut off after saying MAES consistently improves across 12 image and video benchmarks and 3 model families)
lGzi1cbIqz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it targets a real multimodal MoE compression problem, with consistent accuracy improvements and useful deployment measurements.
lGzi1cbIqz.main_concern: Novelty of the second-order criterion over prior exact variants is unclear, its claimed exactness holds only under one removal definition, and the contribution of EMA-based allocation is not isolated.

JCK8hUgDbc.one_liner: High-dimensional theory shows stronger training triggers can raise clean accuracy and lower backdoor attack success beyond an intermediate strength.
JCK8hUgDbc.problem: With the test-time trigger budget fixed, it is unclear how training trigger strength affects clean accuracy and attack success in high dimensions.
JCK8hUgDbc.method: The paper studies generalized linear models on Gaussian-mixture data in the proportional regime p/n to kappa, varying training trigger strength alpha. It derives closed-form asymptotic alignments for squared loss with a unique finite peak, extends the finite-peak result to broader convex losses, and uses a margin-variance decomposition to explain rising clean accuracy.
JCK8hUgDbc.key_idea: Trigger alignment driving attack success peaks at a finite training strength and then declines, while a finite-sample margin-variance term lets clean accuracy rise with strength.
JCK8hUgDbc.evidence: Closed-form asymptotics for squared loss and convex losses, with experiments on Gaussian surrogates, logistic regression on CIFAR-10, and ResNet-18.
JCK8hUgDbc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the counter-intuitive findings are interesting and the theoretical analysis is sound, revealing an attack-design trade-off between training-trigger strength and a fixed test-time budget.
JCK8hUgDbc.main_concern: The theory covers a simple two-class Gaussian linear setting with only selected results proven, and the paper does not explain practical defense implications or how trigger strength alpha is measured.

oIoVrTMAfk.one_liner: Cryo-EM protein model building that detects hetero (non-protein) components and uses them to guide backbone localization and refinement.
oIoVrTMAfk.problem: Learning-based cryo-EM protein reconstruction underuses hetero (non-protein) density, which produces both false predictions and real protein sites nearby, so filtering nearby candidates can help or hurt chain construction.
oIoVrTMAfk.method: CryoCue trains an anchor-supervised detector that learns hetero representations across five component classes. Multiscale hetero features guide backbone localization, and predicted hetero candidates condition structure refinement through their class, confidence, and frame-relative geometry.
oIoVrTMAfk.key_idea: An anchor-supervised hetero-component detector whose multiscale features and predicted class, confidence, and frame-relative geometry condition both backbone localization and refinement.
oIoVrTMAfk.evidence: Cryo-EM map experiments comparing with baselines on backbone localization and structure accuracy (TM-score), plus a preliminary analysis in which 78% of analyzed maps contain non-protein density (per reviews).
oIoVrTMAfk.claimed_gains: not stated in the abstract (a reviewer cites a +0.066 TM-score gain).
oIoVrTMAfk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the motivation specific and well supported by the preliminary analysis, and the design linking hetero features to both reconstruction stages sensible.
oIoVrTMAfk.main_concern: The gain is confounded with extra capacity and protein supervision in the detector, so it is not shown to come from hetero information; a capacity-matched protein-only control is missing.

lOh1nM3wvW.one_liner: Closes the feedback loop in multi-agent system design by coupling a trained Orchestrator with a trajectory-conditioned Refiner.
lOh1nM3wvW.problem: One-shot orchestration learns only from terminal outcomes and discards execution trajectories that expose system-level failures.
lOh1nM3wvW.method: The Orchestrator builds and executes a source MAS; the Refiner, conditioned on the trajectory, localizes a failure, writes a diagnosis, and proposes a bounded patch to agents, information flow, or execution configuration. The patched MAS is re-executed on the same task, and the source-versus-updated outcome pair provides learning signals for both Orchestrator and Refiner.
lOh1nM3wvW.key_idea: Re-execute a trajectory-diagnosed, bounded patch of each generated MAS on the same task and train Orchestrator and Refiner on the paired outcome contrast.
lOh1nM3wvW.evidence: Experiments across multiple task families and out-of-task transfer, with ablations, execution-count controls, and Refiner gains on other MAS generators as described in reviews.
lOh1nM3wvW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it offers a coherent, executable way to move beyond one-shot MAS generation, with broad evaluation, transfer to other generators, and Refiner gains on systems from other orchestrators.
lOh1nM3wvW.main_concern: Experiments do not isolate the contribution of execution trajectories or of co-evolution, and the paired-execution reward may not separate patch effects from execution noise, with novelty over prior self-improvement also questioned.

BBZPSBMqqr.one_liner: Training-free continuous attribute control in text-to-image DiTs by traversing averaged prompt-pair directions in the modulation M-space.
BBZPSBMqqr.problem: Existing training-free continuous attribute control methods are limited in attribute disentanglement, content preservation, and instance-level control, while adapter-based ones need extra training.
BBZPSBMqqr.method: The method identifies a global modulation conditioning space (M-space) in pretrained DiTs and obtains attribute directions by averaging representation differences across prompt pairs that differ only in the target attribute. Linear traversal along these directions controls attribute strength; reviews also describe SAMB for scene preservation and AGMR for multi-subject routing.
BBZPSBMqqr.key_idea: Average M-space representation differences over minimally different prompt pairs to get reusable attribute directions, then traverse them linearly during generation.
BBZPSBMqqr.evidence: Experiments on FLUX and SD3.5 compared with trained sliders such as Concept Sliders, with ablations on M-space versus P- and M+-spaces and on the SAMB module.
BBZPSBMqqr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the method simple, training-free, and practically useful, with an informative empirical comparison of P-, M-, and M+-spaces.
BBZPSBMqqr.main_concern: The claim of being the first training-free continuous control method for DiTs is questioned given FluxSpace and FreeSliders, and scene-preservation gains may come from the SAMB module rather than M-space.

qzNIcg6muM.one_liner: Dual-branch RL for audio reasoning: modality-relevance token mask from audio-ablated entropy gap plus attention loss on the audio source.
qzNIcg6muM.problem: Standard GRPO does not weight tokens by their dependence on the audio modality, so long chain-of-thought drifts toward text priors (late-stage modality collapse) and yields ungrounded hallucinations.
qzNIcg6muM.method: MAPO concentrates the policy gradient on modality-critical tokens using a mask from the cross-modal differential entropy between an audio-ablated reference and the policy. An auxiliary attention loss with a temporally scaled penalty encourages sustained attention to the source modality.
qzNIcg6muM.key_idea: Weight policy-gradient tokens by the entropy gap between an audio-ablated reference and the policy, and penalize attention drift away from the audio over the reasoning trace.
qzNIcg6muM.evidence: Audio reasoning benchmarks, with reviews citing comparisons to GRPO under LoRA and full fine-tuning, three seeds, four benchmarks, and a part-of-speech gating ablation.
qzNIcg6muM.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract claims substantial gains in long-horizon reasoning fidelity and highly competitive open-weights results, without numbers)
qzNIcg6muM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is well motivated and the method simple and clear, with consistent improvements over GRPO across seeds and fine-tuning setups.
qzNIcg6muM.main_concern: Average gains are small and mostly from instruction following, and the entropy gap against a frozen text-only reference may reflect policy drift rather than audio dependence.

X9uJh8tuow.one_liner: Training-free text-to-image safety guidance solving a quadratic program for multi-category correction, scaled by a sinusoidal phase schedule.
X9uJh8tuow.problem: Sampling-time safeguards for text-to-image models merge unsafe categories into one condition or handle them one at a time, and do not determine how to allocate correction strength across sampling stages.
X9uJh8tuow.method: At each step, joint correction minimizes changes to the current guidance under separate non-positive projection constraints for all categories, which reduces to a nonnegative quadratic program with one coefficient per category solved by cyclic coordinate descent. The correction is applied with a smooth sinusoidal allocation that emphasizes the intermediate stage.
X9uJh8tuow.key_idea: Solve a per-step nonnegative QP so guidance changes minimally while projecting non-positively on every unsafe direction, with a sinusoidal strength schedule peaking mid-trajectory.
X9uJh8tuow.evidence: Four T2I safety benchmarks across SD1.5, FLUX.2, and FLUX.1-dev backbones per reviews, with adversarial-prompt tests and ablations on joint correction and phase allocation.
X9uJh8tuow.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract is cut off after claiming state-of-the-art results across four T2I safety benchmarks)
X9uJh8tuow.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the multi-category problem is important, the KKT-based formulation is mathematically grounded, and attack success rate is lowest across benchmarks and backbones.
X9uJh8tuow.main_concern: The extra 2K network predictions per step are not benchmarked for cost, and each component is ablated on only one backbone with some baselines missing.

3ET06cnRrD.one_liner: Benchmarks LLM agents on installing and maintaining footholds across staged system disruptions with deterministic six-level scoring (L1-L6).
3ET06cnRrD.problem: Cybersecurity benchmarks stop at initial access, so whether LLM attackers can establish and maintain durable footholds across restarts and reboots is unmeasured.
3ET06cnRrD.method: Frames persistence as an adversarial survival task decoupled from upfront exploitation: agents use native host mechanisms to maintain footholds across staged disruptions, scored by deterministic checks. The benchmark has 203 core tasks in seven categories plus multi-host and active-defense extensions.
3ET06cnRrD.key_idea: Start evaluation after compromise and revoke access at staged disruptions, scoring prefix levels so failures localize between installation and persistence.
3ET06cnRrD.evidence: Evaluation of five frontier agents on 203 core tasks across seven categories, plus multi-host and defense-enabled extensions.
3ET06cnRrD.claimed_gains: Autonomous persistence success is 27.6%-44.8% across five frontier agents and drops to 5.5%-13.3% on defense-enabled tasks.
3ET06cnRrD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the post-compromise persistence gap is real and the benchmark has careful verification design (nonce rotation, deterministic checks) and diagnostic prefix scoring.
3ET06cnRrD.main_concern: The scaffold comparison drops refused tasks from some denominators, which can reverse the claimed scaffold improvement, and reviewers question whether persistence is a distinct capability.

JBZfiHVcpV.one_liner: Ranks CUTLASS kernels with learning-to-rank models over static estimates of induced hardware behavior, avoiding execution at selection time.
JBZfiHVcpV.problem: CUTLASS exposes tens of thousands of equivalent kernels per operation, making exhaustive autotuning expensive, while analytical selectors need hand-designed rules and learned selectors on raw parameters must infer hardware effects from data.
JBZfiHVcpV.method: Augments candidate kernel configurations with statically computable estimates of hardware behavior, builds a dataset of 4.9 million CUTLASS kernels, and trains gradient-boosted and neural learning-to-rank models to rank candidates within each problem.
JBZfiHVcpV.key_idea: Add statically computed hardware-behavior features to kernel configurations so rankers need not learn hardware consequences from raw parameters.
JBZfiHVcpV.evidence: Held-out exhaustive evaluation on a 4.9 million-kernel dataset, plus data-efficient cross-precision and epilogue-fusion transfer within CUTLASS GEMM and real deep-learning workloads (per the TL;DR).
JBZfiHVcpV.claimed_gains: Hardware-aware representations reduce selection regret by up to 40% relative to structural baselines and 64.2% relative to NVIDIA's matrix-multiply heuristics.
JBZfiHVcpV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it addresses a real systems problem, with a substantial measurement corpus, exhaustive evaluation, and well-motivated features that cut regret.
JBZfiHVcpV.main_concern: The advance over prior learned and hardware-feature approaches (AutoTVM, Ansor) is not isolated, and no end-to-end cost comparison shows execution-free selection beats measuring a few candidates.

0VBns61fh7.one_liner: Forecasts geostrophic currents via Helmholtz-decomposed components in dedicated branches, damping the divergent part at its observed decay rate.
0VBns61fh7.problem: Data-driven models learn the velocity field as a whole and roll out autoregressively, so they learn physically distinct components inaccurately and lose accuracy and stability at long horizons.
0VBns61fh7.method: HelmGeoNet embeds the Helmholtz decomposition into the network architecture so each physically distinct component is learned explicitly. A physics-guided relaxation mechanism damps the divergent component at its observed decay rate to limit error accumulation.
0VBns61fh7.key_idea: Decompose the velocity field by Helmholtz decomposition inside the network, forecast each component in its own branch, and damp the divergent component at its observed decay rate.
0VBns61fh7.evidence: Experiments on daily geostrophic currents against eight spatiotemporal backbones, evaluating current and eddy kinetic energy forecasts over long rollouts.
0VBns61fh7.claimed_gains: Outperforms eight spatiotemporal backbones; at the 20-day lead its eddy kinetic energy RMSE is 0.0029 m^2/s^2 lower than the best baseline.
0VBns61fh7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that embedding physical structure in the architecture (not only a physics loss) and the component-wise analysis give concrete motivation, with strong energy results over 20-day rollouts.
0VBns61fh7.main_concern: The Helmholtz exactness and orthogonality claims are hard to reconcile with a masked, latitude-weighted longitude-latitude grid and FFT-based inversion, so the physical interpretation outruns the numerical formulation.

UvYWl9Jxej.one_liner: Applies role-aware steering gates across selected LLM layers to keep untrusted data representations separate from trusted instructions.
UvYWl9Jxej.problem: Instruction-data separation is enforced through system controls or input-level role encoding, leaving its treatment during depth-wise hidden-state computation unspecified, so injected instructions in data can override the trusted task.
UvYWl9Jxej.method: Role-Conditioned Steering redirects data representations with continuous role-aware gates while leaving instruction representations unchanged. Depth-Aware Paths place the gates across layers, and Schedule Discovery selects a model-specific steering schedule on held-out data before final post-training.
UvYWl9Jxej.key_idea: Extend instruction-data separation from input embeddings to hidden states by steering data-token representations at multiple layers on a discovered, model-specific layer schedule.
UvYWl9Jxej.evidence: Experiments across five Llama and Qwen models (cut off in the abstract text provided); reviews cite ten ASIDE benchmarks, SEP, and StruQ attack-success comparisons.
UvYWl9Jxej.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract text is cut off after 'Experiments across five Llama and Qwen models').
UvYWl9Jxej.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree multi-layer steering clearly improves on embedding-only ASIDE in instruction-data separation and resistance to many prompt-injection attacks across five models and several benchmarks.
UvYWl9Jxej.main_concern: The added value of the selected layer schedule is not isolated from simple multi-layer rotation: random or regularly spaced schedules under matched tuning, and retained utility on task-relevant data, are not shown.

BGzM9s0G0J.one_liner: Video DeltaNet hybridizes local softmax attention with bidirectional linear memory using frame-wise delta updates for efficient video generation.
BGzM9s0G0J.problem: Attention over long spatiotemporal token sequences is the compute bottleneck of video diffusion denoising, and directly applying linear attention loses the fine-grained interactions needed for quality.
BGzM9s0G0J.method: VDN combines local softmax attention with a bidirectional linear memory branch built on Video Delta Attention (VDA), which jointly resolves correlated within-frame writes with a non-expansive inherited-state transition. Separate output projections and learnable gates calibrate the branches, a staged teacher-alignment recipe adds the pathway to pretrained models, and it is applied on MiniMax H3 for video-to-video interactions while text and audio keep softmax.
BGzM9s0G0J.key_idea: Jointly solve all within-frame token writes in a delta-rule linear memory (VDA) so correlated spatial tokens do not cause conflicting updates.
BGzM9s0G0J.evidence: Instantiated on MiniMax H3 with backbone speed measurements on B200 and H200 and 8-NFE distillation against the 50-NFE Dense H3 baseline; reviews cite Radial Attention as the main efficient baseline and an additive-update ablation.
BGzM9s0G0J.claimed_gains: 2.6x and 3.2x backbone speedups on B200 and H200, and a 14.3-second 768p video denoised in 6.70 seconds on eight B200 GPUs, a 14.5x speedup over the 50-NFE Dense H3 baseline.
BGzM9s0G0J.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the frame-wise joint delta update is well motivated for video and the reported speedups are strong.
BGzM9s0G0J.main_concern: Quality evidence is thin: there is no human evaluation, the efficient-attention baseline set is narrow (mainly Radial Attention), and the joint update beats a simpler additive update on only some metrics.

mg9hCSolvk.one_liner: D-Quant entropy-codes rotated, normalized KV-cache values into fixed-size per-token containers using a drift mechanism for parallel attention kernels.
mg9hCSolvk.problem: Fixed-width KV-cache quantization wastes bits on frequent central values and degrades quickly at low bit widths, while entropy coding's variable-length output does not suit highly parallel attention kernels.
mg9hCSolvk.method: After rotation and normalization KV values are near-normal, so D-Quant assigns shorter codewords to frequent symbols and uses a drift mechanism to pack variable-length streams into fixed-size containers that keep dequantization efficient; reviews describe a per-warp bisection search over candidate levels.
mg9hCSolvk.key_idea: Entropy coding decouples the number of quantization levels from bit width, and a drift mechanism repacks the variable-length output into fixed-size per-token storage.
mg9hCSolvk.evidence: Long-context accuracy results with a controlled comparison (output-distribution KL roughly halved on all 27 documents per model) and decoding throughput against a BF16 cache.
mg9hCSolvk.claimed_gains: not stated in the visible abstract; a review cites a 3.5x throughput gain over BF16 at different batch sizes.
mg9hCSolvk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that making entropy-coded KV storage fit fixed-size containers is a sound, well-motivated idea with strong long-context accuracy and practical decoding gains.
mg9hCSolvk.main_concern: The systems evaluation is incomplete: throughput is compared only against BF16 (not KIVI, TurboQuant, or KVComp), encoding and prefill overhead is unanalyzed, and the benefit of fixed-size storage over variable-length coding is not ablated.

kx7yD82L4r.one_liner: A waypoint policy and a flow-based action policy jointly learn structured exploration through trajectory-specific and action-specific reinforcement rewards.
kx7yD82L4r.problem: Low-level action perturbations inefficiently discover coordinated changes in high-level behavior for long-horizon manipulation.
kx7yD82L4r.method: TCoT-RL samples variable-length end-effector waypoint sequences and conditions a flow-based action policy on them. It jointly optimizes both policies using progress and endpoint feedback, separate group-relative advantages, and clipped GRPO objectives.
kx7yD82L4r.key_idea: Sample high-level waypoint trajectories and optimize trajectory and action policies with separate credit assignment and group-relative objectives.
kx7yD82L4r.evidence: Manipulation experiments include LIBERO-plus, reward-matched baselines, waypoint-count comparisons, trajectory interventions, and policy ablations.
kx7yD82L4r.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find trajectory-level exploration well motivated and recognize strong empirical results with useful controlled analyses.
kx7yD82L4r.main_concern: Reviewers find repeated-seed evidence insufficient to establish the reliability of the main performance differences.

zeW7c6yTGU.one_liner: Dynamic clustering of algorithm-response patterns guides specialized evolutionary search toward poorly served problem instances.
zeW7c6yTGU.problem: Optimizing average performance in LLM-assisted evolutionary search can leave difficult instance groups poorly served.
zeW7c6yTGU.method: DyCA reuses accumulated algorithm-instance evaluations to dynamically cluster instances without predefined features. The clusters define specialized search objectives, supported by weighted population management and bias-aware allocation of search resources.
zeW7c6yTGU.key_idea: Co-evolve instance clusters from algorithm-response patterns and allocate search effort to cluster-specific algorithm objectives.
zeW7c6yTGU.evidence: Experiments cover three combinatorial optimization tasks and a control task with heterogeneous instances, plus transfer to public benchmarks.
zeW7c6yTGU.claimed_gains: DyCA reports average improvements of 11.8% in tail robustness and 7.1% in overall performance while maintaining competitive head performance.
zeW7c6yTGU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the simple use of existing evaluation signals to discover instance structure and improve performance across varied tasks.
zeW7c6yTGU.main_concern: Reviewers question the methodological advance over existing specialist portfolios, clustering, and instance-weighting approaches.

aGeK6tj8ox.one_liner: Repeated comparison wins define policy-sampling Markov chains, while adaptive scheduling allocates feedback across prompts.
aGeK6tj8ox.problem: Limited pairwise-feedback budgets must serve prompts with different deployment importance and sampling difficulty without fitting reward models or parameterized policies.
aGeK6tj8ox.method: For fixed finite response pools, repeated pairwise wins accept Markov-chain proposals whose stationary distribution is a KL-regularized policy. An adaptive scheduler estimates local sampling difficulty and tracks a square-root allocation rule across prompts.
aGeK6tj8ox.key_idea: Use repeated-win acceptance for policy sampling and allocate comparisons according to deployment weights and estimated local sampling difficulty.
aGeK6tj8ox.evidence: Bradley-Terry analysis provides finite-sample and asymptotic guarantees, supported by a synthetic instance and 30 constructed SQLite questions.
aGeK6tj8ox.claimed_gains: At T global update rounds, the adaptive procedure achieves an expected aggregate objective gap of O(T^{-1/2}) and an O_p(T^{-1}) rate matching the oracle's order.
aGeK6tj8ox.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the comparison-based sampling construction and substantial theoretical analysis of the returned occupation policies.
aGeK6tj8ox.main_concern: Reviewers question the practical motivation and applicability of maintaining policies over fixed finite candidate responses.

JGDSwAFT0J.one_liner: A teacher samples promising recommendation lists using student reward-probability discrepancies and shares experiences through a replay buffer.
JGDSwAFT0J.problem: Generative listwise recommenders concentrate feedback on frequently sampled lists while potentially useful alternatives remain underexplored.
JGDSwAFT0J.method: Tesco trains a Teacher using the Student's reward-probability discrepancy together with list reward. Teacher and Student alternate sampling and share a replay buffer so the Student learns beyond its current distribution.
JGDSwAFT0J.key_idea: Mix student discrepancy with list reward to train an exploration teacher that supplies additional trajectories through shared replay.
JGDSwAFT0J.evidence: Experiments use three real-world recommendation datasets in simulated online and offline settings, including reward-only and discrepancy-only ablations.
JGDSwAFT0J.claimed_gains: Tesco reports average-reward gains of up to 4.5%.
JGDSwAFT0J.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the exploration problem and find an auxiliary discrepancy-guided sampling policy a reasonable fit for listwise recommendation.
JGDSwAFT0J.main_concern: Reviewers question whether training discrepancy reliably identifies underexploration and whether the motivation is supported by sufficient evidence.

E2hFunZ8f2.one_liner: A bounded reward-dependent correction reweights a frozen reference language model toward the KL-regularized RLVR optimum.
E2hFunZ8f2.problem: Practical sample-based RLVR can deviate from its KL-regularized optimum and concentrate on a narrow subset of successful solutions.
E2hFunZ8f2.method: RAPC derives the Gibbs-reweighted reference optimum and learns a bounded process-level correction from terminal verifier feedback. The acting policy combines this learned correction with the frozen reference distribution.
E2hFunZ8f2.key_idea: Freeze the reference policy and learn a bounded prefix-level reward correction that reweights its next-token distribution.
E2hFunZ8f2.evidence: Reasoning benchmarks with 4B and 7B models compare against full-parameter GRPO, entropy-regularized GRPO, and Q-sharp while examining Gibbs structure and solution coverage.
E2hFunZ8f2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value testing RLVR against its own theoretical optimum and connecting reference-policy reweighting to practical correction learning.
E2hFunZ8f2.main_concern: Reviewers argue that the training objective does not guarantee calibrated reference-success estimates or the claimed Gibbs consistency.

kYTTgXnZXl.one_liner: Joint geometry-latent flow matching generates RNA scaffolds and residue latents before decoding all heavy atoms.
kYTTgXnZXl.problem: RNA sequence-structure co-design must coordinate global folding with nucleotide detail despite limited structural supervision.
kYTTgXnZXl.method: La-Ribo combines a sparse phosphate-sugar-base scaffold with residue-wise latents encoding nucleotide identity and local conformation. A shared flow network generates both, and an RNA-specific decoder reconstructs heavy atoms using an expanded structural corpus.
kYTTgXnZXl.key_idea: Jointly flow-match explicit RNA scaffold coordinates and residue-wise identity-conformation latents, then decode the combined representation into heavy atoms.
kYTTgXnZXl.evidence: Evaluations use a corpus of 168,561 RNA structures, multiple sampling budgets, two refolding models, representation and data ablations, and scaffold-conditioned inverse folding.
kYTTgXnZXl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the curated RNA structural corpus and supporting experiments for the geometry-latent representation.
kYTTgXnZXl.main_concern: A principal concern is the limited methodological distinction from La-Proteina's joint geometry-latent framework.

o6aUM1NGpB.one_liner: Private residual modules at interfaces and internal layers personalize a frozen federated core for heterogeneous visual world models.
o6aUM1NGpB.problem: Federated visual world models must share experience while accommodating client differences in appearance and dynamics.
o6aUM1NGpB.method: FedWM first learns a shared prediction core through parameter averaging, then freezes it. Clients train private residual modules at interfaces and internal layers using each backbone's native prediction objective.
o6aUM1NGpB.key_idea: Federate a shared core, freeze it, and locally train private residuals at both model interfaces and internal layers.
o6aUM1NGpB.evidence: DINO-WM and NanoWM evaluations span PushT, PointMaze, Wall, and Rope with three training seeds, capacity controls, client-scaling studies, and PushT planning tests.
o6aUM1NGpB.claimed_gains: Across five paired planning seeds on frozen personalized PushT tasks, FedWM reports 71.54% success versus 68.46%.
o6aUM1NGpB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the heterogeneous world-model setting, evaluation across two backbones, and controls examining personalization capacity and placement.
o6aUM1NGpB.main_concern: Reviewers find the advance over existing personalized federated learning insufficiently established by the interface-only baseline.

xLPmPvbfVX.one_liner: Survey-grounded risky user requests paired with Android device-state verification benchmark blind obedience versus refusal in VLM mobile agents.
xLPmPvbfVX.problem: Mobile-agent safety evaluations focus on external prompt injections and manipulated UIs while overlooking harmful real-world consequences caused by faithfully executing a user's own risk-sensitive requests.
xLPmPvbfVX.method: Distilling a 2,240-user smartphone survey into twelve harm domains, SafeDroid evaluates mobile agents on risk-sensitive user requests with automated device-state verification. The benchmark separates reaching the risky target state, sustained refusal, and capability failure while checking whether reasoning traces identify the specific consequence.
xLPmPvbfVX.key_idea: Verify final device states on survey-derived risk-sensitive user requests to separate blind target execution, deliberate refusal, and capability failure alongside consequence recognition in mobile agents.
xLPmPvbfVX.evidence: Grounded in a 2,240-user questionnaire across twelve harm domains and evaluated on eleven general-purpose VLMs and five specialized GUI models including Mobile-Agent-v3.
xLPmPvbfVX.claimed_gains: As single agents, general-purpose VLMs reach risk-sensitive target device states in 58.3% of runs without external manipulation, and 93.6% of those trajectories never identify the specific consequence.
xLPmPvbfVX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that shifting safety evaluation to legitimate user-initiated requests fills an important gap and praise device-state verification for distinguishing deliberate refusal from capability failure.
xLPmPvbfVX.main_concern: Reviewers question harm-label reliability and normative definitions—pointing to unreported inter-annotator agreement, author-framed prompts built from only 17 base tasks, and cases where informed user confirmation rather than refusal is appropriate.

2thSEij0ZC.one_liner: Krylov-dimensional contexts compress fixed-policy temporal-difference iterates with characterized accuracy limits and attention-based realizations.
2thSEij0ZC.problem: Theoretical in-context reinforcement-learning constructions often require memory that grows with the number of sampled transitions.
2thSEij0ZC.method: The analysis identifies the Krylov dimension as the minimum context dimension for reproducing the first L fixed-policy TD iterates with a shared linear decoder. It characterizes approximation below that dimension and retained memory for continuous representations, with linear- and softmax-attention realizations.
2thSEij0ZC.key_idea: Compress sampled TD dynamics into their Krylov subspace so context size follows the iterate span rather than the trajectory length.
2thSEij0ZC.evidence: Lower bounds, explicit attention-based encoders and executors, and sampled-task experiments support the context, approximation, and memory results.
2thSEij0ZC.claimed_gains: On a sampled task with full exact rank but small numerical rank, a context accurate to 10^{-2} is 96.4% smaller than TD's sparse sufficient statistics.
2thSEij0ZC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the rigorous characterization of context and memory requirements and experiments supporting the theoretical results.
2thSEij0ZC.main_concern: Reviewers question practical generality because the construction targets fixed-policy evaluation and does not establish applicability to changing policies or broader reinforcement learning.

E6MRXk805b.one_liner: ElectrolyteMD-Bench audits autonomous simulation studies across solvation regimes for scientific validity, evidence integrity, and calibrated completion claims.
E6MRXk805b.problem: Successfully running molecular dynamics software does not establish that autonomous agents can complete scientifically reliable electrolyte studies.
E6MRXk805b.method: ElectrolyteMD-Bench tasks agents with construction, equilibration, production sampling, property analysis, and cross-system interpretation across three electrolyte regimes. It audits simulation validity, analysis validity, evidence integrity, and outcome calibration while agents decide whether to correct, sample further, or stop.
E6MRXk805b.key_idea: Evaluate the entire electrolyte research process against linked physical and evidentiary requirements instead of treating trajectory generation as study completion.
E6MRXk805b.evidence: Eight model-harness configurations conduct comparative studies spanning dilute, high-concentration, and localized high-concentration electrolytes, producing 24 system runs.
E6MRXk805b.claimed_gains: All 24 system runs produce valid production trajectories, but none of the eight studies satisfy all scientific requirements.
E6MRXk805b.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value end-to-end scientific evaluation that checks physical definitions, analysis consistency, and statistical support beyond software execution.
E6MRXk805b.main_concern: A reviewer questions retrospective grading changes, including whether a specific transference-number convention was clearly required by the original task.

6TKGZzPWUZ.one_liner: SceneLM maintains a textual 3D object map by predicting add, edit, and remove operations from images and current state.
6TKGZzPWUZ.problem: Open-vocabulary scene mapping relies on engineered association pipelines and feature-rich persistent memories that increase storage and complexity.
6TKGZzPWUZ.method: SceneLM uses a structured text list of objects as its only persistent scene memory and updates that list for each input image. Iterative map-maintenance supervision comes from an automatic image-annotation pipeline without human training labels.
6TKGZzPWUZ.key_idea: Treat persistent scene mapping as predicting textual object insertion, correction, and removal operations over the current map.
6TKGZzPWUZ.evidence: Language-grounded retrieval and localization benchmarks compare SceneLM with complete mapping systems, with reviews noting supervision and map-update ablations.
6TKGZzPWUZ.claimed_gains: SceneLM reports competitive retrieval and localization performance with a scene representation that is 6-12x more compact.
6TKGZzPWUZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate compact textual map maintenance and the scalable automatically generated supervision for object updates.
6TKGZzPWUZ.main_concern: A reviewer finds the methodological advance over EPM's textual entity memory and Add/Update/Remove operations insufficiently established.

MJSfLMaLEu.one_liner: Pace3D monitors decoded structural progress and rewinds sampling time while retaining latents when target support remains incomplete.
MJSfLMaLEu.problem: Fixed sampling endpoints can leave incomplete sparse structures that later feature-generation stages cannot repair.
MJSfLMaLEu.method: Pace3D compares decoded structure with a target-conditioned reference phase and rewinds the sampling clock while retaining the current latent when progress lags. Source Alignment stabilizes extended trajectories, and Cross-Condition Consensus preserves unchanged source features.
MJSfLMaLEu.key_idea: Use the structure decoder as an online progress sensor and rewind time without resetting the latent when structural completion falls behind.
MJSfLMaLEu.evidence: Structural-lag diagnostics and Eval3DEdit evaluations include qualitative and quantitative comparisons, ablations, and an equal-wall-clock comparison with Nano3D noted in reviews.
MJSfLMaLEu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the structural-progress versus sampling-time mismatch well motivated and adaptive intervention practically useful.
MJSfLMaLEu.main_concern: Reviewers find insufficient direct measurement of structural completion after applying Pace3D because semantic and perceptual scores do not establish completed edits.

hH660RERb2.one_liner: JEPIA trains embeddings through analytically fitted rotations and reflections to infer unseen programs from input-output examples.
hH660RERb2.problem: Program induction needs representations that support inferring programs absent from training using only a few input-output examples.
hH660RERb2.method: JEPIA encodes input-output examples and analytically fits a rotation or reflection between their embeddings. Prediction errors on further inputs train the shared encoder through the fitting procedure, with regularization preventing embedding collapse.
hH660RERb2.key_idea: Train the encoder through a context-fitted transformation so representation geometry supports the same program-inference procedure at evaluation.
hH660RERb2.evidence: Modular addition produces ordered ring embeddings, and cube-transformation experiments transfer from two-move training programs to shorter and longer sequences.
hH660RERb2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find learning representations that reduce program induction to simple transformation fitting interesting and potentially useful.
hH660RERb2.main_concern: Reviewers find broader generalization insufficiently established because evaluations favor the geometric inductive bias and lack key comparator controls.

dXqMUjWpme.one_liner: Skill-π distills reusable multimodal reasoning skills and jointly updates the skill library and policy with stage-specific credit assignment.
dXqMUjWpme.problem: Trajectory-based self-improvement repeatedly consumes sample-specific experience while persistently unsolved examples contribute little reusable knowledge.
dXqMUjWpme.method: Skill-π uses one multimodal policy for skill selection, use, and evolution, assigning learning signals according to each stage's downstream consequences. Newly recovered successful experience updates both the parametric policy and reusable skill library over successive rounds.
dXqMUjWpme.key_idea: Separate credit for selecting, using, and evolving reusable skills, then feed recovered successes into both policy training and library updates.
dXqMUjWpme.evidence: Reviews describe GRPO-based comparisons and analyses of recovered samples, skill dynamics, negative transfer, and computational cost.
dXqMUjWpme.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value reusable cross-sample experience and stage-specific credit assignment as a direction for multimodal self-improvement.
dXqMUjWpme.main_concern: Reviewers find the skill framework's contribution insufficiently isolated because matched no-skill reinforcement-learning and unguided-resampling controls are missing.

nnSoftSyDp.one_liner: Progressive n-gram hash keys select shallow MoE experts while learned scores weight their contributions.
nnSoftSyDp.problem: Token-ID hashing routes every occurrence identically, ignoring context and potentially concentrating frequent-token traffic on particular experts.
nnSoftSyDp.method: ProGram hashes ordered local n-grams using multiple primes, stable deduplication, and fallback probing. It applies routing orders (1, 2, 3) across the first three MoE layers, retaining learned mixture weights and deeper top-K routing.
nnSoftSyDp.key_idea: Increase hash-key context from unigrams to trigrams across shallow layers while learning weights over deterministically selected experts.
nnSoftSyDp.evidence: A 5B-parameter MoE with 412M active parameters per token trains on approximately 100B tokens and undergoes evaluation on 12 knowledge, reasoning, and code benchmarks.
nnSoftSyDp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the clear motivation and simple depth-aware routing-key design.
nnSoftSyDp.main_concern: Ablations and expert analyses do not isolate progressive context expansion from other routing changes or verify the claimed specialization mechanism.

wsUChp8h8H.one_liner: An inner planning loop and cross-novel policy revision generate source-grounded recap videos within a viewing-time budget.
wsUChp8h8H.problem: Novel-to-video recaps require causal story compression, narration timing, and generated visuals without relying on existing film footage.
wsUChp8h8H.method: ReVi's inner multi-agent loop plans story content, narration duration, and shots before generation. Across novels, an outer loop revises both the editing policy and the meta-policy governing its revision.
wsUChp8h8H.key_idea: Plan content, narration timing, and shots within each novel, then recursively revise editing and revision policies across novels.
wsUChp8h8H.evidence: Experiments use two evaluation sets, representative baselines, human ratings, and multi-round improvement measurements.
wsUChp8h8H.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the task's practical motivation and the clear decomposition of narrative, timing, and visual planning.
wsUChp8h8H.main_concern: Baseline comparisons do not establish the direct approach's advantage under equivalent duration controls, repair budgets, and alternative pipelines.

V17rbeVQBV.one_liner: Local back-projection tokens and angle-conditioned self-attention predict missing CT views across acquisition geometries.
V17rbeVQBV.problem: Protocol-specific reconstruction models can require retraining when projection angles, counts, detector dimensions, or data distributions change.
V17rbeVQBV.method: TomoTransformer tokenizes local filtered projections in a spatially separated back-projection space. Self-attention predicts missing views at queried angles, allowing variable inputs and detector dimensions within one architecture.
V17rbeVQBV.key_idea: Represent local filtered projections as tokens in back-projection space and use attention to predict views at queried angles.
V17rbeVQBV.evidence: Training spans medical CT anatomies and natural images, with sparse-view benchmarks, variable-view LoDoPaB-CT evaluation, and zero-shot nanoscale brain tomography.
V17rbeVQBV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the geometric reconstruction design and promising results in the evaluated settings.
V17rbeVQBV.main_concern: Limited view-count, angular-sampling, noise, and transfer tests do not establish the claimed breadth of acquisition generalization.

E4FYfedKmz.one_liner: Digit-conditioned probabilities and binary cross-entropy supervise numerical token learning without numerical-distance penalties.
E4FYfedKmz.problem: Standard language-model likelihood ignores numerical structure, while distance-based losses can over-sharpen or over-flatten digit distributions.
E4FYfedKmz.method: DEL reframes numerical losses through criterion and distance terms, then uses digit conditional probabilities and binary cross-entropy for supervised entropy optimization. It omits numerical-distance penalties and extends the objective to decimals and decimal points.
E4FYfedKmz.key_idea: Use digit-conditioned probabilities and binary cross-entropy to supervise numerical predictions while removing distance-based penalties.
E4FYfedKmz.evidence: Reviews describe five configurations across four model families on mathematics and code tasks, with three-run averages and variability.
E4FYfedKmz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit consistent empirical improvements and the analysis of existing numerical-learning losses.
E4FYfedKmz.main_concern: Missing digit-weighted cross-entropy and simpler digit-loss controls leave DEL's specific mechanism unseparated from extra numerical supervision.

BPVtZ8KxVc.one_liner: Checkpoint and tool-interaction evaluations trace clinical agents' use of evidence through patient-state judgments and actions.
BPVtZ8KxVc.problem: Final-outcome clinical benchmarks obscure failures in evidence use, state updating, and action selection over time.
BPVtZ8KxVc.method: WARD pairs a Longitudinal Track with controlled cumulative evidence and an Interactive Track for tool-mediated management. It evaluates evidence recognition, patient-state judgments, actions, and progress through reference transitions.
BPVtZ8KxVc.key_idea: Evaluate linked evidence, state judgments, and actions at longitudinal checkpoints and during tool-mediated reference transitions.
BPVtZ8KxVc.evidence: WARD includes 4,560 tasks, 240 checkpoints, 40 trajectories, and 95 hospitalizations, evaluating 12 models with scorable outputs.
BPVtZ8KxVc.claimed_gains: The abstract reports linked-evidence nonresponse of 74.47–90.90% and only 11.46% of executed actions advancing a reference transition.
BPVtZ8KxVc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the longitudinal clinical dataset and process-level distinction between judgments and executed actions.
BPVtZ8KxVc.main_concern: Metric definitions and differences in task difficulty confound evidence-linking errors with downstream clinical prediction errors.

aQeAttwdAg.one_liner: Chemically anchored candidate frames preserve orientation ambiguity for non-equivariant 3D molecular generation.
aQeAttwdAg.problem: Single-frame canonicalization can become unstable when molecular geometry does not determine a unique orientation.
aQeAttwdAg.method: AnchorSet estimates poses using chemical-scaffold priors and learned atom-type weights. It retains a compact set of symmetry-equivalent frames under proper signed permutations when orientation remains ambiguous, allowing non-equivariant generation in canonical coordinates.
aQeAttwdAg.key_idea: Estimate chemically anchored poses and preserve unresolved orientation ambiguity as a set of symmetry-equivalent proper-rotation frames.
aQeAttwdAg.evidence: Experiments on QM9 and GEOM-Drugs compare non-equivariant and equivariant generators, with fixed-backbone canonicalization comparisons.
aQeAttwdAg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit set-valued canonicalization as a useful alternative to single-frame alignment and report competitive generation quality.
aQeAttwdAg.main_concern: Design choices and ablations do not isolate candidate-set benefits from scaffold anchoring, learned weights, and frame-selection heuristics.

NZKLQFSo2k.one_liner: Coupled base-and-sugar SE(3) flows jointly generate RNA sequences and structures with two frames per nucleotide.
