NZKLQFSo2k.problem: A single nucleotide frame trades off preserving base interactions against reconstructing the sugar-phosphate backbone.
NZKLQFSo2k.method: DuetRNA models coupled base and sugar frames through SE(3) flow matching for joint RNA sequence–structure generation. A frame analysis motivates using separate coordinate systems for complementary nucleotide geometry.
NZKLQFSo2k.key_idea: Run coupled SE(3) flow matching over separate base-centered and sugar-centered frames for each nucleotide.
NZKLQFSo2k.evidence: Analysis covers seven frame constructions, 11,497 RNA chains, and 31,432 base interactions, followed by inverse-folded and generated-sequence evaluations and ablations.
NZKLQFSo2k.claimed_gains: The abstract reports scTM-validity improvements of 7.67 and 4.33 percentage points over matched baselines under IF and GS, respectively.
NZKLQFSo2k.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the geometric motivation and controlled evidence that dual frames help the implemented model.
NZKLQFSo2k.main_concern: Missing stronger single-frame controls with compatible decoders leave the necessity of independently generated dual frames unresolved.

E0vWmfa2tF.one_liner: Teacher prompt filtering and student frequency interventions target domain-sensitive knowledge in remote-sensing segmentation distillation.
E0vWmfa2tF.problem: Source-domain distillation can transfer teacher sensitivities and encourage student shortcuts that fail under deployment shifts.
E0vWmfa2tF.method: CKD learns prompts that suppress domain-sensitive teacher responses before distillation. A student-side frequency intervention perturbs inputs to discourage domain-related shortcuts, and the framework supports different distillation objectives.
E0vWmfa2tF.key_idea: Filter domain-sensitive teacher representations with learned prompts and intervene on student input frequencies during distillation.
E0vWmfa2tF.evidence: Reviews describe experiments across eight degradation types, multiple configurations, and several distillation objectives, primarily using synthetic shifts.
E0vWmfa2tF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the distinction between teacher-side knowledge filtering and student-side shortcut learning.
E0vWmfa2tF.main_concern: Comparisons do not sufficiently distinguish CKD from existing frequency-filtering and augmentation approaches.

DRCDoanOvH.one_liner: Post-trains promptable segmentation models by aligning mask predictions across varied prompts for the same object toward the highest-IoU prediction.
DRCDoanOvH.problem: Promptable segmentation models like SAM are sensitive to prompt variations, producing degraded or inconsistent masks when users click different locations or phrase text prompts differently for the same object.
DRCDoanOvH.method: Best-Teaches-Rest (BTR) groups diverse spatial or text prompts referring to the same target object, selects the prediction achieving the highest ground-truth IoU as the teacher, and trains the remaining prompt predictions to align with the teacher mask while applying ground-truth supervision only to the teacher. The objective applies across click, text, and joint click-text variations.
DRCDoanOvH.key_idea: Supervises only the highest-IoU mask among multiple prompts for the same object with ground truth while training all other prompt variations for that object to match the best mask.
DRCDoanOvH.evidence: Evaluated by post-training SAM 3 on EntitySeg and testing zero-shot transfer across six object-centric instance segmentation datasets (including LVIS) and real-user clicks.
DRCDoanOvH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that improving mask stability across equivalent user prompts is a practical problem and that BTR consistently improves spatial prompt robustness across datasets.
DRCDoanOvH.main_concern: Methodological novelty over standard multi-prompt consistency regularization and augmented SFT is modest, and aligning prompts degrades noun-phrase text-prompt performance on LVIS while potentially suppressing valid part-level granularity.

fDWkoNKQ9E.one_liner: Builds an aligned composite-background-foreground video triplet dataset to train a dual-branch diffusion model for layered video insertion and decomposition.
fDWkoNKQ9E.problem: Video editing models lack explicit RGBA foreground layer representations and aligned triplet supervision that capture both foreground objects and their associated visual effects like shadows and reflections.
fDWkoNKQ9E.method: The authors construct TriLayer, a dataset of aligned composite, background, and effect-inclusive RGBA foreground video triplets. Using TriLayer, they train DBL-Diffusion, a dual-branch diffusion framework with cross-branch interaction during denoising that jointly models scene RGB video and RGBA foreground layers for object insertion (DBL-Insert) and layer decomposition (DBL-Decompose).
fDWkoNKQ9E.key_idea: Jointly denoises scene-level RGB video and effect-inclusive RGBA foreground layers via cross-branch diffusion interaction supervised by aligned composite-background-foreground video triplets.
fDWkoNKQ9E.evidence: Evaluated on a 65-video test split from the 3,908-triplet TriLayer dataset across video object insertion and video layer decomposition tasks.
fDWkoNKQ9E.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that explicitly modeling RGBA foreground layers together with shadows and reflections via aligned composite-background-foreground video triplets addresses an important gap in layered video editing.
fDWkoNKQ9E.main_concern: Quantitative evaluation is restricted to 65 in-distribution test videos without independent alpha/effect separation metrics, and qualitative supplementary videos exhibit visual artifacts such as boundary flickering and black holes.

qsD3EOuW8Q.one_liner: Schedules environment-task pairs for agentic RL by propagating historical reward variance across a dual-relation environment-and-task graph.
qsD3EOuW8Q.problem: Multi-turn rollout generation and verification across executable environments in agentic reinforcement learning are computationally expensive, requiring data scheduling that accounts for shared environment tools, states, and verifiers under finite rollout budgets.
qsD3EOuW8Q.method: EnvSched models environment-task pairs as nodes in a dual-relation graph connecting tasks within the same environment by shared tools, states, and verifiers, and across environments by abstract execution and reward topology. It propagates historical rollout statistics along both edge types to predict within-task reward variance and allocates rollout batches by balancing high-variance exploitation with coverage quotas across underobserved environments.
qsD3EOuW8Q.key_idea: Propagates rollout reward statistics over a dual-relation graph of within-environment tool/state structure and cross-environment execution topology to schedule high-variance and under-covered environment-task pairs.
qsD3EOuW8Q.evidence: Evaluated with GRPO on Qwen3-Thinking checkpoints (1.7B and 8B) using the EnvScaler training pool across BFCL-v3, tau-Bench, and ACEBench-Agent.
qsD3EOuW8Q.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that treating the environment-task pair as the scheduling unit and leveraging graph structure to balance reward-variance exploitation with environment coverage is well suited for budget-constrained agentic RL.
qsD3EOuW8Q.main_concern: The experimental evaluation only compares against uniform random task selection rather than standard non-graph bandit or UCB schedulers, and omits an intermediate SFT stage, leading to performance drops on ACEBench-Agent.

d2E282Qi0a.one_liner: Benchmarks multi-agent adaptation across 1,400 evolving customer-service episodes and introduces a parameter-free experience-refining framework.
d2E282Qi0a.problem: LLM agents are typically evaluated on isolated tasks in static environments, failing to measure or support continuous adaptation when domain policies, user populations, and operational objectives shift across episodes.
d2E282Qi0a.method: The authors introduce DynaWorld, a dynamic multimodal benchmark of 1,400 customer-service interaction episodes across eight long-horizon scenarios linked by scheduled environmental shifts. They also propose DynEvo, a training-free self-evolving multi-agent framework that updates externalized memory and strategies across episodes using environmental feedback.
d2E282Qi0a.key_idea: Connects multi-turn multimodal evaluation episodes via scheduled policy, user, and objective shifts while updating externalized multi-agent strategy memory between episodes from environmental feedback.
d2E282Qi0a.evidence: Evaluated across eight long-horizon customer-service scenarios (1,400 episodes) in DynaWorld against standard LLM agents and workflow/prompt-optimization baselines (DSPy, EvoAgentX, AutoAgents).
d2E282Qi0a.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that linking evaluation episodes through controlled shifts in policies, user populations, and objectives provides a valuable benchmark for studying cross-episode agent degradation and recovery.
d2E282Qi0a.main_concern: DynEvo uses the judge-computed evaluation metric (Overall Score) directly as its inter-episode feedback signal without giving baselines equivalent feedback, and omits comparisons against actual cross-episode memory baselines like ExpeL or Mem0.

Gf4dfX40D4.one_liner: Routes audio-visual cues into text-referenced and text-residual pathways with final-block migration supervision for frozen-LLM multimodal affective computing.
Gf4dfX40D4.problem: When audio-visual affective representations are injected into a frozen language-centered LLM, the model can reinforce its text-directed prior and ignore contradictory non-textual evidence.
Gf4dfX40D4.method: Text-Bounded Incremental Evidence Migration (TIE) uses textual semantics and text-bounded temporal routing to separate audio and visual features into text-referenced and text-residual pathways before projecting them into the frozen LLM. It applies an auxiliary migration loss derived from the frozen final prediction block along with an order-aware objective for sentiment regression.
Gf4dfX40D4.key_idea: Decomposes audio-visual signals into text-aligned and text-residual pathways and supervises their survival through a frozen LLM using an auxiliary readout loss at the final prediction block.
Gf4dfX40D4.evidence: Evaluated across five benchmarks (three multimodal sentiment analysis and two emotion recognition datasets, including CH-SIMS v2.0, CMU-MOSEI, and CHERMA) across three LLM backbones and five seeds.
Gf4dfX40D4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that investigating whether non-textual evidence survives propagation through a frozen LLM is well motivated and appreciate the multi-dataset, multi-seed evaluation and transferability of the training objectives.
Gf4dfX40D4.main_concern: Diagnostic analyses in the paper's own appendix fail to confirm that text suppresses non-textual evidence or that TIE reduces text-directed shifts, and performance gains outside CH-SIMS v2.0 are negligible or negative relative to PaP.

C4GSlDsBY1.one_liner: Organizes multi-turn agent rollouts as sparse reverse trees and optimizes turn-level policy updates in reverse temporal order with on-policy continuations.
C4GSlDsBY1.problem: Multi-turn agentic reinforcement learning suffers from training instability due to rollout-training context mismatch, coarse credit assignment under sparse terminal rewards, and asynchronous policy drift across trajectory depths.
C4GSlDsBY1.method: Reverse-Turn Policy Optimization (RTPO) structures multi-turn trajectories as sparse reverse trees and updates the policy at the turn level from the final turn backward to the initial turn. At each turn, it uses state-matched sibling rollouts for localized credit assignment and regenerates downstream continuations on-policy so earlier turns are optimized against updated continuation policies.
C4GSlDsBY1.key_idea: Updates multi-turn agent policies backward from terminal turns to initial turns on a sparse branching tree while regenerating downstream continuations with the newly updated policy at each step.
C4GSlDsBY1.evidence: Supported by theoretical bias, drift, and convergence analyses and empirical evaluations on multi-turn mathematical reasoning, knowledge-intensive QA, and agentic benchmarks (including tau^3-Airline).
C4GSlDsBY1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that addressing turn-level credit assignment, context mismatch, and policy drift via state-matched sibling rollouts and on-policy continuations is clearly formulated and well motivated.
C4GSlDsBY1.main_concern: Experiments do not directly ablate reverse-order updates against forward- or random-order updates under the same tree credit assignment and context preservation, leaving the specific necessity of reverse ordering unverified.

av2UkkRkRg.one_liner: Selectively encodes extended visual history near turns and stops and compresses multi-frame tokens for onboard aerial vision-language navigation.
av2UkkRkRg.problem: Large multimodal aerial VLN models are too heavy for onboard UAV execution, while uniformly extending visual history length increases action prediction error during non-critical straight motion.
av2UkkRkRg.method: Motivated by a 490,090-decision analysis showing extra visual frames help near turns and stops but hurt during cruising, AdaFly pairs a 545M-parameter policy with an Adaptive Temporal History Selector that decides when to encode older frames before action-chunk generation. A Context-Conditioned Temporal Memory Compressor then condenses the selected four-frame history from 144 visual tokens into 16 task-relevant memory tokens.
av2UkkRkRg.key_idea: Predicts upcoming turn or stop regimes to conditionally expand visual history from two to four frames and compresses historical visual tokens into 16 context-conditioned memory tokens.
av2UkkRkRg.evidence: Analyzed over 490,090 navigation decisions and evaluated on a 12-scene subset of pre-release Open-FlyV2 alongside onboard UAV deployment latency tests.
av2UkkRkRg.claimed_gains: Extending history from two to four observations reduces action error by 12.29% near turns/stops but increases it by 2.72% elsewhere; AdaFly achieves a 44.94% navigation success rate (a 69.0% relative improvement over a baseline) while compressing four-frame history from 144 to 16 tokens (88.9% reduction).
av2UkkRkRg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the 490k-decision paired analysis showing regime-dependent temporal history utility is compelling and motivates a lightweight onboard architecture.
av2UkkRkRg.main_concern: Gains fail to transfer to unseen scenes (26.89% vs. 27.67% for AeroVLA), adaptive selection yields only a modest +1.72% gain over fixed four-frame history, and key benchmarks/baselines (AeroBrain, OmniNav, DualVLN) lack bibliography citations.

STZnKcijxq.one_liner: Introduces an expert-validated benchmark of 1,092 questions over 799 simulation-grounded optoelectronic device figures to evaluate vision-language models.
STZnKcijxq.problem: Existing scientific figure benchmarks do not evaluate whether vision-language models can read optoelectronic device schematics and characterization plots or connect visual patterns to device physics.
STZnKcijxq.method: OptoFig compiles 1,092 questions across 799 optoelectronic figures spanning circuit schematics, device structures, spectra, mode profiles, and timing diagrams across 39 task types grouped into perception, quantitative reading, and physical/functional reasoning. Every reference answer is grounded in direct figure measurements, simulator/script records, or domain-expert annotation with multi-stage verification.
STZnKcijxq.key_idea: Constructs a simulation- and script-grounded visual QA benchmark over optoelectronic device schematics and performance plots spanning perception, quantitative extraction, and physical reasoning.
STZnKcijxq.evidence: Evaluated across seven vision-language models on 1,092 questions over 799 optoelectronic figures.
STZnKcijxq.claimed_gains: Across seven evaluated VLMs, overall accuracy ranges from 54.2% to 74.5%, with average accuracy 10.2 points lower on hard items than on easy ones.
STZnKcijxq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that grounding answers in simulator records and expert validation across optoelectronic design and characterization figures creates a high-quality domain-specific benchmark.
STZnKcijxq.main_concern: The dataset is heavily skewed toward template-generated electrical questions (66%) with only 128 (~12%) physical and functional reasoning items, and models are evaluated with reasoning disabled or minimized.

2G1htR22YW.one_liner: Jointly routes and schedules LLM queries using implicit user retrial feedback modeled via contextual queueing bandits with multinomial logit preferences.
2G1htR22YW.problem: Online LLM routing and queue scheduling systems rarely account for queue congestion caused by dissatisfied users retrying queries or the user-experience cost of requesting explicit ratings.
2G1htR22YW.method: The authors formulate Contextual Queueing Bandits with Multinomial Logit feedback (CQB-MNL) to infer user satisfaction implicitly from query retrial behavior while tracking server queue dynamics. Their anytime algorithm (ACQB) combines Thompson sampling with decaying arrival-triggered forced exploration, enhanced in practice with contrastively refined query embeddings and disjoint LLM-specific parameters.
2G1htR22YW.key_idea: Infers implicit user satisfaction from query retrials within a contextual multinomial-logit queueing bandit that pairs Thompson sampling with decaying forced exploration to stabilize server queues.
2G1htR22YW.evidence: Supported by theoretical cumulative and queue-length regret bounds and experiments on synthetic queues and offline replay simulations derived from WildChat-1M.
2G1htR22YW.claimed_gains: ACQB achieves a cumulative routing regret of \widetilde{O}(\sqrt{t}) and a queue-length regret of \widetilde{O}(t^{-1/4}) for large t.
2G1htR22YW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that coupling LLM query routing with queue scheduling and implicit retrial feedback addresses a realistic operational challenge in conversational LLM serving.
2G1htR22YW.main_concern: Assumption 2 in the theoretical analysis is mathematically violated when parameter norms grow unbounded in unconstrained MLE, and Thompson sampling is used despite the text noting UCB yields tighter regret bounds.

XcRdr4xog5.one_liner: Refines corrupted scene text in generated images via four-step MeanFlow grouped pixel-space generation of target text regions.
XcRdr4xog5.problem: Text-to-image generators frequently produce illegible small text and complex characters, while VAE-based latent refiners lose fine glyph strokes during reconstruction and full-image editing shifts background colors.
XcRdr4xog5.method: PixText formulates local scene-text refinement as grouped image generation directly in pixel space conditioned on the original image, generating only the target text regions to leave backgrounds untouched. It uses MeanFlow with uniform timestep sampling and multi-depth OCR feature supervision to enable four-step pixel-space generation, and introduces Text Refinement Bench for evaluation.
XcRdr4xog5.key_idea: Generates grouped local text crops directly in pixel space using a four-step MeanFlow trajectory conditioned on the unedited full image to avoid VAE stroke degradation and background color drift.
XcRdr4xog5.evidence: Evaluated on the newly introduced Text Refinement Bench against baselines including FLUX-Text.
XcRdr4xog5.claimed_gains: On Text Refinement Bench, PixText achieves 83.06% glyph pass and 94.66% exact target-character OCR accuracy versus 56.03% and 83.43% for the strongest baseline, while its four-step MeanFlow variant retains 81.84% pass rate in under one GPU-second per image.
XcRdr4xog5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that generating localized text regions directly in pixel space avoids VAE reconstruction loss on fine strokes and preserves unedited backgrounds with strong OCR accuracy gains.
XcRdr4xog5.main_concern: The ablations do not isolate grouped versus independent region generation or pixel-space versus latent-space output under matched training conditions, and the CJK-CLIP Pass metric and benchmark construction lack sufficient validation details.

39hiB7JhUx.one_liner: Prompts or fine-tunes instruction-tuned LLMs to generate the final answer first followed by a post-hoc justification, stopping decoding after the answer.
39hiB7JhUx.problem: Generating intermediate chain-of-thought reasoning traces before the final answer increases inference latency and token costs, and can degrade accuracy on tasks requiring little explicit reasoning.
39hiB7JhUx.method: Post-Reasoning modifies instruction prompts or supervised fine-tuning data (with answer-token loss masked during post-reason tuning) to require models to output their final answer immediately and justify it afterward. At inference time, decoding can stop as soon as the answer token is emitted, incurring no pre-answer reasoning latency while retaining the conditioning benefit of the justification instruction.
39hiB7JhUx.key_idea: Conditions LLMs via prompt suffix or answer-masked fine-tuning to emit the final answer before its justification so inference can halt immediately after the answer token.
39hiB7JhUx.evidence: Evaluated across 117 model-benchmark settings spanning 13 open and proprietary models (7 families) and 9 benchmarks including AMC, HMMT, GSM8K, GPQA, MMLU-Pro, and BIG-Bench Hard.
39hiB7JhUx.claimed_gains: Improves accuracy in 99 of 117 settings (84.62%) with a mean gain of +2.11 accuracy points (15.57% relative), while supervised post-reason tuning improves 91.11% of settings and exceeds prompt-based post-reasoning by +0.77 points (7.17% relative).
39hiB7JhUx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that appending a post-answer justification instruction is a remarkably simple intervention evaluated across a wide range of models and benchmarks with useful stopping-time controls.
39hiB7JhUx.main_concern: Prior work (such as Think-After-Answer and Aux-Think) already introduced answer-first reasoning formats, and the paper overstates the mechanistic explanation as improved latent reasoning rather than a prompt-conditioning effect.

cqWa4nYVKQ.one_liner: Measures stance preservation and polarization across a two-step LLM argument-generation and stance-extraction communication pipeline.
cqWa4nYVKQ.problem: As large language models increasingly draft and summarize human communications, it remains unclear how faithfully an AI-generated message preserves the speaker's intended stance strength and direction when interpreted by a receiver.
cqWa4nYVKQ.method: The authors model AI-mediated communication as a two-step generation-extraction Markov transition matrix over five Likert-scale stance categories, where one LLM generates an argument from a given stance and a second LLM extracts the stance. They define the Stance Preservation Rate (SPR), decompose errors into polarization, neutrality drift, and flipping across 112 debate propositions, and test prompt- and reasoning-based mitigations.
cqWa4nYVKQ.key_idea: Formulates AI-mediated communication as a five-state Markov transition between an argument-generating LLM and a stance-extracting LLM to quantify stance preservation rate and drift modes.
cqWa4nYVKQ.evidence: Evaluated across 9 LLMs and 9 variants on 112 debate propositions, plus a human stance-extraction comparison on a single proposition.
cqWa4nYVKQ.claimed_gains: Across 112 debate propositions, no tested LLM exceeded an SPR of 0.7 under default settings; adding medium reasoning effort to a reflection prompt for GPT-5.4 raised SPR to 0.775, with polarization still accounting for 0.119 of transition mass.
cqWa4nYVKQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that formulating AI-mediated communication fidelity as a stance transition matrix and decomposing failures into polarization, flipping, and neutrality drift is clear and practically relevant.
cqWa4nYVKQ.main_concern: Relying on an LLM extractor as the evaluator conflates generator distortion with extractor calibration bias (especially given undefined boundaries between moderate and strong Likert labels), and human validation covers only one proposition.

51G0g3kWbE.one_liner: Selectively gates unobserved global entities into a privileged MARL teacher and distills relative action advantages anchored to student value estimates.
51G0g3kWbE.problem: In centralized-teacher decentralized-student multi-agent reinforcement learning, feeding the entire global state to the teacher indiscriminately introduces redundant or noisy information that can degrade teacher policies.
51G0g3kWbE.method: Blind-spot Entity-aware Advantage Distillation (BEAD) represents the global state as a set of entities and applies an attention-based gating mechanism so the centralized teacher selectively incorporates only locally unobserved blind-spot entities. It then transfers the teacher's relative action preferences to decentralized students via advantage distillation anchored to each student's own value estimate.
51G0g3kWbE.key_idea: Uses entity-level attention gating to feed only locally unobserved blind-spot entities to a privileged MARL teacher and distills teacher action advantages relative to the student's local value baseline.
51G0g3kWbE.evidence: Supported by theoretical action-preference preservation analysis and empirical evaluations on SMAC and SMACv2 cooperative multi-agent benchmarks.
51G0g3kWbE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that selectively compensating only for an agent's unobserved blind-spot entities rather than dumping the full global state into the teacher is well motivated and clearly presented.
51G0g3kWbE.main_concern: The experimental reporting omits random seed counts, standard deviations, and confidence bands on SMAC/SMACv2 learning curves, and the method requires pre-structured entity state representations.

zUPEDRs09x.one_liner: Decouples LLM-driven GPU kernel generation into high-level computation structure exploration followed by budget-allocated local implementation tuning.
zUPEDRs09x.problem: Single-loop LLM kernel optimization agents interleave structural algorithm changes with low-level parameter tuning, discarding local tuning progress whenever structure changes or locking prematurely into a suboptimal computation structure.
zUPEDRs09x.method: The proposed two-stage framework first explores high-level structural plans—specifying computation decomposition, grid organization, and memory coordination—and selects the top candidate structures using an LLM structural reviewer. In the second stage, an optimization agent applies local implementation refinements from a structured action taxonomy to the selected architectures using compile and runtime profiling feedback.
zUPEDRs09x.key_idea: Factorizes iterative LLM kernel optimization into an initial structural planning stage over decomposition and coordination choices followed by a separate local tuning stage within top-ranked structures.
zUPEDRs09x.evidence: Evaluated across 29 GPU operators in Triton on NVIDIA A800 and H100 GPUs.
zUPEDRs09x.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating high-level kernel structure from local parameter tuning addresses structural lock-in during agentic GPU kernel optimization and is backed by detailed trace analysis across 29 operators.
zUPEDRs09x.main_concern: The Stage-I LLM structural score used to filter five candidate plans down to two is never validated for rank correlation with post-tuning kernel speed, and closely related planning-based kernel agents like AccelOPT are not compared.

DV3TfZYwQE.one_liner: Distills a discrete diffusion language model's committed final-step token distributions back to earlier denoising timesteps during on-policy rollouts.
DV3TfZYwQE.problem: Discrete diffusion language models degrade sharply when parallel token unmasking is accelerated, while offline trajectory distillation requires costly separate teacher generation pipelines.
DV3TfZYwQE.method: Temporal Self-Distillation (TSD) performs single-stage on-policy training by using the model's own token distribution at the final timestep when a token is committed as a teacher target for its predictive distribution at earlier denoising timesteps along the same rollout. This self-distillation objective encourages earlier denoising steps to anticipate committed outputs and supports both masked and uniform-state discrete diffusion models.
DV3TfZYwQE.key_idea: Uses each token's denoising distribution at its commitment timestep as an on-policy distillation target for earlier timesteps along the same trajectory to accelerate parallel decoding.
DV3TfZYwQE.evidence: Evaluated across seven benchmarks in mathematics, planning, and coding (including GSM8K, MATH-500, MBPP, HumanEval, and LiveCodeBench) on LLaDA-8B-Instruct and RL-post-trained policies.
DV3TfZYwQE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that distilling commitment-step predictions back to earlier denoising steps within on-policy rollouts is a simple, low-overhead way to improve parallel decoding without offline teacher caching.
DV3TfZYwQE.main_concern: Main benchmark comparisons are confounded because TSD fine-tunes on task-specific training splits (often with verifier rewards) whereas the primary Fast-dLLM baseline uses an unadapted off-the-shelf base model.

My6dyV7ecS.one_liner: Routes among financial portfolio agents by predicting high-consequence trading dates and gating default-relative switching value.
My6dyV7ecS.problem: Standard best-expert routing treats all classification errors equally, ignoring that portfolio routing mistakes matter far more on trading dates with large return gaps between candidate allocations.
My6dyV7ecS.method: PortfolioRouter uses market-state representations and candidate portfolio proposals to jointly train a general selector, a critical-date detector, a critical-date specialist, and an auxiliary volatility-normalized return predictor. A default-relative value model estimates the historical economic gain of overriding a default agent while penalizing harmful switches, and a quarterly calibrated gate decides whether to execute each switch.
My6dyV7ecS.key_idea: Combines multi-task critical-date detection with a conservatively aggregated default-relative economic switching value estimator and a quarterly calibrated deployment gate to selectively override a default portfolio agent.
My6dyV7ecS.evidence: Evaluated on U.S. and China equity market backtests from 2025 through June 2026 under same-close execution and zero transaction costs.
My6dyV7ecS.claimed_gains: In U.S. and China backtests from 2025 through June 2026, PortfolioRouter achieves mean returns of 34.86% and 45.92%, exceeding the same models' general paths by 8.69 and 13.59 percentage points.
My6dyV7ecS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that weighting routing decisions by the economic return gap between candidate portfolios and selectively overriding a default policy on high-consequence dates aligns well with financial decision-making.
My6dyV7ecS.main_concern: Backtests assume unrealistic same-close execution with zero latency or transaction costs, risk LLM pretraining lookahead leakage on 2025-2026 market data, and show inconsistent gains from consequence-aware supervision on U.S. data.

w6gLmpXdBO.one_liner: Constant-gain Bellman analysis gives finite-sample guarantees for robust average-reward learning under weak communication.
w6gLmpXdBO.problem: Existing guarantees for robust average-reward reinforcement learning rely on restrictive ergodicity, irreducibility, or unichain assumptions.
w6gLmpXdBO.method: The work establishes constant-gain Bellman solutions under radius conditions for KL and f_k uncertainty and any positive radius for total variation and Wasserstein uncertainty. A prior-knowledge-free algorithm estimates robust average reward and learns near-optimal policies with explicit sample guarantees and bias-span bounds.
w6gLmpXdBO.key_idea: Constant-gain Bellman solutions and bounds on the robust optimal bias span support finite-sample analysis for S- and SA-rectangular uncertainty.
w6gLmpXdBO.evidence: Theoretical results cover four uncertainty families and both rectangular structures, while a constructed MDP experiment checks the predicted convergence rate.
w6gLmpXdBO.claimed_gains: The abstract reports a predicted n^{-1/2} convergence rate.
w6gLmpXdBO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value relaxing earlier assumptions to weak communication and covering several uncertainty sets under both rectangular structures.
w6gLmpXdBO.main_concern: Reviewers find limited technical novelty beyond combining and extending established structural results and proof techniques.

CbHteaAWDk.one_liner: UniTrust combines hidden-state risk probes with contrastive activation steering trained through corpus-grounded synthetic supervision.
CbHteaAWDk.problem: Adapting language models to new safety tasks often requires large task-specific datasets for both detection and intervention.
CbHteaAWDk.method: UniTrust trains a detector on frozen hidden representations and extracts steering directions from matched safe and unsafe responses. Corpus-Grounded Synthesis retrieves public contexts and rewrites them according to a task description and a few labeled examples.
CbHteaAWDk.key_idea: A shared hidden-representation space supports risk detection through probes and behavioral intervention through safe-versus-unsafe activation directions.
CbHteaAWDk.evidence: Detection experiments cover ten safety domains and three model families using ten positive and ten negative real examples per task.
CbHteaAWDk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the low-label adaptation pipeline practical and value its evaluation across multiple safety domains and model families.
CbHteaAWDk.main_concern: Reviewers question the contribution beyond closely related synthesis and steering methods because direct comparisons with those methods are missing.

2pk4tcLL9D.one_liner: CycleA routes generated latent features through a frozen understanding branch to supervise image editing with source-image VQA.
2pk4tcLL9D.problem: Unified multimodal models train understanding and generation largely independently, leaving understanding-based guidance for image editing underused.
2pk4tcLL9D.method: CycleA maps generation outputs into the frozen understanding branch through a lightweight frozen projector and applies source-image VQA reconstruction supervision. A feature-alignment loss constrains the mapped features to remain close to real visual features.
2pk4tcLL9D.key_idea: A frozen projector carries differentiable VQA feedback from the understanding branch to generated latents without decoding and re-encoding images.
2pk4tcLL9D.evidence: BAGEL editing experiments include GEN-only and shuffled-QA controls, and the abstract reports improvements after 2,000 post-training steps.
2pk4tcLL9D.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the inexpensive differentiable latent-space connection to the model's own understanding branch.
2pk4tcLL9D.main_concern: Reviewers question how source-image reconstruction and VQA supervision produce editing gains, given unclear supervision compatibility and limited mechanism validation.

3HQHUVYUNk.one_liner: GateTree filters shared evidence by provenance and branch relevance, then revises plans for conservative and exploratory agents.
3HQHUVYUNk.problem: Shared findings can become stale or inapplicable as parallel agents evolve, spreading unsupported assumptions and redundant work.
3HQHUVYUNk.method: GateTree runs conservative and exploratory branches while a GateAgent checks the provenance and scope of shared records. An adaptive planner uses selected context and execution feedback to revise objectives and verification targets.
3HQHUVYUNk.key_idea: Recipient-specific evidence selection and feedback-driven replanning jointly regulate information sharing between two complementary agent branches.
3HQHUVYUNk.evidence: Experiments use SWE-bench Pro, text-only HLE, and GAIA2 with two backbones, component ablations, and context-relevance analyses.
3HQHUVYUNk.claimed_gains: GateTree reduces cost by an average of 30.17% relative to each setting's strongest Pass@2 baseline, while passive sharing reduces Pass@2 by 11.50 points.
3HQHUVYUNk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize stale shared information as a practical collaboration problem and value the evaluation across different benchmarks and backbones.
3HQHUVYUNk.main_concern: Reviewers seek deeper analysis of when the gains occur and whether higher task coverage also improves individual branch quality.

wsSHfjSrMC.one_liner: TCR merges embodied specialists by regressing expert block outputs on trajectory-calibrated inputs replayed through merged prefixes.
wsSHfjSrMC.problem: Parameter alignment and limited offline calibration fail to reliably preserve specialist behavior during closed-loop robot execution.
wsSHfjSrMC.method: TCR collects calibration inputs across expert rollout stages and intermediate action-generation states, then recomputes each block's inputs through the merged prefix. Blockwise regression and a second calibration pass fit one static policy to frozen specialists without gradient training or routing.
wsSHfjSrMC.key_idea: Trajectory and action-generation calibration, combined with merged-prefix replay, lets blockwise regression match expert linear outputs under merging-induced representation shifts.
wsSHfjSrMC.evidence: Experiments merge four pi_0.5 specialists on LIBERO and include physical-robot trials, component ablations, and continual-learning evaluation.
wsSHfjSrMC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers consider calibration on actual execution trajectories well motivated for preserving robot behavior during policy merging.
wsSHfjSrMC.main_concern: Reviewers question how much the method adds beyond existing regression-and-replay merging, with calibration-budget differences complicating attribution.

5a8npzgZeg.one_liner: Frozen-teacher transition anchoring stabilizes classifier-score distillation without an online fake-score model.
5a8npzgZeg.problem: The effectiveness and stabilization requirements of classifier-score signals in text-to-image distillation remain poorly understood.
5a8npzgZeg.method: The work studies condition granularity using synthetic experiments and score-space interpolation, then compares distribution-matching stabilizers with transition anchoring. Transition anchoring constrains student transitions with frozen teacher dynamics instead of tracking the evolving student distribution online.
5a8npzgZeg.key_idea: Teacher transition targets regularize the classifier-score distillation signal at student states without maintaining a fake-score network.
5a8npzgZeg.evidence: Synthetic condition-granularity experiments and text-to-image interpolation accompany a comparison of seven stabilizers on four backbones with six metrics.
5a8npzgZeg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the practical finding that frozen teacher dynamics can stabilize classifier-score distillation without an online fake-score model.
5a8npzgZeg.main_concern: Reviewers find the contribution insufficiently distinguished from existing decoupled DMD and trajectory or consistency distillation objectives.

bzyfCGPcet.one_liner: Separate curvature, loss-balance, and update-alignment diagnostics expose distinct large-step dynamics in no-momentum Muon.
bzyfCGPcet.problem: The classical gradient-descent edge-of-stability picture does not adequately describe Muon's large-step pretraining dynamics.
bzyfCGPcet.method: The study defines separate diagnostics for generalized sharpness, finite-step loss balance, and temporal update alignment. Theoretical examples and checkpoint interventions test how these quantities respond to learning rate and batch size in no-momentum Muon.
bzyfCGPcet.key_idea: Finite-step loss balance and consecutive-update alignment are measured separately because equal effective curvature can produce different update-direction relationships.
bzyfCGPcet.evidence: Evidence includes matrix-quadratic analysis, controlled networks, language models from 22M to 1B parameters, and checkpoint interventions in 22M and 130M models.
bzyfCGPcet.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value studying Muon's dynamics and find the distinction between loss balance and update-direction alignment informative.
bzyfCGPcet.main_concern: Reviewers argue that a loss-neutral identity and decoupled update alignment do not establish the claimed dynamical edge-of-stability interpretation.

LOHzPGrcTQ.one_liner: SpecEvo pairs cheap parallel program search and persistent search-history guidance with sparse frontier-model interventions.
LOHzPGrcTQ.problem: LLM-driven evolutionary discovery spends expensive reasoning on routine trials while underusing failures and saturated search directions.
LOHzPGrcTQ.method: Lightweight Speculators generate candidate programs, and a lightweight Advisor consolidates successes and failures into persistent guidance. At sparse checkpoints, a frontier-model Navigator inspects stagnation and synthesizes, refines, or reframes candidates.
LOHzPGrcTQ.key_idea: Cheap models explore and consolidate search evidence while a frontier model intervenes only at strategic checkpoints.
LOHzPGrcTQ.evidence: Experiments cover 176 tasks across four scientific and algorithmic discovery domains with multiple budgets and evolutionary-search baselines.
LOHzPGrcTQ.claimed_gains: SpecEvo reports up to 80% lower API cost than frontier-model baselines and up to 1.5× greater evaluation efficiency than cost-efficient baselines on equation discovery.
LOHzPGrcTQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the practical division of work between cheap and frontier models for reducing scientific-search cost.
LOHzPGrcTQ.main_concern: Reviewers consider the framework an incremental combination of established search archives, history-based guidance, and model-allocation methods.

Dj0TsbdzjT.one_liner: VisualRefineBench separates reflection, action choice, and editing to diagnose image self-refinement failures under matched image-operation budgets.
Dj0TsbdzjT.problem: It remains unclear whether unified multimodal models reliably improve delivered image quality by inspecting and revising their own outputs.
Dj0TsbdzjT.method: VisualRefineBench combines end-to-end refinement evaluation with fixed-input Reflection, Decision, and Editing tasks. It tracks initial, best-intermediate, and delivered quality and compares refinement against an Oracle best-of-N baseline under equal image-operation budgets.
Dj0TsbdzjT.key_idea: Component diagnostics and best-intermediate versus final-image scores distinguish error detection, action selection, editing damage, and final-selection failures.
Dj0TsbdzjT.evidence: The abstract evaluates nine UMMs across 800 examples with a four-image-call budget and tests controller replacement across four generator-editor combinations.
Dj0TsbdzjT.claimed_gains: Replacing the whole Controller with a model stronger in Reflection improves mean final quality by about 17 points across four generator-editor combinations.
Dj0TsbdzjT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the component-level diagnostics and the distinction between generating a better intermediate image and selecting it as the final output.
Dj0TsbdzjT.main_concern: Reviewers question automated-judge reliability and request independent human or cross-family validation of the benchmark scores and controller gains.

FpAHxLiQwj.one_liner: ReasonMaxxer applies contrastive training only at high-entropy token decisions using a small set of offline base-model rollouts.
FpAHxLiQwj.problem: Reasoning improvements from reinforcement learning may require costly optimization even when useful solution paths already exist in the base model.
FpAHxLiQwj.method: Token-level analyses compare base and RL models to locate sparse corrections at uncertain decision points. ReasonMaxxer uses base-model entropy to gate a contrastive loss on offline rollouts without online generation or an RL-trained model.
FpAHxLiQwj.key_idea: Entropy gating restricts contrastive updates to uncertain token positions where sparse policy corrections change reasoning trajectories.
FpAHxLiQwj.evidence: Token analyses span multiple model families and RL algorithms, with targeted-versus-random correction experiments concentrated on mathematical reasoning.
FpAHxLiQwj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the token-level observations and the simple attempt to recover reasoning improvements with less training cost.
FpAHxLiQwj.main_concern: Reviewers find the evidence insufficient for the broad claim that RL selects existing capabilities rather than learning new ones.

trElgj8hwg.one_liner: Signed feedforward-loop regularization embeds excitatory-inhibitory circuit motifs into larger networks to bias their computational behavior.
trElgj8hwg.problem: How excitatory-inhibitory organization specializes feedforward-loop computation and translates into larger-network behavior remains unclear.
trElgj8hwg.method: The paper analyzes four excitatory-inhibitory configurations of three-node feedforward loops under specified inputs and background conditions. A differentiable signed-motif loss enriches larger networks with selected loops as structural learning priors.
trElgj8hwg.key_idea: A differentiable loss increases selected signed feedforward loops so their direct-versus-relay pathway interactions become structural priors in larger networks.
trElgj8hwg.evidence: Circuit-dynamics analysis links motifs to initiation, switching, stopping, and context-dependent release, while MiniHack evaluations test task-dependent behavioral biases.
trElgj8hwg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the connection between interpretable local circuits and larger-network behavioral capacities interesting and meaningful.
trElgj8hwg.main_concern: Reviewers question the strength and fairness of empirical comparisons, including limited baselines and possible parameter and training-budget mismatches.

TWumYIWTHS.one_liner: OJS uses a reference QMIX threshold to protect candidate optimal joint actions while softly downweighting potentially interfering samples.
TWumYIWTHS.problem: Monotonic value mixing can suppress optimal individual actions when inferior teammate actions contaminate their training samples.
TWumYIWTHS.method: OJS derives a screening threshold from the maximum of a least-squares QMIX projection and approximates it with an independently trained reference QMIX. Candidate samples receive unit weight, while other samples receive adaptive soft weights based on potential interference.
TWumYIWTHS.key_idea: A separate reference QMIX defines a candidate set whose samples retain full weight while lower-valued samples receive interference-dependent weights.
TWumYIWTHS.evidence: The paper presents projection-based guarantees and cooperative benchmark experiments including matrix games, ablations, and sensitivity analyses.
TWumYIWTHS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the practical screening design and the breadth of coordination experiments and ablations.
TWumYIWTHS.main_concern: Reviewers question the theoretical foundation and its applicability, with one supplying a counterexample to Proposition 1 and another identifying a theory-implementation mismatch.

n3XVaerJax.one_liner: CATER routes reliably solved problems to concise self-distillation and inconsistent problems to correctness-based reinforcement learning.
n3XVaerJax.problem: Uniformly shortening chain-of-thought responses can damage unsolved reasoning while leaving mastered problems unnecessarily verbose.
n3XVaerJax.method: CATER uses each problem's online student success rate to select between on-policy concise self-distillation and correctness-based reinforcement learning. Routing changes as competence evolves, separating compression of reliable solutions from learning on inconsistently solved problems.
n3XVaerJax.key_idea: Online correctness determines whether a problem receives a concise self-distillation signal or a reinforcement-learning signal.
n3XVaerJax.evidence: Qwen3-4B evaluations cover five benchmarks spanning mathematical reasoning, scientific reasoning, and code generation, with routing ablations and additional model results.
n3XVaerJax.claimed_gains: On Qwen3-4B, CATER reduces reasoning tokens by 39.1% on average across five benchmarks while maintaining comparable overall accuracy.
n3XVaerJax.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers consider competence-based routing a sensible way to reduce unnecessary reasoning while preserving correctness on harder problems.
n3XVaerJax.main_concern: Reviewers find the contribution beyond existing adaptive compression methods unclear without comparisons to CEEH and PACE.

ERVPQMCGpn.one_liner: AREO predicts masked patch embeddings autoregressively with temporally consistent masking for remote-sensing representation learning.
ERVPQMCGpn.problem: Remote-sensing foundation models struggle with observation noise and insufficient modeling of fine-grained temporal structure.
ERVPQMCGpn.method: AREO combines high-ratio temporally consistent masking with a causal predictor that estimates masked patch representations from current and preceding context. Feature prediction replaces observation-level reconstruction while preserving patch-level temporal structure.
ERVPQMCGpn.key_idea: A causal predictor reconstructs masked patch embeddings from current and earlier context while temporally consistent masking preserves sequence structure.
ERVPQMCGpn.evidence: AREO pretrains on SSL4EO-S12 and evaluates frozen and fine-tuned backbones on three temporal and two static datasets with masking and prediction ablations.
ERVPQMCGpn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find temporally directed embedding prediction useful for remote sensing and recognize the reported temporal-benchmark improvements.
ERVPQMCGpn.main_concern: Reviewers see limited methodological novelty beyond combining established masked self-distillation, teacher, and masking components.

lL6IKLZdCX.one_liner: AS²D drafts audio-conditioned tokens independently of the target prefix so drafting and target verification run concurrently.
lL6IKLZdCX.problem: Conventional speculative decoding serializes drafting and verification by coupling the drafter to the target's evolving verified prefix.
lL6IKLZdCX.method: AS²D lets an audio-conditioned drafter follow its own history while the target verifies and corrects available candidates. The target advances alone when candidates are unavailable, and the Android implementation uses MNN.
lL6IKLZdCX.key_idea: Source-conditioned drafts advance independently of target-prefix updates, while target-side verification decides which candidates to commit.
lL6IKLZdCX.evidence: Evaluation covers two target models, four phones, seven datasets, and three tasks over 12.2 hours of audio using phone-profile replay and limited native validation.
lL6IKLZdCX.claimed_gains: AS²D increases pooled ASR throughput by 42–76% over Target-only across four phones in phone-profile replay, with slowdowns on 5.7% of windows.
lL6IKLZdCX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the practical mobile implementation and reported throughput gains from decoupling audio drafting and verification.
lL6IKLZdCX.main_concern: Reviewers find native-device validation too limited relative to replay-based results, particularly given observed differences from target-only outputs.

9yBpZHu6LY.one_liner: RideBench tests ride-hailing forecasts under exogenous disturbances and long horizons using a synthesized four-year regional dataset.
9yBpZHu6LY.problem: Existing forecasting evaluations inadequately capture external disturbances and tradeoffs between long-horizon trends, pointwise errors, and near-term accuracy.
9yBpZHu6LY.method: RideBench builds on a marketplace-derived synthesized dataset with weather, holiday, and large-event scenarios. It evaluates regular week-ahead and eight-week-ahead forecasts using disturbance-specific and temporal-aggregation analyses.
9yBpZHu6LY.key_idea: Scenario-based forecasting tests combine exogenous covariates with near-term and long-horizon metrics on the same regional time series.
9yBpZHu6LY.evidence: The benchmark covers 200 spatial areas over four years at half-hourly resolution and evaluates over 30 methods with horizons up to 2,688 steps.
9yBpZHu6LY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the substantial domain-specific dataset and scenario-level evaluation that exposes failures hidden by average forecast error.
9yBpZHu6LY.main_concern: Reviewers question whether weather and event-impact variables labeled future-known would actually be available at forecast time, especially over eight weeks.

6gD5WHS4ei.one_liner: Adversarial attack-defender iteration evolves executable agent prompts, validators, and tool-control logic while keeping model weights frozen.
6gD5WHS4ei.problem: Static agent defenses struggle to keep pace with changing attacks, environments, and model behavior.
6gD5WHS4ei.method: DefenseFlywheel alternates an attacker that discovers failures with a defender that proposes executable harness patches. The optimization spans prompts, validators, and tool-control logic without retraining the underlying model.
6gD5WHS4ei.key_idea: Use newly discovered attacks as a curriculum for iteratively patching and selecting executable agent defenses.
6gD5WHS4ei.evidence: Experiments cover five victim models on AgentDojo Banking, cross-model and cross-suite transfer, adaptive attacks, a WASP browser-agent study, and prompt-only ablations.
6gD5WHS4ei.claimed_gains: Attack success falls from 36.3% to 3.2% on AgentDojo Banking and from 77.5% to 20.0% against an adaptive attacker.
6gD5WHS4ei.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize executable harness optimization as a useful security direction and credit the framework's experimental contribution.
6gD5WHS4ei.main_concern: The evaluation leaves generalization to broader agent environments and previously unrecognized attack mechanisms insufficiently established.

gPFmL2xw2y.one_liner: Task-relevant fixed-camera selection and temporal target updates support language-guided navigation in changing indoor environments.
gPFmL2xw2y.problem: Egocentric navigation cannot observe task-relevant target movements or pedestrian interactions outside the robot's current view.
gPFmL2xw2y.method: EgoExo-VLN combines onboard observations with selected fixed-camera evidence and updates target representations over time to revise navigation goals. Its benchmark controls target relocation and absent, conflicting, or non-conflicting pedestrian conditions.
gPFmL2xw2y.key_idea: Select task-relevant external-camera evidence and maintain target information over time to update navigation decisions.
gPFmL2xw2y.evidence: The benchmark contains 8,096 episodes across 90 indoor scenes with scene-disjoint splits, controlled pedestrian conditions, and static tasks, alongside ablations and a one-scene real-world evaluation.
gPFmL2xw2y.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that off-camera environmental changes motivate the task and that the dynamic benchmark offers useful controlled evaluation.
gPFmL2xw2y.main_concern: Comparisons and ablations do not isolate exocentric visual evidence from extra geometry, pose information, and controller components.

ELb1Hcc11c.one_liner: Wasserstein robustness analysis separates diffusion score-estimation error into statistical learning cost and intrinsic distribution-shift cost.
ELb1Hcc11c.problem: Diffusion-model theory largely assumes the deployment distribution matches the training distribution.
ELb1Hcc11c.method: The analysis studies score estimation for Ornstein-Uhlenbeck diffusion over Wasserstein perturbations and constructs an explicit finite-sample estimator that does not require the shift radius. It extends the decomposition to unknown low-dimensional subspaces and positive-time reverse sampling.
ELb1Hcc11c.key_idea: Decompose worst-case shifted score risk into nominal estimation error and a minimax-optimal term quadratic in Wasserstein radius.
ELb1Hcc11c.evidence: Matching upper and lower bounds establish robust score-estimation rates, intrinsic-dimension adaptation, and positive-time reverse-sampling guarantees in KL divergence.
ELb1Hcc11c.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize distribution shift as a relevant problem and credit the explicit robustness formulation and shift-cost characterization.
ELb1Hcc11c.main_concern: Reviewers question how much insight the additive combination of known nominal-estimation results and a shift-stability bound contributes.

jReXTN8Egq.one_liner: A query-conditioned gate scales subject-relevant MLP neurons, trained through relative rewards across intervention configurations.
jReXTN8Egq.problem: Fixed internal steering cannot accommodate the different knowledge and reasoning demands of individual queries.
jReXTN8Egq.method: Q-NeuS builds a compact subject-guided candidate neuron space and predicts neuron-wise modulation coefficients with a lightweight query-adaptive gate. Neu-GRPO trains the gate using relative performance across intervention configurations while keeping the backbone fixed.
jReXTN8Egq.key_idea: Use query-induced activations to predict neuron-specific scaling coefficients within a subject-guided candidate space.
jReXTN8Egq.evidence: Reviews report improvements across 21 in-domain model–benchmark combinations spanning two model families and sizes from 3B to 32B, with neuron analyses and ablations.
jReXTN8Egq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the motivating neuron analyses and the broad evaluation showing improvements over base models.
jReXTN8Egq.main_concern: The absence of a learned query-independent scaling baseline prevents isolating the contribution of query adaptivity.

bzvE9FTJOW.one_liner: A finite-multiplier Lagrangian and blockwise robust aggregation enable first-order, single-loop federated bilevel updates.
bzvE9FTJOW.problem: Byzantine-robust federated bilevel methods require expensive higher-order differentiation or repeated inner-loop synchronization.
bzvE9FTJOW.method: FOBFBL forms three coupled stochastic-gradient blocks under a finite Lagrangian multiplier and robustly aggregates them at their natural scales in one round. Its Polyak-momentum variant removes stochastic variance from the persistent Byzantine error.
bzvE9FTJOW.key_idea: Robustly aggregate three coupled first-order gradient blocks from a finite-multiplier Lagrangian in a single communication round.
bzvE9FTJOW.evidence: The paper proves stationarity bounds under lower-level strong convexity and last-iterate bounds under an upper-level PL condition, with hyperparameter-optimization experiments described in reviews.
bzvE9FTJOW.claimed_gains: The stationarity analysis yields O(epsilon^-2) iterations above a residual floor, including O(1/lambda^2) Lagrangian bias.
bzvE9FTJOW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate avoiding higher-order products and repeated inner loops, together with bounds separating optimization, Byzantine, and multiplier errors.
bzvE9FTJOW.main_concern: Inconsistent experimental model descriptions and unclear local-update protocols leave uncertain whether the theoretical assumptions hold in the implementation.

8WrIQPcWje.one_liner: CPU frame clustering postpones visual encoding until retrieval and query-driven detail recovery.
8WrIQPcWje.problem: Continuous visual encoding limits concurrent video-stream serving under a fixed GPU budget.
8WrIQPcWje.method: StreamIndex groups incoming frames using CPU-side statistics and encodes one representative per finalized cluster for retrieval. At query time, it selects relevant clusters, chooses frames using motion, and reuses stable spatial features.
8WrIQPcWje.key_idea: Index streams with lightweight frame statistics, then encode retrieved details selectively using motion-based frame selection and spatial feature reuse.
8WrIQPcWje.evidence: Experiments use Qwen-VL and LLaVA-OneVision on OVO-Bench and StreamingBench, with a multi-stream 1080p query-load test.
8WrIQPcWje.claimed_gains: At 16 streams and two queries per minute per stream, StreamIndex achieves a P95 response latency of 5.57 seconds.
8WrIQPcWje.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize continuous encoding as a practical bottleneck and find the training-free separation of indexing and encoding useful.
8WrIQPcWje.main_concern: Low-level motion and similarity heuristics may discard action-critical information or reuse stale features without establishing semantic validity.

eKykbVqVgk.one_liner: UI transition graphs and action-aligned video diagnose deviations, loops, and recovery in mobile GUI agent trajectories.
eKykbVqVgk.problem: Final task-success metrics miss unstable GUI execution paths that contain unnecessary actions, loops, or errors.
eKykbVqVgk.method: GraceBench represents reachable mobile-app interactions as UI Transition Graphs and aligns dynamic observations with graph states using video-grounded evaluation. It measures process stability through deviation, loop burden, and recovery metrics.
eKykbVqVgk.key_idea: Align action videos to task-specific UI transition graphs and label trajectory deviations, repeated states, and returns to valid paths.
eKykbVqVgk.evidence: Reviews describe trajectory comparisons with matched outcomes and a blinded human audit of a 10% transition sample assessing deviation, recovery, and loop labels.
eKykbVqVgk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that diagnosing execution quality beyond final task success is practically useful.
eKykbVqVgk.main_concern: Incomplete reference graphs can label valid alternative routes as deviations, undermining the validity of the stability metrics.

pr1KKYiTs2.one_liner: Shared-sample concentration analysis characterizes TwoNN through sample size and covariance spectra rather than manifold dimension alone.
pr1KKYiTs2.problem: In high dimensions, nearest neighbors may fall outside local neighborhoods needed to interpret TwoNN as intrinsic dimension.
pr1KKYiTs2.method: The paper analyzes the pooled inverse-mean-log-ratio estimator for anisotropic Gaussian data and noiseless spheres as sample size and dimension grow together. Prediction-preserving feature rescalings probe its behavior in neural representations.
pr1KKYiTs2.key_idea: Derive the pooled nearest-neighbor ratio estimator's sample-resolution target while accounting for dependence between ratios from the same sample.
pr1KKYiTs2.evidence: Gaussian and spherical experiments test the theoretical laws, and prediction-preserving rescalings probe five CIFAR-10/ResNet-18 models.
pr1KKYiTs2.claimed_gains: Covariance-aligned rescaling increases TwoNN by a median factor of 2.20 while preserving every prediction, versus 0.995 for random orientations with identical singular values.
pr1KKYiTs2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the explicit sample-size- and spectrum-dependent characterization and its treatment of shared-sample dependence.
pr1KKYiTs2.main_concern: The theory's distributional and rank assumptions limit applicability to low-intrinsic-rank manifolds and general neural representations.

3HDmBMmDsK.one_liner: Matching constructions and lower bounds establish a strict attention-head hierarchy for one-layer transformers with finite ReLU readouts.
3HDmBMmDsK.problem: The expressivity gained by adding attention heads remains insufficiently characterized when a feed-forward block can also contribute computation.
3HDmBMmDsK.method: The paper constructs decision problems realizable by one-layer transformers with h+1 heads and proves that h heads cannot solve them. The separation permits arbitrary fixed embedding dimensions and finite ReLU readouts over unbounded input lengths.
3HDmBMmDsK.key_idea: Construct a language with an exact head requirement and match an explicit attention construction with a lower bound surviving finite ReLU readouts.
3HDmBMmDsK.evidence: Matching upper and lower bounds establish the hierarchy for every head count in the one-layer, fixed-network, unbounded-input-length setting.
3HDmBMmDsK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the exact hierarchy and its survival under arbitrary fixed finite ReLU readouts are the main theoretical strengths.
3HDmBMmDsK.main_concern: The separation's one-layer, unbounded-length setting limits broader conclusions about practical finite-context head-count tradeoffs.

j8Jrb0OZmr.one_liner: Shared-encoder prediction and task-conditioned scoring shape world-model representations around action comparisons while retaining factual dynamics.
j8Jrb0OZmr.problem: Low prediction error can hide small task-relevant differences between candidate actions that determine planning decisions.
j8Jrb0OZmr.method: PC-TIG jointly trains a factual world model and query-conditioned scorer through a shared encoder. It uses direct joint updates or prediction-priority updates for feedback actions and complete action segments.
j8Jrb0OZmr.key_idea: Let task-comparison gradients shape a shared predictive representation while constraining updates that conflict with factual prediction.
j8Jrb0OZmr.evidence: Five-seed stochastic navigation and multi-objective HalfCheetah segment-ranking experiments compare matched predictive and geometry-learning baselines, with frozen-representation controls described in reviews.
j8Jrb0OZmr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the prediction–decision connection and controlled experiments designed to examine representation effects.
j8Jrb0OZmr.main_concern: Missing controls that remove only the maximum-candidate error term leave its contribution beyond ordinary joint task-supervised learning unclear.

g70YJF2Cwd.one_liner: Executable certificates verify spatial tool-use derivations and supply targeted process supervision for urban reasoning agents.
g70YJF2Cwd.problem: Correct final answers can conceal misuse of spatial evidence or invalid intermediate computations.
g70YJF2Cwd.method: UrbanSDF constructs executable certificates linking entity bindings, tool arguments, returned observations, spatial computations, and final decisions. It uses tool-protocol supervision, targeted faithful demonstrations, and Conditional-Dual GRPO in staged training.
g70YJF2Cwd.key_idea: Check executable dependencies between entity bindings, tool evidence, spatial calculations, and final decisions to supervise derivations separately from answer correctness.
g70YJF2Cwd.evidence: Reviews describe staged ablations, four backbones, Controlled/Full settings and cross-city transfer including held-out Sydney.
g70YJF2Cwd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value separating answer correctness from derivation faithfulness through interpretable executable checks and evaluations across backbones and cities.
g70YJF2Cwd.main_concern: The verifier's reliability and treatment of alternative valid derivations remain insufficiently specified or independently validated.

q4jkjwtQkv.one_liner: Compute–accuracy scaling priors and reference-front geometry assign scalar rankings to architecture tradeoffs during evolutionary search.
q4jkjwtQkv.problem: Pareto dominance leaves accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs incomparable, while set-dependent ranking heuristics can be unreliable with few sampled architectures.
q4jkjwtQkv.method: CATOS uses a compute–accuracy scaling prior and geometric constructions involving reference fronts, local ideal points, and a Pareto corridor to rank architectures. CATOS-EA integrates the scalarization into evolutionary search.
q4jkjwtQkv.key_idea: Fit compute–accuracy reference fronts and use their local geometry to assign architectures a scalar tradeoff score.
q4jkjwtQkv.evidence: Experiments compare multiobjective and constrained search methods on NATS-Bench and assess transfer of the constructs to HW-GPT-Bench.
q4jkjwtQkv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find structural tradeoff ranking meaningful and recognize its usefulness under limited evaluation budgets.
q4jkjwtQkv.main_concern: The distinct contribution of the geometric scalarization over existing reference-front methods and simpler alternatives remains unclear.

jDFuw9smxN.one_liner: A model fitted to recent evaluations supplies improvement proposals and Jacobian-shaped exploration inside population optimizers.
jDFuw9smxN.problem: Population optimizers must balance local improvement and exploration without exceeding a fixed objective-evaluation budget.
jDFuw9smxN.method: JANUS fits a model online to recent search evaluations and reuses it to propose local improvements and shape exploratory sampling. It replaces selected candidate slots while preserving the host optimizer's update rules and evaluation budget.
jDFuw9smxN.key_idea: Reuse one online surrogate to generate exploitation candidates and shape exploratory sampling within existing population-optimizer slots.
jDFuw9smxN.evidence: Evaluations cover BBOB, UAV planning, multiobjective optimization and industrial auto white balance, including frozen-configuration confirmation with new optimizer seeds.
jDFuw9smxN.claimed_gains: At 500 dimensions and 20,000 evaluations, selected configurations improve Sep-CMA-ES on 13 of 16 BBOB functions with zero or one significant regression, while mean UAV cost falls 12.8% versus DE at 2,500 evaluations and mean reproduction angle error falls 22.5% versus CMA-ES in a single-run 1,134-parameter calibration study.
jDFuw9smxN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the flexible integration with existing optimizers and promising results across application domains.
jDFuw9smxN.main_concern: The presentation and justification of implementation choices do not clearly establish how the proposed design applies across different optimization settings.

KJQ2ZEgEVm.one_liner: Entity, event, and topic anchors organize cross-session dialogue into query-relevant records injected into existing memory systems.
KJQ2ZEgEVm.problem: Retrieved memory fragments often leave cross-session relationships implicit for the generator.
KJQ2ZEgEVm.method: GRAVITY consolidates raw dialogue into entity profiles, temporal event traces, and cross-session topic summaries. A host-independent layer retrieves relevant records and injects them through query and prompt interfaces.
KJQ2ZEgEVm.key_idea: Consolidate dialogue into structured entity, event, and topic records and inject query-relevant anchors at generation time.
KJQ2ZEgEVm.evidence: Experiments cover five heterogeneous memory systems on LongMemEval and LoCoMo under two LLM configurations, with same-host representation comparisons and component analyses.
KJQ2ZEgEVm.claimed_gains: With a shared LightMem host, answer template, and generator, the entity–event–topic representation reaches 83.9% on LoCoMo, 3.6% above the strongest of six alternative auxiliary pipelines.
KJQ2ZEgEVm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize consistent improvements across hosts and benchmarks and the practical prompt-level integration.
KJQ2ZEgEVm.main_concern: Comparisons do not fully isolate memory organization from additional evidence, context volume, and computational budget.

CZiJw1CCxg.one_liner: Stochastic report samples and localized visual prototypes support conservative finding-level edits to frozen medical model outputs.
CZiJw1CCxg.problem: A single radiology-report decode can omit supported findings or include unsupported claims, and repetition across decodes does not establish correctness.
CZiJw1CCxg.method: HIDE extracts finding candidates from an initial draft and additional stochastic decodes, combining cross-sample consistency with localized prototype-based visual verification. It adds supported omissions, removes unsupported claims, or abstains when evidence is inconclusive.
CZiJw1CCxg.key_idea: Treat stochastic decodes as finding proposals, verify them against visual prototypes, and make source-constrained add, remove, or abstain decisions.
CZiJw1CCxg.evidence: Reviews describe evaluations across multiple frozen generators and datasets, including comparisons on MIMIC-CXR and component ablations.
CZiJw1CCxg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the recovery of omitted findings useful and consider combining sample consistency with visual verification a sensible design.
CZiJw1CCxg.main_concern: The methodological distinction from prior sampling-based checking, localized visual verification, and report post-editing remains limited.

VseZJ6MGKd.one_liner: Prototype-margin training preserves terminal feature-space cells when quantizing flow models for single-step generation.
VseZJ6MGKd.problem: Minimizing velocity reconstruction error does not ensure that quantized flow models preserve the terminal distribution or correct feature-space cells.
VseZJ6MGKd.method: CM-QAT trains a low-bit, one-step student against a teacher's terminal geometry in a frozen feature space. A nested partition and differentiable prototype-margin objective encourage each source sample to reach the correct terminal cell.
VseZJ6MGKd.key_idea: Optimize prototype margins within a nested feature-space partition so quantized one-step outputs preserve teacher terminal-cell membership.
VseZJ6MGKd.evidence: Counterexamples and conditional feature-space Wasserstein bounds support the objective, with experiments on Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10 and class-conditioned ImageNet-256.
VseZJ6MGKd.claimed_gains: CM-QAT enables generation with weights as low as 2-bit and 3-bit using a single step (1-NFE).
VseZJ6MGKd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the terminal-geometry perspective and reported generation-quality improvements at low precision.
VseZJ6MGKd.main_concern: Baseline objectives, initializations, and evaluation conditions are insufficiently matched or documented to establish fair comparisons.

YvPe6D85Lz.one_liner: Signal-and-noise coefficient dynamics track how network topology and client placement shape decentralized feature learning.
YvPe6D85Lz.problem: Optimization and consensus theory does not explain how decentralized communication affects learned features and individual clients' generalization.
YvPe6D85Lz.method: The paper tracks predictive-signal and sample-noise coefficients during decentralized gradient descent for two-layer CNNs. Topology-aware quantities yield early generalization and fitted-iterate risk guarantees, with an extension to periodic local updates.
YvPe6D85Lz.key_idea: Track how communication propagates signal and sample-specific noise coefficients to derive client-dependent learning and risk quantities.
YvPe6D85Lz.evidence: Theoretical bounds for two-layer CNNs accompany synthetic and real-data experiments under IID and non-IID partitions, including controlled client-placement comparisons.
YvPe6D85Lz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the feature-learning view and its explanation of placement effects that graph connectivity alone misses.
YvPe6D85Lz.main_concern: The guarantees cover a restrictive signal–noise model and client-local risk, limiting their implications for broader heterogeneous-data generalization.

vIS18zNPOe.one_liner: Overlapping payload windows form a trellis for exact watermark decoding and guide adaptive watermark strength under a KL budget.
vIS18zNPOe.problem: Position-wise watermarks fragment evidence, while whole-message scoring makes exact decoding costly as payload size grows.
vIS18zNPOe.method: TrellisMark assigns each token to an overlapping local payload window and strengthens its evidence with multiple independent heads. Trellis decoding recovers the maximum-score message, and online allocation varies strength according to recovery value under a cumulative KL budget.
vIS18zNPOe.key_idea: Share token evidence through overlapping payload windows, decode their trellis exactly, and allocate strength using current competitor margins.
vIS18zNPOe.evidence: The paper proves recovery and online-allocation regret bounds and reports exact-message recovery and recovery–quality comparisons against watermarking baselines.
vIS18zNPOe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate overlapping windows as a compromise between shared payload evidence and tractable exact decoding.
vIS18zNPOe.main_concern: Exact message recovery deteriorates substantially under mild text edits, leaving practical robustness uncertain.

9kAjBKFTjd.one_liner: Elimination-forest layers schedule independent parallel reveals, with tree depth determining exact unmasking rounds in ferromagnetic Ising models.
9kAjBKFTjd.problem: Exact single-coordinate conditionals do not prevent independent parallel commitments from distorting a joint distribution.
9kAjBKFTjd.method: The paper characterizes exact parallel sampling by separation in the dependency graph after previously revealed vertices are removed. Minimum-height elimination forests define optimal fixed commit-once schedules, and a KL decomposition separates factorization error from learned-conditional error.
9kAjBKFTjd.key_idea: Reveal elimination-forest layers so no residual path connects variables sampled together, making the minimum exact round count equal tree depth.
9kAjBKFTjd.evidence: Theoretical characterizations and KL results accompany synthetic Ising experiments with planner-aware training and comparisons to dependency-guided decoding baselines.
9kAjBKFTjd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the exact tree-depth characterization and separation of parallelization error from conditional-model error.
9kAjBKFTjd.main_concern: Reliance on a known dependency graph and synthetic Ising evaluations leaves applicability to realistic language distributions unestablished.

jBNgeyO5p9.one_liner: Difference-of-convex duality recasts matching as implicit registration with modular optimal-transport subproblems.
jBNgeyO5p9.problem: Problem-specific matching solvers make it difficult to address varied matching objectives within a common optimization framework.
jBNgeyO5p9.method: The paper rewrites difference-of-convex matching objectives as implicit registration problems and derives a dual optimization formulation. It applies this framework to quadratic matching, including balanced and unbalanced Gromov–Wasserstein variants, with modular regularized optimal-transport solvers.
jBNgeyO5p9.key_idea: Separate the nonconvex matching term from convex transport through a dual registration formulation that permits interchangeable transport subproblem solvers.
jBNgeyO5p9.evidence: Convergence analyses include inexact inner updates, and numerical studies cover graphs, point clouds, meshes, word embeddings, and fracture matching.
jBNgeyO5p9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the common mathematical framework, modular solver design, and analysis that accounts for inexact computation.
jBNgeyO5p9.main_concern: Targeted quantitative comparisons do not sufficiently establish the added contribution over existing matching-to-registration and dual Gromov–Wasserstein methods.

kCYXuqBxmm.one_liner: Paired runs with and without individual skills estimate their utility on generated, execution-verified repository requirements.
kCYXuqBxmm.problem: The practical benefit of an individual software-engineering agent skill is unclear before installation.
kCYXuqBxmm.method: SWE-Skills-Bench pairs public skills with pinned repositories, generates ten requirements per skill, and builds deterministic verifiers and containers. Paired evaluations aggregate outcome changes into per-skill utility profiles and statistically classify skills as helpful, ineffective, or harmful.
kCYXuqBxmm.key_idea: Hold the repository, requirement, verifier, and agent configuration fixed while toggling skill access to measure per-skill outcome changes.
kCYXuqBxmm.evidence: The benchmark covers 98 skills with ten requirements each under four agent–model configurations, yielding 3,920 paired evaluations.
kCYXuqBxmm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the skill-focused paired evaluation and findings that procedural guidance can help or harm depending on the model and agent configuration.
