kCYXuqBxmm.main_concern: Automatically generated requirements and verifiers lack sufficient independent validation to establish that measured skill utility reflects correct task behavior.

pq9psxBn7R.one_liner: Enhances low-light images using CP-factorized 5D illumination-contrast photometric and channel-pair spatial detail lookup tables.
pq9psxBn7R.problem: RGB-only lookup tables cannot distinguish identically colored pixels under different illumination and contrast, while channel-independent spatial lookups neglect cross-channel structural coherence.
pq9psxBn7R.method: PD-Net cascades a Dual-Condition Photometric LUT (DCP-LUT) indexing RGB values with illumination and dual-scale contrast maps in 5D, followed by a Channel-Pair Spatial Detail LUT (CSD-LUT) using channel-pair projection, rotation-cascaded dilated L-shaped lookups, and cyclic Gauss-Seidel propagation. Each 5D LUT is parameterized as a sum of rank-one tensors via canonical polyadic (CP) decomposition to avoid materializing dense grids.
pq9psxBn7R.key_idea: Cascade a 5D illumination-and-contrast photometric lookup table with a channel-pair Gauss-Seidel spatial detail lookup table parameterized via canonical polyadic tensor decomposition.
pq9psxBn7R.evidence: Evaluated across nine paired and unpaired low-light image enhancement benchmarks (including SICE and FiveK) under full-reference and no-reference protocols.
pq9psxBn7R.claimed_gains: Reduces 5D lookup-table storage complexity from O(N^5) to O(KN); quantitative image-enhancement gains are cut off in the truncated abstract.
pq9psxBn7R.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating 5D context-conditioned photometric lookup from cross-channel spatial lookup with CP tensor factorization is technically coherent and backed by ablations.
pq9psxBn7R.main_concern: Reviewers flag missing dataset-split and LUT hyperparameter specifications, overstated novelty relative to prior conditioned and CP-factorized LUTs (4D LUT, WLUT, AttentionLUT), and an incorrect bibliography citation for CIDNet.

VrqTtI50Vj.one_liner: Distills pretrained diffusion text-image attention into a Layer-0 visual token scorer refined via budget-preserving Swap-GRPO reinforcement learning.
VrqTtI50Vj.problem: Visual token pruners relying on internal VLM attention signals suffer from structural biases like attention sinks that misidentify query-relevant visual regions.
VrqTtI50Vj.method: The framework offline-distills text-image cross-attention from a pretrained diffusion model into DiffScorer, a lightweight module that selects query-relevant visual tokens at Layer 0 prior to LLM prefill. Counterfactual Swap-GRPO then refines DiffScorer alone by exploring budget-preserving token swaps around its deterministic selection using answer rewards from the frozen VLM.
VrqTtI50Vj.key_idea: Distill pretrained diffusion cross-attention offline into a lightweight pre-LLM token scorer and refine selections via budget-preserving token-swap GRPO rewarded by frozen-VLM answers.
VrqTtI50Vj.evidence: Evaluated across two VLM architectures, multiple pruning ratios, and visual understanding benchmarks including HR-Bench 8K and Box+SAM supervision controls.
VrqTtI50Vj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find offline distillation of diffusion text-image attention into an inference-light Layer-0 token scorer well motivated and effective across retention ratios.
VrqTtI50Vj.main_concern: Reviewers note that experiments do not cleanly isolate diffusion supervision against matched VLM-attention distillation or stronger grounding teachers, while Swap-GRPO adds small gains and omits recent pruning baselines.

6wGCmRrlUF.one_liner: Clusters training examples by gradient similarity to estimate cluster utility from few scored representatives and allocate selection budgets.
6wGCmRrlUF.problem: Pointwise data-attribution methods score every training candidate independently at high compute cost while selecting redundant examples with overlapping gradient behavior.
6wGCmRrlUF.method: ACE groups candidate samples into clusters by gradient similarity, scores a small number of representatives per cluster to form an unbiased, variance-controlled cluster utility estimator, and allocates the selection budget across clusters.
6wGCmRrlUF.key_idea: Group training examples by gradient similarity, score a few cluster representatives for unbiased cluster-level utility estimation, and allocate data-selection budgets across clusters.
6wGCmRrlUF.evidence: Supported by estimator unbiasedness and variance proofs plus LLM post-training (Llama-3.2-3B, Mistral-7B) and pre-training data-selection experiments using Qwen2.5-0.5B proxy gradients against baselines including OPUS.
6wGCmRrlUF.claimed_gains: Achieves up to a 33.8x end-to-end speedup in post-training—surpassing full-data training on Llama-3.2-3B and Mistral-7B using 10% of data—and an 8.86x speedup over sample-level OPUS in pre-training.
6wGCmRrlUF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that lifting data attribution and budget allocation from individual samples to gradient-similar clusters yields large selection speedups while reducing redundancy.
6wGCmRrlUF.main_concern: Reviewers cite incremental novelty over existing attribution scores, unisolated ablations separating representative scoring from budget allocation, and unclear alignment between Qwen2.5-0.5B clustering gradients and larger target models.

3ZaqCR58b5.one_liner: Decomposes node trajectories into background, accumulation-release, and shock roles before learning delayed physical propagation and functional graph relations.
3ZaqCR58b5.problem: Learning spatiotemporal graph relations directly from raw node series entangles persistent background evolution with gradual accumulation and sparse shocks.
3ZaqCR58b5.method: CANDOR decomposes each node trajectory into persistent background, gradual accumulation-release, and sparse shock components. Conditioned on these components, a delay-aware physical branch models directed topological propagation while a topology-unconstrained functional branch infers latent dependencies from background dynamics, combined via context-adaptive fusion.
3ZaqCR58b5.key_idea: Decompose local trajectories into persistent background, accumulation-release, and shock components before coupling a delay-aware directed topological branch with a background-conditioned functional graph branch.
3ZaqCR58b5.evidence: Evaluated against 15 baselines over three seeds across two urban traffic benchmarks (including METR-LA) and three newly constructed river water-quality datasets.
3ZaqCR58b5.claimed_gains: Achieves the lowest aggregate normalized error across five datasets, outperforming the overall runner-up by 7.25%.
3ZaqCR58b5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers commend the strong forecasting performance of the compact (~0.9M parameter) model across 15 baselines and two domains, including three new river dissolved-oxygen datasets.
3ZaqCR58b5.main_concern: Reviewers highlight the omission of closely related D2STGNN from both citations and baselines despite strong module-level similarity, alongside non-parameter-matched decomposition ablations.

xuRSWArTbY.one_liner: Co-trains Diffusion Transformer robot policies by denoising the current observation alongside action prediction without future-frame targets.
xuRSWArTbY.problem: Adapting pretrained generative Diffusion Transformers to robot control commonly relies on costly future visual prediction during co-training even when omitted at inference.
xuRSWArTbY.method: NowWAM introduces a future-target-free co-training formulation that denoises the current observation across noise levels while predicting robot actions from the same visual stream. Coupling action prediction to the continuum of current-observation denoising states adapts the generative prior without synthesizing future frames.
xuRSWArTbY.key_idea: Denoise the current visual observation while predicting robot actions from the shared Diffusion Transformer visual stream across noise levels instead of predicting future frames.
xuRSWArTbY.evidence: Evaluated on simulated robot control benchmarks including LIBERO-Plus with FLUX2-Klein, alongside controlled comparisons of past, current, clean-endpoint, and future visual targets.
xuRSWArTbY.claimed_gains: Reaches 87.7% on LIBERO-Plus with FLUX2-Klein, improving over the future-target co-training baseline by 6.1 points while halving training cost.
xuRSWArTbY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find re-examining the necessity of future visual prediction well motivated and appreciate the simple, training-efficient current-observation denoising design and controlled target ablations.
xuRSWArTbY.main_concern: Reviewers note the absence of real-world robot experiments and inference latency measurements, plus limited mechanistic analysis distinguishing generative adaptation from denoising self-supervised representation learning.

USCZMv1mhe.one_liner: Transforms static 3D human avatars into dynamic 4D avatars by decoding video-diffusion dynamic textures into 3D Gaussians.
USCZMv1mhe.problem: Person-agnostic static 3D avatars lack pose-dependent clothing wrinkles, whereas person-specific dynamic avatars require expensive multi-view capture per subject.
USCZMv1mhe.method: AvatarDynamizer upgrades off-the-shelf static avatars into controllable 4D avatars using a video-diffusion-based Dynamic Texture Generator to produce motion-dependent surface textures, which a Generalized Gaussian Decoder maps into 3D Gaussians for multi-view-consistent rendering. The authors also collect a dense multi-view human motion dataset (DynaHuman) to bridge identity-rich and motion-rich data.
USCZMv1mhe.key_idea: Generate motion-dependent surface dynamics in 2D texture space with a video diffusion model and decode them into 3D Gaussians for multi-view-consistent avatar rendering.
USCZMv1mhe.evidence: Evaluated across four datasets including the newly collected multi-view DynaHuman dataset against competing dynamic avatar baselines.
USCZMv1mhe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that using dynamic textures to bridge pretrained video diffusion priors with explicit 3D Gaussian rendering is well motivated and supported by the new DynaHuman dataset.
USCZMv1mhe.main_concern: Reviewers cite unvalidated 3D geometric deformation versus texture-only shading effects, limited component novelty over prior dynamic-texture Gaussian works, modified baseline reimplementations, and unreported inference FPS.

OXbXgquphd.one_liner: Low-rank fusion, task-identity disentanglement, and prototype quantization suppress identity re-leakage after multimodal fusion.
OXbXgquphd.problem: Fusing separately protected EEG and eye-movement representations can recombine residual cues and restore subject identifiability.
OXbXgquphd.method: PrivFusionNet reweights cross-modal interactions by task utility and identity risk, attenuates identity directions in the fused space, and quantizes representations into subject-shared task prototypes. It directly optimizes privacy at the fusion level.
OXbXgquphd.key_idea: Protect the fused representation through risk-weighted interactions, identity-direction removal, and subject-shared prototype quantization.
OXbXgquphd.evidence: Leave-one-session-out identity attacks and leave-one-subject-out emotion recognition evaluate EEG-eye fusion on SEED-IV and SEED-V.
OXbXgquphd.claimed_gains: User identification accuracy falls from 25.33% to 7.57% on SEED-IV and from 46.38% to 6.11% on SEED-V under leave-one-session-out evaluation.
OXbXgquphd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that demonstrating identity re-emergence after fusion exposes a relevant weakness of unimodal privacy protection.
OXbXgquphd.main_concern: Simple fusion-level privacy baselines are absent, and ablations suggest the codebook drives most of the privacy improvement.

41KgJBDu3u.one_liner: Structural-entropy graph partitions shortlist experts before capability-conditioned retrieval selects one responder.
41KgJBDu3u.problem: Querying every heterogeneous language-model expert to choose a responder is prohibitively expensive for query-level routing.
41KgJBDu3u.method: SEER partitions train-only query-expert outcomes into semantic communities using two-dimensional structural entropy, then exports a Top-3 candidate set with local memory correction. A capability planner and route selector use retrieved historical outcomes and separate GRPO policies to choose one expert before answering.
41KgJBDu3u.key_idea: Use structural graph communities for candidate search and capability-conditioned historical evidence for final expert selection.
41KgJBDu3u.evidence: Evaluation spans 20 benchmarks with open-source and closed-source expert pools and includes routing ablations.
41KgJBDu3u.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the interpretable division between graph-based candidate pruning and evidence-based language selection without inspecting current responses.
41KgJBDu3u.main_concern: Two trained 4B policies and extra generation steps lack matched cost comparisons, while repaired training candidates complicate evaluation fairness.

jTZo4036Yx.one_liner: Same-state counterfactual branching trains a coordinator to choose modular or end-to-end embodied policies.
jTZo4036Yx.problem: Embodied coding agents cannot learn which policy family succeeds in a physical state when only outcomes of selected branches are observed.
jTZo4036Yx.method: RoboAware organizes skills into five semantic stages and restores identical states to execute each admissible policy family. Execution-Aware Learning combines Monte Carlo tree search with Q-learning to distill counterfactual outcomes into family-conditioned values.
jTZo4036Yx.key_idea: Learn family-selection values from counterfactual outcomes generated by executing alternative policy branches from locked physical states.
jTZo4036Yx.evidence: Single-episode evaluations cover 100 tasks, with routing ablations and tests across RoboSuite, LIBERO-Pro, and RoboTwin.
jTZo4036Yx.claimed_gains: RoboAware reaches a 77.0% overall success rate and a 90.0% average on RoboSuite.
jTZo4036Yx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that same-state counterfactual outcomes address selection bias and that internal routing ablations support adaptive coordination.
jTZo4036Yx.main_concern: Training and evaluation use the same 100 tasks with different scene seeds, and weakened external baselines prevent clean generalization and superiority claims.

i7INKmVQYZ.one_liner: Reflection-alignment rewards and sampled-failure abstention improve reasoning reliability within one structured completion.
i7INKmVQYZ.problem: Large reasoning models hallucinate through both flawed inference and missing factual knowledge, which require different reliability behaviors.
i7INKmVQYZ.method: REIN trains a think-reflection-answer sequence for explicit self-critique before answering. A separate reward encourages abstention when no sampled reasoning chain yields a correct answer, without inference-time controllers or multi-round critiques.
i7INKmVQYZ.key_idea: Align reflection with draft correctness and use sampled completion failures as the training signal for knowledge-boundary abstention.
i7INKmVQYZ.evidence: Mathematical and commonsense reasoning evaluations span multiple model families and include component ablations and reflection diagnostics.
i7INKmVQYZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value addressing reasoning and knowledge hallucinations separately within a single-pass reflection-and-abstention framework.
i7INKmVQYZ.main_concern: Sampled failures are an imperfect knowledge signal, and the framework largely combines established reflection and abstention training methods.

ezBYm2cIpd.one_liner: Partitioned-path supervision trains weather-conditioned variable-span transitions for vegetation rollouts from generated states.
ezBYm2cIpd.problem: World-model representations can lose predictive value when forecasts continue from generated intermediate states rather than observed history.
ezBYm2cIpd.method: SpanWorld advances a latent spatial vegetation state through shared weather-conditioned variable-span transitions. Partitioned-path learning supervises direct predictions at every date and predictions continued from model-generated states under sampled temporal partitions.
ezBYm2cIpd.key_idea: Train one variable-span transition on random temporal partitions using observed endpoints for both direct and composed forecast paths.
ezBYm2cIpd.evidence: GreenEarthNet's 100-day dense NDVI forecasting task supports direct-versus-continued comparisons, state replacement tests, and weather replacement tests.
ezBYm2cIpd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value separating direct endpoint accuracy from continued-prediction accuracy and the controlled comparison that changes only the supervision path.
ezBYm2cIpd.main_concern: Methodological novelty over Deep-OSG is unclear, and the central comparison relies on one seed and an in-house control.

iizvKiY6w4.one_liner: Instruction-guided expert selection and cross-modal token weighting reduce interference in streaming visual instruction tuning.
iizvKiY6w4.problem: Task-incremental continual visual instruction tuning does not handle interleaved, recurring, and disappearing tasks within streaming data chunks.
iizvKiY6w4.method: StrLoRA first selects a sparse expert subset from textual instructions, then weights selected experts token by token using cross-modal attention between local visual tokens and the global instruction. A regularized two-stage framework supports learning without explicit task labels.
iizvKiY6w4.key_idea: Route instructions to sparse experts before applying visual-token-dependent weights within the selected subset.
iizvKiY6w4.evidence: Experiments cover InternVL and Gemma backbones, two data streams, varied stream lengths and task compositions, component ablations, and unseen instructions.
iizvKiY6w4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that mixed streaming tasks are practically relevant and that StrLoRA improves aggregate performance and forgetting across backbones.
iizvKiY6w4.main_concern: Comparisons do not isolate cross-modal token weighting from simpler routing or rule out reliance on dataset-specific instruction templates.

92fSAxVgsh.one_liner: Reliability calibration selects and merges complementary visual-only and visual-text SAM3 segmentation candidates.
92fSAxVgsh.problem: Class-name text can either help or hurt frozen SAM3 visual prompting under cross-domain few-shot segmentation shifts.
92fSAxVgsh.method: A shared support-query canvas feeds visual-only and visual-text branches that generate candidate masks. SAM3 confidence, support-query prototype consistency, and cross-branch agreement estimate reliability for mask selection and merging without training or learnable modules.
92fSAxVgsh.key_idea: Calibrate candidates from complementary SAM3 prompting branches using confidence, prototype consistency, and inter-branch agreement.
92fSAxVgsh.evidence: Cross-domain few-shot benchmarks span natural images, remote sensing, and medical imaging under 1-shot and 5-shot evaluation.
92fSAxVgsh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the simple fully frozen pipeline and strong average results without source-domain data or parameter updates.
92fSAxVgsh.main_concern: Ablations do not separate candidate pooling from calibration benefits, and the closest frozen-SAM3 predecessor is not directly compared.

bmsV6bCBe7.one_liner: Evidence-conditioned escape rooms separate association, observation, intervention, and counterfactual reasoning in interactive agents.
bmsV6bCBe7.problem: Interactive task success can hide an agent's failure to recover causal structure that remains useful after conditions or objectives change.
bmsV6bCBe7.method: ELEMENTARY generates escape-room tasks under four evidence regimes and validates that permitted evidence determines each solution. Intervention transfer and historical replay tests distinguish immediate control success from reusable causal knowledge.
bmsV6bCBe7.key_idea: Control solution-relevant evidence availability within shared interactive environments to separate identifiability from agent reasoning failure.
bmsV6bCBe7.evidence: Seven proprietary and open-weight LLMs are evaluated on 120 original validated questions, with 120 independently generated questions and repeated-run robustness checks.
bmsV6bCBe7.claimed_gains: The highest average success rate is only 44.2%; in I3 Causal Propagation, all 70/70 episodes reach the first control target, but only 1/70 reaches the second.
bmsV6bCBe7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the evidence-regime design, solvability validation, and intervention-transfer result exposing the gap between control and reusable mechanism knowledge.
bmsV6bCBe7.main_concern: Ten fixed instances per family, limited repetitions, and missing heuristic or budget-relaxed controls make low causal-transfer scores hard to interpret.

SJzojGYfA1.one_liner: Pairs VLM active-light source reasoning with a recurrent physical decomposition backend for multi-illuminant white balance.
SJzojGYfA1.problem: Visible light fixtures poorly indicate true scene illumination because sources may be off, hidden, or spatially overlapping, and real datasets lack per-source labels.
SJzojGYfA1.method: AskLight uses a VLM to filter detected light proposals, infer hidden active sources, and map each source to a dominant region, initializing a recurrent differentiable decomposition backend. The authors also render Infinigen-Light with per-source activity, visibility, and region annotations.
SJzojGYfA1.key_idea: Uses a VLM to construct an explicit active-source-to-region inventory that initializes a recurrent physical illumination decomposition backend.
SJzojGYfA1.evidence: Evaluated on the newly rendered Infinigen-Light synthetic dataset and LSMI splits.
SJzojGYfA1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the active-source framing is well-motivated and the Infinigen-Light dataset is a useful contribution.
SJzojGYfA1.main_concern: Reviewers note that the VLM's specific gain is not isolated from the recurrent backend or photometric priors, and that pipeline compute cost and generalization are uncharacterized.

E2c5ed5Rew.one_liner: Human-annotated benchmark of data and control input-output dependences in LLM agents for evaluating information flow tracking.
E2c5ed5Rew.problem: Information flow tracking defenses against prompt injection rely on estimating LLM output-input dependences, but no human ground-truth benchmark exists.
E2c5ed5Rew.method: Witness provides fine-grained human-annotated data and control dependences across 11 agents over benign and prompt-injected trajectories as a testable oracle. Twelve frontier and open-weight models are evaluated on recovering exact dependence sets.
E2c5ed5Rew.key_idea: Formulates an LLM agent's output-input data and control dependences as a standalone human-annotated oracle for benchmarking IFT analyzers.
E2c5ed5Rew.evidence: Evaluated 12 frontier and open-weight models across 11 agents on benign and prompt-injected trajectories.
E2c5ed5Rew.claimed_gains: Even the best evaluated model recovers an output's exact dependence set only half the time.
E2c5ed5Rew.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark fills an important gap for prompt-injection security by isolating dependency identification and exposing poor control-dependence recall.
E2c5ed5Rew.main_concern: Reviewers note that human counterfactual annotations are partly semantic and subjective rather than direct causal interventions on the underlying models.

Rx5QwawqpH.one_liner: Hierarchical agent memory that contrasts successful and failed trajectories to extract evidence anchors for abstraction and retrieval.
Rx5QwawqpH.problem: Agent memories face a trade-off between noisy full trajectories and over-abstracted rules that lose their evidential grounding.
Rx5QwawqpH.method: HIERAMEM contrasts trajectories with different outcomes to extract discriminative action-observation evidence anchors, which constrain rule abstraction into a three-level hierarchy. At inference, success and failure anchors index retrieval at task and decision levels.
Rx5QwawqpH.key_idea: Extracts contrastive action-observation evidence anchors to both ground abstract memory formation and address two-level inference retrieval.
Rx5QwawqpH.evidence: Evaluated across five agent benchmarks and multiple LLM backbones with component ablations.
Rx5QwawqpH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the motivation is clear and using evidence anchors for both memory abstraction and dual-level retrieval is intuitive.
Rx5QwawqpH.main_concern: Reviewers point out missing variance/dispersion across runs, lack of retrieval hit-rate evaluation, and overly complex mathematical notation.

PqLXqLOXq6.one_liner: Trajectory-centric benchmark synchronizing streaming VLM outputs with visual states to score proactivity, silence, latency, and memory.
PqLXqLOXq6.problem: Isolated VideoQA evaluations miss continuous streaming assistant behaviors such as when to speak, stay silent, or respond quickly.
PqLXqLOXq6.method: SVI-Bench comprises 75 expert-authored items across nine categories with 272 rubric criteria covering five interaction dimensions. Its InteractFlow framework logs synchronized visual frames and model outputs to allow inspectable, rescorable trace evaluation.
PqLXqLOXq6.key_idea: Synchronizes streaming VLM outputs with contemporaneous visual states in saved traces to score five trajectory-level interaction dimensions.
PqLXqLOXq6.evidence: Evaluated five deployed streaming VLM configurations across 75 items and 272 criteria.
PqLXqLOXq6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that evaluating human-perceived streaming trajectories with traceable, rescorable logs addresses a genuine evaluation gap.
PqLXqLOXq6.main_concern: Reviewers flag inconsistent latency clocks across items (wall time versus adapter-reported inference time) and the small, category-imbalanced 75-item dataset.

U1tOxNuTS6.one_liner: Proposes EvoRS, evolving an executable Reward-DAG via an agentic designer using on-policy rollouts during open-ended RL.
U1tOxNuTS6.problem: Fixed rubric-based reward systems in open-ended RL become unreliable over training due to reward hacking, coverage gaps, and reduced discriminability.
U1tOxNuTS6.method: EvoRS represents the reward system as an executable Reward-DAG and uses an agentic designer to update rubrics, scoring mechanisms, and signal composition from on-policy rollouts and reward traces.
U1tOxNuTS6.key_idea: Updates an executable Reward-DAG (criteria, scorers, composition) on-policy via an agentic designer diagnosed from rollout traces.
U1tOxNuTS6.evidence: Evaluated on writing and roleplay tasks across three judges, plus ablations against fixed reward systems.
U1tOxNuTS6.claimed_gains: Across writing and roleplay, EvoRS outperforms the base policy by 2.107 and 4.767 points, respectively, under all three judges.
U1tOxNuTS6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find evolving the entire reward system via a Reward-DAG well-motivated for mitigating reward hacking in open-ended RL and note consistent gains on writing and roleplay.
U1tOxNuTS6.main_concern: Experiments use only Qwen models without compute-matched or close dynamic-rubric baselines (e.g., EvoRubric), and failure-diagnosis reliability and LLM designer cost are insufficiently analyzed.

ACuCPfyRs1.one_liner: Proposes FoRA, detaching frozen LLM features into a client-side factorized residual adapter for forward-only federated fine-tuning.
ACuCPfyRs1.problem: Federated LLM fine-tuning faces a trade-off between memory-heavy client backpropagation through the backbone and noisy zeroth-order optimization.
ACuCPfyRs1.method: FoRA keeps the LLM backbone frozen and forward-only, detaching multi-level representations into a local Split-and-Bridge factorized residual adapter trained with first-order gradients and global-reference function-space regularization.
ACuCPfyRs1.key_idea: Trains a local factorized residual adapter with first-order gradients on detached multi-level frozen backbone representations, regularized in function space.
ACuCPfyRs1.evidence: Non-convex convergence and memory-separation analysis plus experiments comparing against first-order PEFT and FedMeZO baselines.
ACuCPfyRs1.claimed_gains: Reduces peak allocated client GPU memory by 27.3%-59.2% over first-order baselines and outperforms FedMeZO by 6.99-18.37 points in Final-10 Accuracy.
ACuCPfyRs1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate targeting client memory bottlenecks in federated LLM fine-tuning by keeping the backbone forward-only while retaining exact first-order local updates.
ACuCPfyRs1.main_concern: The unmergeable side module adds inference latency, novelty over detached side-tuning is limited, and evaluations omit complex reasoning, math, or code tasks and full communication-cost analysis.

bCbhbH5Xrv.one_liner: Proposes SCORPIO, scaling post-nonlinear causal discovery via sigmoid normalizing flows and local likelihood-based greedy edge ordering.
bCbhbH5Xrv.problem: Existing multivariate post-nonlinear causal discovery methods rely on recursive sink identification and fail to scale beyond small graphs.
bCbhbH5Xrv.method: SCORPIO parameterizes inverse outer transforms with strictly monotone sigmoid normalizing flows for tractable node likelihoods, greedily adds edges by local likelihood gain, and prunes via marginal residual independence tests.
bCbhbH5Xrv.key_idea: Uses monotone sigmoid normalizing flows for tractable node likelihoods to greedily learn topological order via local-only model updates.
bCbhbH5Xrv.evidence: Synthetic experiments across noise families, mechanisms, densities, and 100-500 variables plus a semi-synthetic manufacturing dataset.
bCbhbH5Xrv.claimed_gains: Under a 24-hour limit, SCORPIO is the only evaluated multivariate PNL method completing beyond 100 variables, scaling up to 500 variables.
bCbhbH5Xrv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize substantial wall-clock speedups (21.6 min vs 13.7 h at 100 variables) that make multivariate PNL causal discovery feasible at 100-500 variables.
bCbhbH5Xrv.main_concern: Greedy ordering lacks population-level consistency guarantees, ablations do not isolate flow likelihood from greedy ordering, and utility beyond sparse synthetic PNL data is unestablished.

ELBzqPEx8A.one_liner: Proposes PReViD, replaying student rollouts with teacher-side clear-image and evidence prefixes filtered by a placebo prefix.
ELBzqPEx8A.problem: In visual on-policy distillation, early visual mistakes remain in the student response history and distort the teacher's subsequent contextual supervision.
ELBzqPEx8A.method: PReViD replays the student rollout under controlled clear-image and evidence-prefix contexts, subtracts a placebo text-only prefix to isolate visual/contextual effects, and reweights teacher supervision accordingly.
ELBzqPEx8A.key_idea: Replays student rollouts under teacher-side visual and evidence prefixes, using a placebo prefix to filter generic text effects without altering inference.
ELBzqPEx8A.evidence: Evaluated across detailed visual understanding benchmarks (including V*, Zoom, MME-EN), model scales, and teacher settings with random-gate and shuffled-prefix controls.
ELBzqPEx8A.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the clean, zero-inference-overhead teacher-side interventional replay design and consistent gains on detailed visual understanding benchmarks.
ELBzqPEx8A.main_concern: A direct plain-OPD baseline using the same privileged clear image and evidence prefix is missing, and re-implemented baselines score below their published numbers.

VlHmHiE5g4.one_liner: Proposes MPQ, projecting policy action chunks onto B-spline demonstration prototypes at execution time to diagnose skill-policy failures.
VlHmHiE5g4.problem: Jointly learned latent skill codebooks and decoders confound whether closed-loop policy failures stem from the vocabulary, skill selection, or execution.
VlHmHiE5g4.method: MPQ places a parameter-free library of B-spline demonstration segments after the policy, snapping predicted action chunks to yaw-aligned nearest prototypes with bounded corrections, and swaps selector/reference components one at a time.
VlHmHiE5g4.key_idea: Places a parameter-free B-spline demonstration library after trained policies to attribute closed-loop failure between selection and execution.
VlHmHiE5g4.evidence: Evaluated across six policy architectures in simulation (including a 7B VLA) and component-swapping diagnostics on LIBERO-90 with 256 prototypes across three backbones.
VlHmHiE5g4.claimed_gains: Across six architectures in simulation, wrapping policies with MPQ changes task success by +0.6 points on average.
VlHmHiE5g4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the fixed B-spline prototype execution layer clean and well-motivated for preserving policy performance while diagnosing skill-policy failures.
VlHmHiE5g4.main_concern: Full selection-execution diagnostics rely on ACT-derived selectors where ACT still predicts full actions, and calling the reference comparator a ceiling overstates Equation 1.

Hp0hn0O6vs.one_liner: Detects LLM-generated text by projecting a frozen reader LLM's intermediate layer into vocabulary space to score style signatures.
Hp0hn0O6vs.problem: Existing LLM-generated text detectors output opaque probabilities or rewrite scores without exposing human-readable internal concepts behind their verdicts.
Hp0hn0O6vs.method: VisScore decodes a single intermediate layer of a frozen reader LLM into its vocabulary space, identifies LLM-signature and human-signature vocabularies from train-split logit differentials, and scores documents by their activation hit rates on these named words.
Hp0hn0O6vs.key_idea: Projects one frozen reader LLM layer into vocabulary space and scores documents by hit rates on train-derived LLM- versus human-register signature words.
Hp0hn0O6vs.evidence: Evaluated on DetectRL-X spanning eight languages, four generators, and six domains, including altered LLM-generated text.
Hp0hn0O6vs.claimed_gains: VisScore reaches a document-level AUC of 99.8 on DetectRL-X.
Hp0hn0O6vs.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that VisScore's vocabulary-space scoring is simple, well presented, interpretable, and achieves strong empirical detection results.
Hp0hn0O6vs.main_concern: Reviewers cite missing related work (such as Text Fluoroscopy), incremental novelty over RepreGuard and SeqXGPT, and discrepancies in how baseline methods were reimplemented.

A4riN1KQtP.one_liner: Parameterizes continuous MDP transitions with analytically normalizable squared neural families for provable regret and MLE-based RL.
A4riN1KQtP.problem: Model-based continuous RL approaches often have intractable partition functions or lack joint theoretical regret bounds and practical implementations.
A4riN1KQtP.method: The authors define Squared Family MDPs whose transition densities are parameterized by non-negative squared families with analytically computable normalizers. They derive a sublinear regret bound and implement RESNEF, which learns transition densities via exact MLE to extract representations for continuous control.
A4riN1KQtP.key_idea: Squared neural family transition models yield non-negative densities with analytical normalizers, enabling exact MLE training alongside Hellinger-based regret bounds.
A4riN1KQtP.evidence: Theoretical regret analysis and empirical evaluations on diverse continuous control tasks (including HalfCheetah and Humanoid) vs. SAC, DiffSR, and CTRL.
A4riN1KQtP.claimed_gains: Derives an tilde-O(dH sqrt(T)) regret bound and reports up to 40% performance improvements over baselines across continuous control tasks.
A4riN1KQtP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that analytically normalizable squared-family densities neatly solve partition-function intractability for MLE-based transition modeling.
A4riN1KQtP.main_concern: Reviewers point out a gap between the theoretical algorithm and neural RESNEF, inconsistent task performance (trailing SAC on Humanoid), and 13.4x higher wall-clock time per iteration.

cc1sddTsQo.one_liner: Couples low-rank compression and quantization via quantization-aware compression (QaMC) and activation stabilization (ASQ) for LLM deployment.
cc1sddTsQo.problem: Applying model compression and quantization independently to LLMs yields suboptimal accuracy under low memory budgets due to compression-induced distribution shifts and rank-order changes.
cc1sddTsQo.method: The authors propose CoCaQ, combining quantization-aware model compression (QaMC) to construct quantization-friendly low-rank representations and optimize layer-wise ranks with a quantization-aware loss, with activation stabilization for quantization (ASQ) using norm balancing and orthogonal rotation smoothing.
cc1sddTsQo.key_idea: Jointly optimizing layer-wise low-rank compression under quantization sensitivity while stabilizing intermediate bottleneck activations aligns compressed structures with low-bit quantization.
cc1sddTsQo.evidence: Experiments across multiple LLM families (including Qwen3-8B), compression ratios, and quantization bit-widths, plus W4A8 latency evaluations in the appendix.
cc1sddTsQo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the motivation clear, the bottleneck diagnosis convincing, and the experimental comparisons across models and compression ratios comprehensive.
cc1sddTsQo.main_concern: Reviewers consider the methodological novelty incremental over existing SVD/quantization techniques and note missing GPU inference-speed analysis and unclear compression-quantization configuration selection.

0fqzhOkEtI.one_liner: Trains machine learning force fields without precomputed DFT labels by minimizing the variational Kohn-Sham energy of predicted densities.
0fqzhOkEtI.problem: Supervised machine learning force fields require expensive converged SCF DFT calculations to label every training geometry.
0fqzhOkEtI.method: The network predicts an atomic-orbital matrix whose eigendecomposition yields an admissible electronic density, trained by minimizing the variational Kohn-Sham energy over unlabelled geometries from empirical force-field trajectories.
0fqzhOkEtI.key_idea: Minimizes the variational Kohn-Sham energy of the network's own predicted electronic density matrix over unlabelled molecular geometries.
0fqzhOkEtI.evidence: Evaluations on ten organic molecules (rMD17) and the 3BPA temperature-extrapolation benchmark compared against DFT and MLIP baselines.
0fqzhOkEtI.claimed_gains: Across ten drug-like and small organic molecules, the model reaches a mean force error of 0.98 meV/A against converged DFT.
0fqzhOkEtI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the label-free variational formulation and the mathematical handling of density-matrix admissibility and analytic gradients.
0fqzhOkEtI.main_concern: Reviewers note strong overlap in core objective with recent variational DFT training works (e.g., Mathiasen et al. 2024, Li et al. 2024) and question evaluating DFT-cost motivation primarily on small rMD17 molecules.

D3bVw9vjFj.one_liner: Reweights long-tailed audio classes using teacher-filtered temporal evidence mass from a constrained temporal head.
D3bVw9vjFj.problem: Class reweighting by sample count ignores that audio recordings of equal count vary in how much informative vs. redundant or background content they contain.
D3bVw9vjFj.method: CETE (Constrained Effective Temporal Evidence Learning) trains a temporal head with classification constraints and a total-weight penalty to score informative frames, filters confident predictions via an EMA teacher, and combines aggregated class temporal weights with sample counts to set loss weights.
D3bVw9vjFj.key_idea: Estimates class-level effective evidence by summing teacher-filtered temporal attention weights from a constrained head and uses it to adjust long-tailed class loss weights.
D3bVw9vjFj.evidence: Evaluated on VGG-Sound-LT, iNatSound, BirdCLEF, and controlled-imbalance DESED benchmarks across multiple backbones with zero inference overhead.
D3bVw9vjFj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the motivation is clear and audio-specific, and that the training-only design adds no inference cost while improving balanced accuracy.
D3bVw9vjFj.main_concern: Reviewers note a theory-implementation gap, single-seed results with modest 1–2 point gains, and confounding between temporal evidence and teacher acceptance rate (difficulty-based reweighting).

AE2FlsoV3k.one_liner: Selects non-redundant reading lists via monotone submodular optimization over knowledge threads weighted by predicted future uptake.
AE2FlsoV3k.problem: Paper selection methods based on citations or independent LLM scores suffer from redundancy and retrospective bias.
AE2FlsoV3k.method: WCov extracts contribution-level claims from papers, groups them into knowledge threads, predicts future thread uptake (number of later papers continuing the thread) without citations, and solves monotone submodular weighted maximum coverage with greedy selection.
AE2FlsoV3k.key_idea: Groups extracted paper claims into knowledge threads, predicts citation-free future uptake, and greedily maximizes submodular uptake-weighted thread coverage.
AE2FlsoV3k.evidence: Evaluated on graph neural networks and federated learning corpora (selecting from <=2020 papers, observing 2021–2022 uptake) with held-out late-window and source-grouped folds.
AE2FlsoV3k.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that formulating reading-list construction as submodular contribution-thread coverage cleanly addresses redundancy and temporal leakage.
AE2FlsoV3k.main_concern: Reviewers point out the lack of human audit for LLM-extracted claims/matches, circularity in the LUC metric (underperforming citations on FCov), and unclear added value of the learned predictor over observed early uptake.

9zZAsUaf0N.one_liner: Encodes clinical practice guidelines into latent memory slots dynamically activated by patient state for sequential medical decision-making.
9zZAsUaf0N.problem: RAG-based and parametric medical agents fail to turn clinical practice guidelines into traceable, state-dependent control logic for sequential decisions.
9zZAsUaf0N.method: CPGAgent encodes guidelines as latent memory slots activated by an evolving patient state machine to plan trajectories, evaluated on CPGTrajBench, a multimodal benchmark where evidence is progressively revealed.
9zZAsUaf0N.key_idea: Encodes clinical guidelines as latent memory slots gated by a structured patient state machine to condition sequential planning.
9zZAsUaf0N.evidence: Experiments on the proposed CPGTrajBench multimodal executable benchmark.
9zZAsUaf0N.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that modeling sequential guideline adherence under progressively revealed evidence on CPGTrajBench is clinically important and well-structured.
9zZAsUaf0N.main_concern: Experiments lack matched-budget RAG planner baselines and fail to verify claims of easy guideline updatability or potential training-test trajectory leakage.

cOvTv63ZI7.one_liner: Compares prose versus statistical memory representations from a 62-day telescope agent archive on quantitative target-observability prediction.
cOvTv63ZI7.problem: Persistent agent memory is often assumed helpful, yet how derived quantities and textual formats affect quantitative prediction accuracy is poorly understood.
cOvTv63ZI7.method: Using 62 days of logs from a solar telescope agent, the authors compare prose consolidation, a nightly stratified statistical snapshot, and the snapshot plus past-error notes across 680 replayed prompts and five LLMs.
cOvTv63ZI7.key_idea: Tests prose summaries against stratified statistical snapshots and error-feedback notes derived from the exact same observation archive.
cOvTv63ZI7.evidence: 62-day deployed telescope archive and replay of 680 prompts across five LLMs from four laboratories, including matched-content format controls.
cOvTv63ZI7.claimed_gains: The statistical snapshot cuts mean absolute error from 22-25 to about 16 minutes and bias from +16/+13 to +6/+5, whereas prose memory is indistinguishable from no memory.
cOvTv63ZI7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the real-world operational archive, multi-model replay, and transparent reporting of negative results.
cOvTv63ZI7.main_concern: Representation format is confounded with added statistical information not present in prose, and one reviewer flagged temporal causality violations in baseline implementations.

YvDiiDEPkM.one_liner: Corrects flow-matching single-cell perturbation velocities at inference using reference-based failure diagnostics and MGDA-style norm-preserving consensus.
YvDiiDEPkM.problem: Flow-matching models extrapolating to unobserved context-perturbation pairs suffer from effect collapse, perturbation confusion, and context drift.
YvDiiDEPkM.method: PROVE diagnoses those three failure patterns from final-state estimates at each sampling step using cross-context references, computes local corrective directions, and merges them with the frozen velocity via MGDA minimum-norm consensus without changing velocity norm.
YvDiiDEPkM.key_idea: Diagnoses collapse, confusion, and drift against cross-context references at each sampling step and blends corrections via norm-preserving MGDA consensus.
YvDiiDEPkM.evidence: Evaluated across nine backbone-dataset combinations in cross-cell-line and cross-state single-cell perturbation transfer, plus diffusion and pathway analyses.
YvDiiDEPkM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree PROVE is a well-motivated training-free plug-in that consistently improves all five perturbation metrics across all nine model-dataset combinations.
YvDiiDEPkM.main_concern: Reviewers note missing simpler reference-using baselines (endpoint-only correction or direct interpolation) and warn that reference priors can dampen genuine context-specific biological variation.

ICrQrzUlub.one_liner: Coordinates overlapping local recursive reasoning views via normalized soft-consensus targets and persistent disagreement memory.
ICrQrzUlub.problem: Splitting structured reasoning tasks into overlapping local views for small recursive networks creates coordination conflicts when different views propose inconsistent values for shared variables.
ICrQrzUlub.method: NRR pairs a shared local reasoner (updating proposals and private states per view) with an explicit negotiation step using a normalized soft-consensus system and disagreement memory carried across recursion rounds.
ICrQrzUlub.key_idea: Couples overlapping local recursive reasoners through an explicit normalized soft-consensus negotiation step that feeds unresolved overlap disagreement back into subsequent rounds.
ICrQrzUlub.evidence: Evaluated on Sudoku-Extreme, Maze-Hard, and large mazes against native TRM, Sheaf-ADMM, and Global-RecurProx baselines with controlled ablations.
ICrQrzUlub.claimed_gains: Reaches 95.2% exact solve on Sudoku-Extreme and 90.4% on Maze-Hard.
ICrQrzUlub.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the explicit local-coordination mechanism, theoretical conditioning analysis, and favorable accuracy-latency trade-offs on large mazes compared to global recurrence.
ICrQrzUlub.main_concern: Reviewers note that Global-RecurProx matches NRR on standard-sized tasks—obscuring how much gain comes from negotiation itself—and that the main text lacks clarity and a Related Work section.

VEeF3jqSrb.one_liner: Trains recurrent reasoning models with an adversarial critic aligning outputs to local distributions around ground-truth solutions.
VEeF3jqSrb.problem: Instance-level point supervision in recurrent reasoning models becomes brittle on hard tasks where valid solutions occupy a tiny region of output space.
VEeF3jqSrb.method: DART constructs a local target distribution around the ground-truth solution and trains a critic with an adversarial objective to align the recurrent model's output distribution with that target.
VEeF3jqSrb.key_idea: Replaces single-point supervision with an adversarial critic aligning recurrent model outputs to a local noisy target distribution around ground truth.
VEeF3jqSrb.evidence: Evaluations on Maze, Chess, and masked Sudoku using Deep Thinking Systems and Tiny Recursive Models, compared against label smoothing and Gaussian soft targets.
VEeF3jqSrb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the motivation is clear and DART improves robustness and accuracy on stress-tested synthetic reasoning tasks like Sudoku and Maze.
VEeF3jqSrb.main_concern: Evaluations are restricted to synthetic benchmarks where gains over label smoothing are small on Maze, and ablations do not fully isolate adversarial distribution alignment from target softening.

eZkpLj0pnr.one_liner: Plans structured edit specifications with an MLLM, conditionally grounds masks via SAM 3, and executes edits via flow matching.
eZkpLj0pnr.problem: Instruction-based image editing often under-edits or alters unrelated regions because the intended visual intervention boundary remains implicit.
eZkpLj0pnr.method: MSVI uses a fine-tuned MLLM planner to output a structured edit specification (regime, transition, semantic actions, spatial layout), conditionally invokes SAM 3 via a deterministic compiler when localized grounding is needed, and feeds the result to a flow-matching editor trained with a source-copy suppression loss on MSVI-13K.
eZkpLj0pnr.key_idea: Predicts a structured edit specification with an MLLM to conditionally trigger SAM 3 masking before conditional flow-matching editing with source-copy suppression.
eZkpLj0pnr.evidence: Evaluated on the MSVI-13K test split against open-source instruction-based editing baselines.
eZkpLj0pnr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the minimal sufficient visual intervention framing clear and the MLLM-planner + SAM 3 + flow-matching pipeline coherent.
eZkpLj0pnr.main_concern: Reviewers point out unfair in-domain evaluation on MSVI-13K against un-finetuned baselines, error propagation in the non-end-to-end multi-model pipeline, and evaluation of only a single small planner (Qwen3.5-4B).

md6iSWAvIR.one_liner: Models multi-scale precipitation kinematics with quaternion Fourier operators and normal-tangent boundary decomposition.
md6iSWAvIR.problem: Standard spectral nowcasting models fail to disentangle scale and orientation, while continuous pixel losses blur sharp precipitation boundaries.
md6iSWAvIR.method: QFSNet maps wavelet-decomposed multi-scale fields into a quaternion representation, applies a two-sided Quaternion Fourier Transform across three branches (fine-scale, macroscopic, and local phase transport), and uses normal-tangent decomposition to preserve sharp edges.
md6iSWAvIR.key_idea: Combines a wavelet-quaternion representation and two-sided Quaternion Fourier Neural Operator with normal-tangent decomposition to decouple directional kinematics and boundary sharpening.
md6iSWAvIR.evidence: Evaluated across multiple precipitation nowcasting benchmarks against spatial, optical-flow, generative, and spectral baselines.
md6iSWAvIR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper targets a timely problem with broad empirical comparisons and strong benchmark performance.
md6iSWAvIR.main_concern: Reviewers question methodological novelty over prior wavelet-quaternion (QWNet) and differentiable CSI-loss works, and note unexplained negative branch interactions in ablations (where Fine-only nearly matches the full model).

L1pQGN82LD.one_liner: Compiles past skill-guided trajectories into one slotted prefab procedure per task type for test-time selection and slot filling.
L1pQGN82LD.problem: Re-orchestrating agent skills on the fly for every task of the same type incurs extra LLM calls, latency, and discards prior execution structure.
L1pQGN82LD.method: FlatSkill induces one verified, slotted prefab procedure per task type from past skill-guided trajectories offline. At test time, the agent selects the matching prefab and fills in its slots rather than composing skills anew, allowing prefabs built by stronger models to be reused by smaller ones.
L1pQGN82LD.key_idea: Compiles skill-guided trajectories offline into one slotted, trajectory-verified procedural prefab per task type for zero-recomposition test-time slot filling.
L1pQGN82LD.evidence: Evaluated on ALFWorld, ScienceWorld, WebShop, and MedCalc-Bench with DeepSeek-V3.2 and cross-model prefab transfer.
L1pQGN82LD.claimed_gains: Outperforms existing methods in all evaluated settings with DeepSeek-V3.2 while taking fewer interaction steps than the strongest baseline.
L1pQGN82LD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the approach is practical, improves over baselines across tested settings, and demonstrates useful cross-model prefab reuse.
L1pQGN82LD.main_concern: Reviewers criticize the limited novelty and missing comparisons against existing workflow-reuse methods (e.g., Agent Workflow Memory, SkillWeaver, Agentic Plan Caching) and simple/outdated benchmarks.

Ph0zgLABTd.one_liner: Benchmarks generative fluid intelligence in unified multimodal models across pattern induction, ad-hoc constraints, and counterfactual contextual rules.
Ph0zgLABTd.problem: Existing visual generation benchmarks test memorized crystallized knowledge and overlook generative fluid intelligence—inducing patterns and following novel contextual rules on the fly.
Ph0zgLABTd.method: GENIUS evaluates 14 models across three dimensions (inducing implicit patterns, executing ad-hoc constraints, and adapting to contextual knowledge), diagnoses recognition-vs-generation gaps via VQA probes, and proposes a training-free attention intervention.
Ph0zgLABTd.key_idea: Tests in-context rule induction and counterfactual prior override in unified multimodal models, paired with VQA probing and a training-free attention intervention.
Ph0zgLABTd.evidence: Systematic evaluation of 14 representative models on GENIUS and attention-intervention experiments.
Ph0zgLABTd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the clean interleaved multi-image setup, broad 14-model diagnostics, and focus on in-context rule adaptation over memorized priors.
Ph0zgLABTd.main_concern: Reviewers raise overlapping rubrics where realism penalizes counterfactual tasks, incremental distinction from recent reasoning T2I benchmarks, and aesthetic trade-offs in the Bagel intervention.

FBlmC2raHk.one_liner: Shapes broad pre-RL confidence priors via correctness-conditional SFT with mixed, target-balanced confidence targets to calibrate reasoning models.
FBlmC2raHk.problem: Large reasoning models have pre-RL confidence priors concentrated on high values, suppressing policy gradient updates for rare confidence values and hindering calibration RL.
FBlmC2raHk.method: CalibSFT adds a pre-RL supervised fine-tuning stage using mixed question-success-rate and response-correctness targets balanced across the confidence spectrum. Correctness-conditional supervision calibrates confidence on all responses while supervising reasoning only on correct ones.
FBlmC2raHk.key_idea: Pre-trains a broad confidence prior via target-balanced, correctness-conditional SFT using mixed success-rate and correctness targets before calibration RL.
FBlmC2raHk.evidence: Theoretical Brier-risk lower-bound analysis and experiments across 16 mathematical and general reasoning benchmarks and multiple RL algorithms.
FBlmC2raHk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that CalibSFT provides a well-motivated diagnosis of concentrated pre-RL confidence priors and delivers broad empirical calibration gains across RL methods.
FBlmC2raHk.main_concern: Reviewers note that balanced vs. unbalanced sampling is only ablated after SFT rather than after RL, leaving the causal role of broader exploration unresolved.

KIGGxNm6gG.one_liner: Generates executable scene-rendering programs for proxy videos and applies early-step conditioning to guide pretrained video diffusion models.
KIGGxNm6gG.problem: Video diffusion models generate videos in a black box where physics, object placement, motion, and camera trajectories are imagined rather than computed.
KIGGxNm6gG.method: Code Video Model writes an executable program from a prompt to lay out scenes, animate objects, place a camera, and compute dynamics from equations, rendering a proxy video and reference image. It then conditions a pretrained video model on the proxy video only during early sampling steps before dropping the conditioning to preserve visual appearance.
KIGGxNm6gG.key_idea: Rendering an executable physics-and-layout program into a proxy video and attending to it only during early denoising steps.
KIGGxNm6gG.evidence: Evaluated on CodeVideoBench (22 cases across eight categories), qualitative comparisons, and a user preference study.
KIGGxNm6gG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that pairing coding agents for explicit layout and physical grounding with pretrained video models for visual detail is practical and yields competitive visual results.
KIGGxNm6gG.main_concern: Reviewers note that the 22-case evaluation set is too small, the heuristic early-step cutoff still allows structural misalignment or post-cutoff trajectory drift, and early-step conditioning has limited novelty.

rDSslZwWfK.one_liner: Organizes multi-step search as a dynamic sub-question DAG with dependency-grounded scoring and causal error localization for agent training.
rDSslZwWfK.problem: LLM-based search agents track dependencies implicitly, causing early retrieval or reasoning errors to compound without identifying affected downstream steps.
rDSslZwWfK.method: SearchMapper represents search as an adaptively growing DAG of sub-questions, scored by a hierarchical model on redundancy, clarity, and progressiveness to guide iterative refinement. A NEAR-guided algorithm uses the DAG structure to localize errors via hypothesis-space contraction, supervising a three-stage pipeline of imitation, alignment, and generalization.
rDSslZwWfK.key_idea: Making search dependencies explicit in a sub-question DAG to drive hierarchical process scoring and non-descendant error attribution.
rDSslZwWfK.evidence: Evaluated a 30B model across five deep-search benchmarks against same-scale search agents with Stage I and RL ablations.
rDSslZwWfK.claimed_gains: Recovers 85.2% of failed trajectories at an average of 1.63 iterations, lifts the five-benchmark average from 54.9 to 63.9, leads same-scale 30B search agents on four of five benchmarks, and uses 35.6% fewer steps or tokens (abstract truncated).
rDSslZwWfK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that explicit DAG dependency structure yields consistent empirical and ablated gains across deep-search benchmarks for a 30B agent.
rDSslZwWfK.main_concern: Reviewers criticize NEAR's contraction rule as an unjustified heuristic that assumes single faults and oracle gold-answer stopping rather than a principled localization guarantee.

XXV72hQlVe.one_liner: Transfers context-internalization hypernetworks across LLM backbones by linearly aligning inputs, preserving intermediate representations, and relearning parameter generators.
XXV72hQlVe.problem: Context-internalization hypernetworks are tightly coupled to a specific LLM backbone's dimensions and layer count, making retraining for each new LLM prohibitively expensive.
XXV72hQlVe.method: Using representational similarity analysis, the authors decompose Doc-to-LoRA hypernetworks into an input projection, a Perceiver module, and a LoRA parameter generator. HyperBridge transfers a source hypernetwork to a new LLM backbone by linearly aligning the input projection, preserving the intermediate Perceiver representations, and re-learning the architecture-specific parameter generator.
XXV72hQlVe.key_idea: Decomposing hypernetworks into linearly alignable input projections, transferable intermediate Perceiver representations, and backbone-specific parameter generators.
XXV72hQlVe.evidence: Supported by representational similarity analysis (RSA/CKA) and component-level transfer ablations on Doc-to-LoRA hypernetworks.
XXV72hQlVe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the component-wise transferability analysis is informative and provides a concrete recipe for reusing trained hypernetwork components.
XXV72hQlVe.main_concern: Reviewers note that the findings are tied to the single Doc-to-LoRA architecture without establishing generality to other hypernetwork designs or reporting efficiency gains.

Z3N7BLKklK.one_liner: Synthesizes and locally repairs evidence-grounded infographics using a typed visual-symbolic dependency graph with layered execution and verification.
Z3N7BLKklK.problem: Infographic generation and editing struggle to keep facts, visual relations, and supporting evidence consistent without globally regenerating the entire canvas.
Z3N7BLKklK.method: InfoAgent compiles requests into an Infographic Visual Description (IVD) typed dependency graph tracking factual payloads, provenance, execution routes, and verification obligations, executes layered raster and editable symbolic objects with design priors, and performs dependency-aware localized repair.
Z3N7BLKklK.key_idea: Represents facts, provenance, execution routes, and verification checks in a typed dependency graph so edits localize to affected objects and recheck protected obligations.
Z3N7BLKklK.evidence: Evaluated on IGenBench, the new 200-request InfoGraphicBench-Evidence benchmark, and 120 audited repair cases with ablations.
Z3N7BLKklK.claimed_gains: Achieves 93.0 Q-ACC and 59.0 I-ACC on IGenBench, raises InfoGraphicBench-Evidence complete-checklist pass rates from 21.5% (Same-IVD Prompt) to 23.5% (initial) and 28.5% (after repair), and edits 12.4% of the canvas versus 67.3% for global regeneration.
Z3N7BLKklK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the typed dependency-graph intermediate representation for localized repair and the thorough evaluation including a new benchmark and human audits.
Z3N7BLKklK.main_concern: Reviewers note low absolute whole-infographic reliability (28.5% full checklist pass rate), unvalidated IVD compiler completeness, and non-budget-matched baseline comparisons.

NwTYm3PZPT.one_liner: Assigns DNA barcodes across full taxonomic hierarchies—including unsequenced taxa—using a set-encoding network and calibrated novelty thresholds.
NwTYm3PZPT.problem: Standard DNA barcode classifiers restrict predictions to taxa present in the sequence reference, missing the majority of species in taxonomic hierarchies that lack reference sequences.
NwTYm3PZPT.method: TaxoSet uses a 0.34M-parameter marker-agnostic set-encoding network over retrieval scores and taxonomy structure trained by holding out entire clades, outputting a prediction set of indistinguishable unsequenced siblings when a calibrated novelty threshold (5% FPR on known species) rejects a single reference name.
NwTYm3PZPT.key_idea: Trains a sequence-free set-encoding network via leave-clade-out retrieval simulation and applies a calibrated novelty threshold to return either a reference name or an unsequenced candidate set.
NwTYm3PZPT.evidence: Evaluated across curated ITS, 12S, 16S, and COI references (2.4M species) with leave-clade-out splits and an external taxonomic benchmark.
NwTYm3PZPT.claimed_gains: At a 5% false-positive rate on held-out known species, TaxoSet reaches 69% coverage (median 11 names) on ITS queries with absent genera and 82% coverage (median 37 names) on an external benchmark.
NwTYm3PZPT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the practical open-reference problem framing for biodiversity surveys, realistic leave-clade-out evaluation, and strong coverage from a compact 0.34M-parameter network.
NwTYm3PZPT.main_concern: Reviewers cite poor writing clarity and missing training details, as well as large candidate set sizes on some markers (e.g., COI) that reduce practical actionability.

CyAlVWQ6eo.one_liner: Constructs preference-aligned AI rewards over set-valued predictions directly from human utility functions and decision-under-uncertainty criteria.
CyAlVWQ6eo.problem: Extending a human utility function to reward set-valued AI predictions by aggregating utilities over constituent states violates true decision-maker preferences under uncertainty.
CyAlVWQ6eo.method: The authors model human decision behavior via selection strategies induced by decision criteria (Laplace, maximin, maximax, minimax regret), formalize validity and alignment conditions over arbitrary terminal act sets, prove compatibility with standard aggregators, and provide an algorithm to construct aligned rewards.
CyAlVWQ6eo.key_idea: Models human choices under set-valued uncertainty via decision-criterion selection strategies rather than state-utility aggregation to construct provably preference-aligned rewards.
CyAlVWQ6eo.evidence: Theoretical compatibility proofs and an illustrative simulation study on random utility functions.
CyAlVWQ6eo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the clearly identified flaw in state-aggregation rewards and the mathematical rigor of the validity and alignment proofs.
CyAlVWQ6eo.main_concern: Reviewers note the lack of realistic applications or learning experiments—with the only simulation restricted to small synthetic utilities and singleton acts—leaving practical relevance unestablished.

4DsCSc4YN8.one_liner: Distills frozen video diffusion model future representations into a single-step visual encoder for real-time robot action prediction without video generation.
4DsCSc4YN8.problem: World-action models relying on iterative future video denoising are too slow for real-time robot control and can fail when generated frames are inaccurate.
4DsCSc4YN8.method: DreamFree trains a visual encoder via representation distillation to predict a frozen pretrained video diffusion model's predictive representations from only the current observation, then trains an action module on those features to predict actions without generating future videos.
4DsCSc4YN8.key_idea: Distills a frozen pretrained video diffusion model's predictive features into a current-observation visual encoder so an action module runs without iterative video denoising.
4DsCSc4YN8.evidence: Evaluated on RoboCasa simulation and DROID real-robot manipulation tasks, plus video-only task transfer including cross-embodiment demonstrations and latency benchmarks.
4DsCSc4YN8.claimed_gains: Performs real-time closed-loop control at 11Hz with a 14B video diffusion backbone while achieving higher success rates than prior VLAs and WAMs.
4DsCSc4YN8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers commend the broad experimental evaluation, low latency with a 14B backbone, and video-only cross-embodiment task transfer results.
4DsCSc4YN8.main_concern: Reviewers question the methodological novelty relative to prior predictive-representation and video-free WAM methods (such as Fast-WAM and FLARE) and note confusing figures and notation.

P6oLUIe8YR.one_liner: Trains interactive 3D grounding via trajectory-level preference optimization and a history-aware adapter to prevent premature candidate pruning.
P6oLUIe8YR.problem: In interactive 3D visual grounding with ambiguous queries, filtering candidates based only on current query-object matching prematurely discards targets needed for later disambiguation.
P6oLUIe8YR.method: The framework formulates interactive 3D grounding as sequential candidate refinement using trajectory-level preference optimization over ordered candidate transitions, subsequent feedback, and final outcomes. A trajectory-aware adapter fuses interaction history and candidate belief to emit residual updates for candidate representations and grounding scores.
P6oLUIe8YR.key_idea: Optimizes early candidate filtering via trajectory-level preference learning and a trajectory-aware residual adapter conditioned on interaction history and candidate belief.
P6oLUIe8YR.evidence: Evaluated across four 3D grounding backbones with ablations on round ordering and feedback signs, comparing direct and trajectory training schemes.
P6oLUIe8YR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the premature-discard problem is well motivated and that trajectory-aware training consistently improves target survival across backbones.
P6oLUIe8YR.main_concern: Reviewers criticize the lack of external baseline comparisons, confounded backbone fine-tuning capacity in the direct baseline, and modest final grounding accuracy gains.

kK08uotu5P.one_liner: Evolves multi-agent prompts and topologies using an internal Sense-of-Agency score combining expected performance and prediction-outcome agreement.
kK08uotu5P.problem: Evolving multi-agent systems at inference time typically relies on external verifiers or separate LLM evaluators, which are unavailable in many deployment settings.
kK08uotu5P.method: SOAP defines a computational Sense of Agency (SoA) signal capturing an agent's expected performance and how closely post-execution self-assessment matches that expectation. Using intra-agent and inter-agent SoA feedback, it iteratively updates prompts and interaction topologies without external evaluators.
kK08uotu5P.key_idea: Guides prompt and topology updates using an internal Sense-of-Agency score combining anticipated performance and prediction-outcome self-assessment agreement.
kK08uotu5P.evidence: Experiments and ablations across BrowseComp-Plus, Plancraft, WorkBench, and Cloudcast using multiple LLM backbones.
kK08uotu5P.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find removing external evaluators timely and appreciate the clear two-level decomposition and multi-benchmark evaluation.
kK08uotu5P.main_concern: Reviewers point out that the SoA objective A(p,o)=p(1-|p-o|) is maximized at an optimistically biased prediction p=(1+o)/2 rather than calibrated p=o, and lacks a self-assessment-only ablation.

dTKO9wbV3J.one_liner: Suppresses random spatial-frequency bands during training, aggregates multi-depth backbone features, and matches compression for synthetic video detection.
dTKO9wbV3J.problem: Synthetic-video detectors evaluated on raw footage collapse under realistic streaming re-encoding because their decisions rely on compression-sensitive spatial frequency bands.
dTKO9wbV3J.method: The method randomly suppresses spatial frequency sub-bands during training so no single band is indispensable, aggregates features from multiple network depths, and matches compression conditions between real and synthetic training samples to remove compression shortcuts.
dTKO9wbV3J.key_idea: Applies random frequency-band dropout, multi-depth feature readout, and compression-matched real/synthetic training pairs to eliminate single-band compression vulnerability.
dTKO9wbV3J.evidence: Analyzed and evaluated on the quality-controlled SynthForensics benchmark across pristine to CRF40 compression levels and cross-generator transfer.
dTKO9wbV3J.claimed_gains: Trained on a single generator, the detector holds 90.0% AUC at CRF40 on SynthForensics (moving from 99.7% on default quality), whereas a prior detector drops from 93.2% to 44.6% AUC.
dTKO9wbV3J.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value elevating realistic streaming re-encoding to a primary evaluation axis and showing how benchmark rankings collapse under compression.
dTKO9wbV3J.main_concern: Reviewers note limited methodological novelty, confounding between compression-matched training data and architectural changes, and evaluation restricted to a single libx264 codec.

mYcCtZu7Yl.one_liner: Routes multimodal sentiment features into redundancy, synergy, and uniqueness experts via MLLM-estimated priors plus entropy-triggered latent refinement.
mYcCtZu7Yl.problem: Multimodal sentiment analysis struggles because textual, acoustic, and visual cues vary in whether they are redundant, synergistic, or uniquely decisive across instances.
mYcCtZu7Yl.method: The Reason-Decompose-Deliberate (RDD) framework prompts an MLLM with chain-of-thought to estimate instance-specific cross-modal role vectors for routing gates (MIRR), extracts redundant, synergistic, and unique features via dedicated experts (IGED), and refines high-entropy uncertain samples iteratively using a latent think token (UALD).
mYcCtZu7Yl.key_idea: Uses MLLM-predicted Partial Information Decomposition role gates to route features into specialized experts and applies entropy-triggered latent think-token refinement.
mYcCtZu7Yl.evidence: Evaluated on three multimodal sentiment benchmarks (including MOSI and CH-SIMS per reviews) with ablations and visualization analyses.
mYcCtZu7Yl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find applying Partial Information Decomposition roles (redundancy, synergy, uniqueness) to adaptive multimodal sentiment fusion interesting.
mYcCtZu7Yl.main_concern: Reviewers cite missing controls isolating the Qwen2.5-Omni MLLM's contribution, lack of explicit information-theoretic constraints verifying decomposition, and omitted recent PID baselines.

J7yJzJxRgZ.one_liner: Freezes pretrained reconstructor weights at test time and optimizes one activation or input tensor via measurement-only data consistency.
J7yJzJxRgZ.problem: Sparse-view reconstruction errors lie largely in the measurement operator's null space, which image-space data-consistency gradient descent cannot reduce.
J7yJzJxRgZ.method: Guided by an error bound showing null-space reduction depends on alignment between network updates and true error, Routed Data Consistency (RDC) freezes all pretrained weights and optimizes a single activation or input tensor per scan using measurement-only loss. A label-free held-out-view check selects when weight updates remain preferable.
J7yJzJxRgZ.key_idea: Minimizes measurement-only data-consistency loss over one freed activation or input tensor of a frozen reconstructor to move null-space error.
J7yJzJxRgZ.evidence: Theoretical bound plus experiments on eight-view cone-beam CT, nine simulated settings, 61 clinical scans, and MRI, super-resolution, inpainting, and deblurring operators.
J7yJzJxRgZ.claimed_gains: RDC ends 1.72 dB above the range oracle on eight-view cone-beam CT, gains 2.75 dB on average over nine simulated settings (3.6x faster than weight-space adaptation to match it), gains 1.09 dB on 61 clinical scans at 40 steps, and predicts the better variable in 110 of 115 comparisons.
J7yJzJxRgZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the practical problem of adapting frozen reconstructors from measurements alone and the broad multi-modality evaluation.
J7yJzJxRgZ.main_concern: Reviewers question novelty over prior intermediate-layer/input optimization methods (ILO, PINER), qualify the label-free claim due to labeled hyperparameter calibration, and note diminishing gains under noise or longer budgets.

dmJeZ2FraF.one_liner: Adds an execution-time 84-cue target-state risk gate that selectively rescales waypoint translation for PPO-trained VLA trackers.
dmJeZ2FraF.problem: Fine-tuning embodied visual tracking VLA policies with PPO improves persistence but increases collision rates because episodes that previously lost the target instead end in contact.
dmJeZ2FraF.method: TRACE freezes the PPO-updated 0.6B VLA tracker and adds a lightweight risk head over 84 cues (candidate boxes, identity margins, range-and-bearing probe, and policy commands). When calibrated risk exceeds a threshold, TRACE rescales the translational waypoint component while leaving yaw unchanged, keeping actions identical on over 98% of steps.
dmJeZ2FraF.key_idea: Triggers translational waypoint rescaling via a calibrated 84-cue target-state risk gate while leaving the underlying VLA policy and yaw commands unchanged.
dmJeZ2FraF.evidence: Paired evaluations, matched slowdown controls, and episode-level analyses across three EVT-Bench settings using a 0.6B VLA tracker.
dmJeZ2FraF.claimed_gains: Reduces distracted-tracking collision rate by 3.96 percentage points while further improving success and following rates, keeping actions identical to PPO on >98% of steps.
dmJeZ2FraF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers highlight the practical finding that RL persistence gains increase collision risk and value the lightweight, minimally invasive intervention with matched controls.
dmJeZ2FraF.main_concern: Reviewers note the lack of real-robot validation, reliance on simulator oracle perception cues, and test-episode overlap in training/thresholding the risk gate.

t2vjQRh2bk.one_liner: Forms 3D spatial relations jointly from reference frames, geometry, and language via an order-aware query-conditioned geometry controller.
t2vjQRh2bk.problem: Fixed, query-independent geometric relation encodings discard query-critical cues and leave directional semantics under-constrained relative to the relevant reference frame.
t2vjQRh2bk.method: FROG introduces a relation-centric 3D spatial reasoning framework where an order-aware geometry controller extracts relational semantics from the query to adapt measurement directions and multi-scale weights. Reference frames are integrated directly into relation formation via tokenwise spectral rotations.
t2vjQRh2bk.key_idea: Jointly constructs 3D spatial relations using a query-conditioned order-aware geometry controller and reference-frame-aligned tokenwise spectral rotations.
t2vjQRh2bk.evidence: Evaluated across two backbones on ScanRefer, Multi3DRefer, ASR, and Real-3DQA using both ground-truth instances and Mask3D proposals.
t2vjQRh2bk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers note consistent grounding improvements across backbones and benchmarks with a compact parameter footprint (~3.99M added parameters).
t2vjQRh2bk.main_concern: Reviewers observe that most gains come from reference-frame relative positional encodings rather than language adaptation, and lack comparisons against conventional pose-conditioned baselines.

so4DHZgiyi.one_liner: Benchmarks generated software tests on 619 tasks and 82,579 candidate patches via Joint Validation Rate and curates SFT data.
so4DHZgiyi.problem: Evaluating generated software tests only on single reference patches misses tests that accept incorrect patches or reject valid alternative patches.
so4DHZgiyi.method: SWEPATCHTEST collects 619 tasks from SWE-bench Pro, SWE-bench Multilingual, and DeepSWE with 82,579 candidate patches from coding-agent trajectories, replaying tests to measure Joint Validation Rate (reproduction, correct-patch acceptance, and incorrect-patch rejection). It also uses validation scores to select and scale demonstrations for SFT.
so4DHZgiyi.key_idea: Replays generated test suites against large pools of correct and incorrect candidate patches to measure Joint Validation Rate and curate SFT trajectories.
so4DHZgiyi.evidence: Evaluated across 619 tasks with 82,579 candidate patches and downstream SFT repair experiments on three SWE-bench benchmarks.
so4DHZgiyi.claimed_gains: The best-performing configuration achieves 9.21% JVR despite 59.29% reference reproduction; validation-selected SFT approximately triples JVR and improves downstream repair across three SWE-bench benchmarks.
so4DHZgiyi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that single-reference test evaluation hides test overfitting and that patch-discrimination benchmarking is a useful resource.
so4DHZgiyi.main_concern: Reviewers note limited conceptual novelty over prior test-overfitting studies, reliance on imperfect original oracle tests for patch labels, and insufficient deeper failure analysis.

2miOfAB1Gx.one_liner: Evaluates LLM web-app generation using coverage-guided agent exploration, state-transition graph abstraction, and decoupled three-axis scoring.
2miOfAB1Gx.problem: Static web-app benchmarks credit unreachable code, while interactive benchmarks suffer from incomplete exploration that confounds app defects with agent execution failures.
2miOfAB1Gx.method: WebCraftBench instruments generated web applications and uses code coverage to guide a user-simulating exploration agent, abstracting interaction traces into a state-transition graph. Separating exploration from scoring, it evaluates visual aesthetics, usability, and requirement alignment across 369 real-world requirements and 5,088 acceptance criteria.
